Spoilers for Season 2, Episode 6 of Marshals are ahead! You can stream the series with a Paramount+ subscription and catch new episodes on CBS every Sunday.

The episode of Marshals that just aired on the 2026 TV schedule is inspired by a tragedy that actually happened to one of its stars and American Indian Affairs Coordinator, Mo Brings Plenty, and his family. In 2024, his nephew, Cole Brings Plenty, died, and a coroner ruled out foul play. His family disagreed with that, and they’re still looking for answers. In this week's episode of Marshals, Mo’s nephew, Troy, is found dead, and he and Kayce work to prove that it was a murder, not suicide. Ultimately, the case is left unsolved, and according to Mo Brings Plenty, that was a very important detail to include.

Knowing that “Roughstock” was inspired by his own experiences, I asked Mo Brings Plenty, who plays Mo in Marshals and Yellowstone, about details in the episode he was happy to see included. He immediately noted that he was glad the case was left unsolved, because that kind of outcome happens in real life, often, as the actor explained:

Oh, I was happy to see that when the police officer said he just kind of blew it off, because that's really the case. And so I was happy that we showed that legitimate part of it. Not every officer is that way, but in some cases, in some states - primarily states that have a high American Indian population - that occurs.

When I spoke to Mo in March this year about an episode of Marshals having to do with missing American Indians, he told me they “haven’t got any answers for” what happened to his nephew, Cole.

In this episode of Marshals, it’s made very clear that while Troy’s case will stay open, it will likely go unsolved. It’s obvious that it’s not being prioritized by law enforcement, and despite the marshals best efforts, there is no solution as to who killed Troy by the end of the episode. When I asked Mo why it was important for this episode to go without a solution to Troy’s case, he said:

Because the wheel of justice doesn't turn for us as American Indian people, and of course we're tax-paying people as well. And so, you know, first responders get their funding through taxpayers, tax funding, and so when it doesn't work for us, then it's so frustrating. It's like, ‘Well, why are we even paying taxes?’ And so that's one of the things that is impactful for me, and that I need to continue to speak about because it is occurring.

In the case of Mo’s real nephew, Cole, he was found dead a few days after he was reported missing and named as a suspect in a domestic violence case. Two years later, Mo spoke to THR and claimed that his nephew’s death had gone “uninvestigated,” while the Lawrence Police Department said there was “no foul play involved in Cole’s death.”

When I spoke to Mo about this topic recently and how it was represented on this Yellowstone show, he said:

It's sad for me and my family, especially when I hear the cry for other nationalities and in foreign countries, when the very same thing is occurring to us as the original inhabitants within this country, we're basically flying over mission fields to get to mission fields.

According to the U.S. Department of the Interior Indian Affairs, there are “approximately 4,200 missing and murder cases that have gone unsolved.” And when I asked Mo Brings Plenty if Marshals could ever circle back to Troy’s unsolved case, he said:

Absolutely, it could definitely happen. But you know, there are so many stories. I mean, my family is not the only family. This isn't the first time something like this has occurred in real life. You know, there are many stories, many families, different situations, different circumstances that are going through the same thing.

Overall, he was clear that there are lots of stories like his that should be shown on Kayce’s Yellowstone spinoff. He’s not the only one who has lost a loved one in this way and was left without answers, and he’s hoping to see more of those stories depicted on Marshals.

Now, to see how Mo’s story continues, you can watch the next episode of Marshals on November 22 at 8:30 p.m. ET, and you can stream it the next day on Paramount+.

#3694. UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch is more worried "about the amount of time" people will spend on GTA 6 than the game's violent content

"I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter. I didn't hit anybody after playing those games."

Leader of the UK Conservative Party (and former Mortal Kombat player) Kemi Badenoch is more worried about the amount of time people will spend playing GTA 6 rather than the game itself.

Every new Grand Theft Auto game invites some amount of controversy over its in-game violence or depictions of sex and drugs - from San Andreas' raunchy Hot Coffee mini-game to GTA 5's graphic torture scene. Ahead of GTA 6's release this week, the Tory leader downplayed those fears.

"I would be more worried about the amount of time people were spending on a game than the game specifically. I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter. I didn't hit anybody after playing those games," Badenoch said in a news conference shared by Sky News (good spot, IGN).

While Badenoch's stance might be surprising for the normally right-wing UK political party, she did still worry over children who might play GTA 6 for too long. There are probably far worse ways for kids to spend their time than engaging with a long-form story like GTA 6's, though, especially in an era with endless amounts of 10-second clips to mindlessly scroll past and declining funding into youth programs.

"I haven't played Grand Theft Auto, I know people are worried about the game content. At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half an hour on it and then went out and did something else. They are two different things," Badenoch added.

GTA 6's release is imminent and is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time. One analyst even suggested GTA 6 could make over $2bn in its opening weekend - that's handily more money than Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey made during its entire run in cinemas, for context.

This has ignited some fears within the community of the COD-ification of Battlefield.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

A few things come to mind when I think about what the greatest fear of a Battlefield player is. It could be a glint atop the mountains on Liberation Peak, reliving the launch of Battlefield 2042, or maybe it's the randomised recoil from the first Battlefield. All of these are good bets, but I think the real shared nightmare of most Battlefield players is that someday it'll morph into Call of Duty.

To be fair, this fear isn't entirely unfounded. Bryan Beede was previously appointed as Battlefield's general manager after spending 19 years working on Call of Duty and has now been promoted to group general manager at EA. Taking his place is another Call of Duty veteran, Sam Cooper, who worked as Call of Duty's global product management and head of live service.

"I'm excited to share that I've joined Electronic Arts as general manager of Battlefield," Cooper says in a LinkedIn post. "I started my games career at EA on the FIFA team, so coming back to where it all began feels extra special.

"Battlefield is an iconic franchise that has something no other shooter has: all-out warfare, destruction at massive scale, squads play, and a passionate community that has stuck with this franchise for more than two decades."

Now this in and of itself isn't enough to sound any alarm bells for players concerned whether or not Battlefield can stay true to form, especially since Beede was appointed as Battlefield GM back in 2021 prior to Battlefield 6's release. But this alongside some questionable new skins has some Battlefield players worried that Battlefield is becoming more "en-cod-ified".

A big talking point during Battlefield 6's launch was players begging the devs to ignore COD's trend of gimmicky skins and instead stay true to its in-game realism for cosmetics. This has largely been the case—although the Dead Space collab was a near miss. But now some believe the cracks are starting to show with the new Fox Hunter skin pack.

"There's absolutely no way you can defend this," one player says in response to the skin pack. "There's a pseudo furry skin in Battlefield now. The defense I've heard is that 'it's plausible', while these are plausible, the masks are just, no? What tactical purpose does wearing a Japanese baby mask [or] a furry mask serve?" I'd argue, however, that it could stun an enemy Battlefield player long enough for you to secure a kill, and therefore there's at least some tactical purpose to it.

#3692. Original GTA 6 leaker pleads guilty to hacking Rockstar Games, years after first revealing Lucia

The 21-year-old responsible for hacking Rockstar Games and leaking in-development GTA 6 footage in 2022 has pleaded guilty to a number of offenses.

The GTA 6 leaker was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay at a hospital due to his severe autism, but was more recently deemed fit for trial and moved to a regular prison earlier this January. On Monday, at the Woolwich Crown Court in South East London, he pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games and a number of other companies, including Uber and EE/BT, in cyber attacks estimated to have caused £10m in damages.

At the time of his Rockstar hack - when he was between the ages of 16 and 17 - the leaker was already under police protection at a Travelodge hotel to keep him from rival hackers he had allegedly stolen Bitcoin from. Somewhat surprisingly, he then managed to hack the multi-billion dollar game maker with nothing but an Amazon Fire Stick, the hotel room's TV and a bluetooth-connected keyboard and mouse.

As the BBC reports, he also managed to break into the developer's Slack channels, before threatening to release the GTA 6 source code if Rockstar failed to contact him within the day. The leaker has yet to be sentenced.

Those 2022 leaks were quite substantial, too, revealing about an hour of unfinished gameplay and clueing the world in on Lucia's existence - the series' first female protagonist in years. Of course, those 2022 leaks shouldn't be confused with 2026's, which saw Cyberleek spill nuggets of nearly finished clips onto the internet, despite Rockstar's best efforts to keep GTA 6 a closely guarded secret.

"We recently suffered a network intrusion in which an unauthorised third-party illegally accessed and downloaded confidential information from our systems, including early development footage for the next Grand Theft Auto," Rockstar said at the time, before it had officially unveiled GTA 6. "At this time we do not anticipate any disruption to our live game services, nor any long-term effect on the development of our ongoing projects. We are extremely disappointed to have any details of our next game shared with you all in this way."

Four years later, GTA 6 is finally around the corner - you're probably already aware considering the marketing frenzy Rockstar's been drumming up.

#3690. Star Wars: Galactic Racer is getting much-requested split-screen multiplayer and new mode in 2027

The surprisingly awesome arcade podracing game Star Wars: Galactic Racer is getting split-screen multiplayer next year after loud fan requests, developer Fuse Games has announced.

Split-screen racing comes as part of an entirely new mode called Free Play that'll also allow players to mix and match vehicles, characters, tracks and planets in a galaxy far, far away. So, maybe don't expect to bring friends into the game's vast, pre-existing suite of modes just yet.

"We heard you," the studio wrote on social media. "Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to Star Wars: Galactic Racer. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action."

We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at @Fuse_Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to STAR WARS: Galactic Racer™. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action.

Galactic Racer already has a pretty good selection of online multiplayer modes, like the 12-player speeder races and 8-player podracing tours, but there's currently no way to play with your mates in the same room.

Chris Donlan loved the thrilling racing game for mixing the best bits of Star Wars and Burnout - Fuse Games does have plenty of old Criterion DNA, mind you. "It's new games, with Roguelite choices and endless unlockables, and it's also old games, with cruel and ingenious courses where everything can be lost in an instant. It's a Galaxy Far, Far Away, and it's also Paradise City," he wrote in Eurogamer's five-star review.

With Galactic Racer and Zero Company under its belt, Lucasfilm Games said it's now "more flexible" about which developers it accepts pitches from. Hopefully, that'll lead to even more interesting games set in Star Wars' ultra flexible world.

#3689. ‘Actively Makes The Game Worse’: Fans Are Furious With Pikmin 4′s Paid Nintendo Switch 2 ‘Upgrade’

Last Thursday, Pikmin 4 finally received its Nintendo Switch 2 Edition upgrade, promised to add improved visuals, voice commands for the adorable Oatchi, and a new set of bonus levels in the added “Dandori Academy.” But rather than serve as an incentive for Pikmin lovers to return to the game over the weekend, it looks like it’s mostly just pissed off people who paid the $10 for what they say barely qualifies as an upgrade.

Updated this graphic again now that Dandori Academy is out and… ðð

At least XDE isn't alone anymore https://t.co/2ZGYyqrcuE pic.twitter.com/B9tsSXziSb

— Shifted Pyro (@ShiftedPyro) November 15, 2026

At the time I’m writing this, Pikmin 4 Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy (to use its full, Christian name) has a 2.1 user score on Metacritic out of 265 ratings. While 265 isn’t a huge amount of user reviews, that is a remarkably low score for a game that has a base version sitting comfortably at 8.9. And the comments are full of the same, repeated complaints: framerates are still at 30 FPS, loading screens now take longer than they did in the original, and the new content is mostly a bunch of reused maps from the base game that can only be played at certain times.

“charging customers for almost no content nor technical enhancements (in fact, load times are even longer on NSW2 – itâs a disgrace!)” reads a 0/10 review from laurack.

“This is essentially a paid downgrade and calling this is a ‘lazy Switch 2 Edition’ or a ‘waste of money’ is an understatement for what is supposed to be an upgrade,” writes PrestonandTom in a 1/10 review. “This ‘upgrade’ of Pikmin 4 somehow manages to make the game run significantly worse with standard load times going from 6 seconds to 30+ seconds. The framerate went from an consistent 30 FPS to an inconsistent 30 FPS. Even despite all these problems, the new content isn’t that fun or engaging for the player by offering weak rewards for getting good dandori scores. The resolution is higher, but the tradeoff is not worth it and neither is the ‘new’ dandori academy content which mostly consists of old dandori levels that are already available in the base game.”

“While Pikmin 4 remains the undisputed peak of the franchise, this ‘Switch 2 Edition’ is a tough sell for returning veterans,” writes marcoskalil in a 7/10 review. “The bump in resolution and draw distance is welcome, but it ultimately highlights older textures that haven’t been properly upscaled for the new hardware. The bonus mode offers genuinely fun, meaningful content for long-time fans, yet it falls short of justifying the upgrade price. If you missed the original launch, this is undeniably the definitive way to play. However, if you have already conquered PNF-404 on the base Switch and is looking for more quality Olimar adventures, keep your Pikmin planted and hold out for Pikmin 5.”

“Very disaster edition game scam man!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!” wrote Lolitroppotsund in a succinct 0/10 review.

There are also a handful of criticisms, both there and in other communities, of the big Dandori Academy banner taking up space on this edition’s menu screen:

Bruh , Pikmin 4 nintendo switch 2 edition title screen is so ugly byu/Independent-Week-463 inPikmin

Now, not everyone is convinced the upgrade is horrible. Over on the Pikmin subreddit, longtime franchise fans are rolling their eyes a bit at the metascores, suggesting they’re “overdramatic” and that the release is in line with some of Nintendo’s other Switch 2 Edition upgrades. That said, not an awful lot of people are actively popping up in strong defense of the new edition, instead mostly just insisting it’s not as bad as the score suggest.

is it really that bad? byu/Papanataaa inPikmin

I’ve been holding off on playing Pikmin 4 for this update, but now I’m left questioning whether or not I ought to just save myself some money and buy the regular edition. The fans are right that it’s not the end of the world, and admittedly Nintendo didn’t promise much. But it is still a paid upgrade that, in at least one respect, makes the original game worse, and doesn’t seem to add much meaningful to balance that out. Pick it up at your own risk.

Warning! The following contains spoilers from the 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way episode "Out Of The Frying Pan, Into The Family." Stream the episode with an HBO Max subscription, and read at your own risk!

Niles Valentine has kept his wife, Matilda, in the dark since the start of the 2026 TV schedule about his plan to move to Ghana. He finally decided to drop the bombshell in this latest episode, and predictably, she was pretty upset to learn he was no longer working toward bringing her to the United States. Given her anger, there was a possibility this married 90 Day couple could split at the end of the season.

With various rumors floating around the internet about their status, I decided to do a bit of digging to see what I could find on whether series veterans Niles and Matilda are still together. While I didn't expect either of them to break their contract agreements and explicitly say one way or another, I think it's safe to say it looks like they're still together, with some predictable updates.

Niles posted a photo on Instagram of what appeared to be the inside of an apartment in the United States back on November 13th. Readers can take a look at the post below, in which he showed the difference someone's posture can make. Take a look:

A post shared by Niles Valentine (@roman_cupid_95)

That doesn't look like any room in Matilda's apartment, which has me guessing he's back in the United States at this point. I can't claim to be an expert on apartments in Africa, but I've lived in a good deal of American ones that have that exact same look when it comes to the bathroom!

Niles returning home feels like the most obvious outcome in this season of 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way. Matilda married him in the hopes of coming to the United States and not just having a better life for herself but for her family back in Africa as well. She's obviously mad that Niles couldn't make it happen as soon as he promised, but that doesn't mean she wants him to give up.

If Niles has returned to the US, I think it's fair to speculate that he and Matilda are still together. The pair still follow each other on Instagram, which usually feels like an obvious sign that 90 Day couples are still together and married.

Why 90 Day Fiancé's New Florida Spinoff Has Me Questioning If We've Lost The Plot

If we get to the end of 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way and learn that Niles is still working to bring Matilda to the United States, I won't be surprised. That's been the goal from the start, and I think he made a rash decision to move to Africa without looking into how difficult it would be for him to start a life in the country.

Niles may not be incredibly wealthy, but his earning potential in the United States is likely higher than it would be in Ghana. Even if she doesn't have her husband with her, I can understand wanting to wait as long as it takes for him to find a way to bring her to the United States rather than changing the plan.

90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way continues on TLC on Sundays at 8:00 p.m. ET. We'll see how things shake out for Niles and Matilda down the stretch, and keep an eye on the other couples taking part as well.

#3687. EA really doesn't want you to delete Madden NFL 27 to make room for GTA 6

"Don't let 210GB get between you and your league."

Assuming you didn't just buy a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S to play Grand Theft Auto 6, your console's limited storage space is likely already strained, meaning tough choices may have to be made to make room for Rockstar's chonky 212GB crime game.

In a move I don't remember seeing before, EA is asking players to spare Madden NFL 27 from the purge to free up console storage space. As spotted by Push Square, a desperate in-game message pops up when you launch the American Football game, pleading with you not to delete it.

The message highlights 17th November as the date of a Madden NFL 27 update, though its styling, wording and choice of background seem to hint at GTA 6.

"Don't delete!" it reads, as shared by Zirksee on X. "[Encrypted Signal] The target is locked. The crew is assembling for a high-stakes run. Await the signal from our insider on 11/17… do not leak this transmission."

EA's language and intention, however, are much clearer in this post on X, which specifically references GTA 6's large file size in a cheeky way, seemingly promoting the same update.

"Don't let 210GB get between you and your league," the post reads, clearly quoting GTA 6's file size.

The update in question is fairly notable, adding a Madden 97 throwback with era-appropriate players, playbooks and what looks to be 16-bit visuals. Though it's obviously not related to GTA 6 in any way, it's easy to see why EA would fear a significant drop in players once Rockstar's game arrives, something other publishers are undoubtedly worried about.

As part of a recent restructuring, EA laid off 400 employees, closed down BioWare, cancelled unannounced projects and revealed a refocusing on its core franchises and biggest monkey-makers. That includes EA Sports, of course, where a team is currently developing a game codenamed Project Gridiron, described as "a social-first open-world experience for our American Football team".

GTA 6 launches at midnight on November 19 in your own local time zone for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S according to Rockstar support. Since it isn't a simultaneous global launch time that does mean that folks over in New Zealand (and everyone else in the same time zone) will be the first to play GTA 6. More on that below.

I feel like everyone in Florida should get an upgrade from ET to NZ time in this one case, just sayin'.

Okay, this is decades old console lore stuff. As explained above, a rolling launch that happens at midnight local time means that people in New Zealand will unlock GTA 6 first. For big launches of years past, some folks have changed the region setting on their console to spoof being in a different time zone. That means they can unlock the ability to start playing the game before midnight in the time zone where they're actually located, get it?

Is the New Zealand trick going to work for GTA 6? I'm not sure, I only know that people will definitely try it. Some launches of years past have put measures in place to block the trick. Here's Sony's guidance on changing your PlayStation account region versus Microsoft's explainer on updating your Xbox account country, which you shouldn't do unless you're actually moving to New Zealand this month, of course. Don't tell Rockstar you heard anything from me.

All the cloak and dagger stuff is sort of thrilling, maybe, but I'd take a global launch as is standard on PC any day.

#3685. World of Warcraft: Forever's in-game economy has been ravaged by an exploit that allowed players to farm thousands of gold

World of Warcraft: Forever has suffered its first economic nightmare, as a dungeon farm exploit has left some players with thousands of gold in their bags while the vast majority of players are barely above their first hundred.

This exploit was quickly and quietly hotfixed by Blizzard, but not before a currently-unknown number of players were able to make out like bandits. In basic terms, the new Blackmaw Hold dungeon includes several packs of non-elite, easy to kill enemies right at the start of the dungeon. Prior to the hotfix, the loot drop tables for these enemies were incorrect, and worth vastly more in terms of gold than they should have. Keen-eyed players spotted this but kept it quiet, running into the dungeon and quickly killing off these early mobs and resetting the dungeon every hour.

This was possible on every class, and according to Twitch streamer Ziqo, allowed players to farm out hundreds of gold in a few hours. He is seen streaming with over 4,000 gold - and claims other streamers made out with more than that.

For an idea of how much money that is, one of the most expensive things a player will likely buy on their character throughout the original Classic World of Warcraft is the expert riding skill. It takes a long time to save up for, and stands as a major accomplishment in the life of a character. It costs around 900 gold. These players, in just a few days of dedicated grinding, will have been able to pay this price several times over.

Looking at community hubs for the game (Reddit or the official World of Warcraft forums), regular players are demanding Blizzard take action - going further than just the already-deployed hotfix. Maya on the WoW forum wants the ill-gotten gold to be removed and for players to be banned who made use of the Blackmaw Hold exploit, writing: "Remove the gold or I and many others will just quit. This is worse than the bots at this point."

Flnrodi on Reddit, referring to streamers who took advantage of this exploit, wrote: "Not sure what to say. The fact that he did this all offstream says enough that [Ziqo] (and others) knew that this is not intended and 100 percent considered an exploit. Personally, I think there should be some kind of punishment and definitely all the gold [should be] revoked."

You may be wondering why this is such a big deal? So what if a few players can get fancy mounts faster, or snatch up some really good gear on the player auction house? Well, exorbitant sums of money in the hands of a few players can have a massive impact on a server's economy. You could, for example, use your newfound wealth to flip every listing of a certain rare resource on the auction house and mark the price up significantly for profit, which obviously inflates the price for regular players. Likewise, you can out-bid other players for rare and powerful BOE items, which in turn raises the prices of those as sellers may find they can make more cash than they could off such drops prior to the exploit.

This all has an inflationary effect, and could push a server's economy to a more expensive level faster than it otherwise would. Even if this effect isn't so drastic, these players can essentially gear out multiple characters in fantastic gear without putting in the hours, or out-bid the rest of the community on the Black Market Auction House for rare and largely unparalleled special loot.

The counter argument against punitive measures is that these players didn't cheat. They didn't buy gold from real-money-traders, nor did they plug in some external tool to give them an unfair advantage over others. They simply put in the time to get to around level 55, ran a dungeon, and killed mobs repeatedly for valuable drops. Would it have been a good thing to flag the exploit the moment they found out about it? Sure. But once other players at your level take advantage of it, and no strict ruling around whether doing so is punishable, it's arguably in a player's best interest to join in while the going is good.

As of writing, there's been no official word from Blizzard on what it intends to do beyond fixing the exploit. Given the required level to take on Blackmaw Hold, the number of exploiters cannot be too large, and the sheer amount of gold they gained in a small amount of time should make them easy to flag. Rolling back their accounts and reverting the gold they gained back to a pre-exploit amount certainly appears to be a popular option. Whether Blizzard actually does so, or enforces other punishments, is the big question.

#3684. The World’s Favorite Fanfiction Website Has Finally Returned After A Hack Took It Down For Weeks

Readers rejoice, Archive of Our Own has returned. The Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) has announced that the popular fanfiction website has been restored after a security incident late last month required it be taken down for emergency maintenance.

[update] Identified: AO3 is now up! Some features have been temporarily disabled to allow us to bring the site back earlier than the four-week mark. At this time, icons across the site (user icons, collection icons, etc.) are disabled, external work importing is unavaila…

— AO3 Status (@status.archiveofourown.org) 2026-11-15T08:28:56.090Z

Instead of the four weeks that were projected, the outage lasted roughly two, with the site coming back in time for folks preparing for the Thanksgiving holiday break, but possibly not soon enough for authors hoping to bank some work. In the site’s absence, several AI-slop-powered imitators popped up, composed of fics scraped from the site before its shutdown. One such site offered to “pay” authors royalties from purchases of AI-generated audiobooks of their fanfics. After a massive outcry that included alerting OTW of possible copyright infringement, the site was shut down.

The shutdown galvanized online fan communities, many of which resorted to sharing databases of downloaded fics to tide readers over until AO3 could come back. But such emergency fandom measures were themselves the source of discussion and debate concerning the ethics of redistributing fandom works outside of protected spaces like AO3, potentially without authorial consent and in defiance of the etiquette that generally exists between people who write fic and those who read it.

Those discussions aren’t going anywhere, but they may take a backseat now that AO3, like Aragorn busting through the gates of Helm’s Deep, has returned. Some features, including the ability to download fics in specific e-reader formats, are still disabled for now and OTW reports that the site may respond more slowly than normal due to everybody and their mom rushing back to get to their Heated Rivalry fics.

A couple's first Christmas after a wedding can come with a few scheduling headaches.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

With the 2026 TV schedule heading into the holiday season, many are likely preparing for their favorite yuletide programming and getting ready for other festivities. We can reportedly count Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce amongst such people, as they are reportedly figuring out their first Christmas as a married couple. And apparently, deciding where to spend the holiday has become a little complicated. Per a new report, the newlyweds want to celebrate with both families without making either set of parents feel left out.

The Grammy winner and her Kansas City Chiefs tight end husband on married July 3 at Madison Square Garden, an event Kelce later described as one of the best nights of his life. Now, Rob Shuter alleges in his Naughty But Nice substack that the newlyweds have been discussing their first Christmas together. Per Shuter, an insider claims:

Neither wants to disappoint their parents, but they also don’t want their first Christmas as a married couple to become a tug-of-war. They want everyone to feel included.

It's a familiar holiday scheduling problem, although the families involved are rather more recognizable than most. Swift's parents, Andrea and Scott, have long been central to her Christmas celebrations, while Kelce remains close to his mother, Donna, and father, Ed. Swift even grew up on a Christmas tree farm in Pennsylvania, an experience she later turned into a holiday song. With both sets of traditions to consider, choosing where to spend the holiday allegedly hasn't been straightforward.

The Kelces already have some well-established food traditions. Kylie Kelce has praised Swift's baking alongside Donna Kelce's famous dinner rolls, so there would apparently be no shortage of people willing to contribute to Christmas dinner.

Also, the couple may already have a solution in mind. Instead of traveling between family gatherings or deciding which parents to visit, Shuter's sources says Swift and Kelce are considering hosting Christmas themselves. The idea would bring their relatives to one celebration, although no final plans have been publicly announced. A second source told Shuter:

They think bringing everyone together is the perfect answer. They get to start their own traditions without making either family feel they’ve lost out. It’s about creating one big family Christmas.

There's at least one reason a gathering away from a football stadium might be easier this year. As it so happens, the Chiefs don't have a game scheduled on Christmas Day in 2026, according to the team's published schedule. Kansas City is set to host the New England Patriots on Dec. 21 and the San Francisco 49ers on Dec. 27, leaving Christmas Day free of a game-day obligation.

Last Christmas looked a little different for the couple. The Chiefs played the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium on Dec. 25, with Swift and her parents in attendance. She and Kelce also surprised several stadium employees with Christmas gifts.

Kelce has already talked about looking forward to his first Christmas as a married man. Earlier this month, while promoting Tommy Hilfiger's winter collection, he told Women's Wear Daily he was excited to start new traditions with Swift. Although there's at least one he's apparently keeping: his mom Donna's homemade blueberry muffins.

The families have spent Christmas together before. Back in 2023, the “Shake it Off” performer's brother Austin showed up at a Chiefs game dressed as Santa Claus and surprised Kelce with a Christmas present. Both families also played a part in the couple's July wedding, with Austin serving as Swift's man of honor and Jason Kelce standing beside his brother as best man. The newlyweds even asked guests to make charitable donations instead of bringing wedding gifts. So, getting everyone together for Christmas wouldn't exactly be a first for the newlyweds.

Neither Swift nor Kelce has confirmed Shuter's report, so where they'll spend Christmas and whether both families will be there remains to be seen. But with the holiday just a few weeks away, they still have time to figure things out. However they end up celebrating, might I suggest checking out our list of the best Christmas movies? At least that'll give everyone something to watch once the presents are opened.

#3682. Man Allegedly Shot Sister to Death After Their Mom Died in Hospice Care

Police believe that a Mississippi man fatally shot his sister after their mother apparently died of natural causes while in hospice care at their home.

Richard Timothy Ward was charged with three counts of attempted murder on Monday, November 16, after he shot at three deputies with the Escambia County Sheriff’s Office in Pensacola, Florida.

Officers in Long Beach, Mississippi, also said that Ward, 64, is the prime suspect in the killing of his sister, Kimberly Hernandez. However, he has not yet been charged with her murder.

Long Beach police reported to a home on the morning of Friday, November 13, after they received a report of a shooting after a hospice worker found two dead women in the home.

Hernandez, 63, and her mother, Doris Crimmins, were later identified as the victims, according to WLOX.

The coroner said that Hernandez was fatally shot, while Crimmins, 84, apparently died of natural causes while she was in hospice care. An autopsy is expected to be performed at a later date, which will determine Crimmins’ official cause of death. Both Hernandez and Crimmins lived at the home where they were found dead.

Ward was quickly named a suspect in the case and was tracked to the Sweet Dreams Inn in Pensacola, Florida, which is about 130 miles from where his mother and sister died.

Escambia County Sheriff Chip W. Simmons said in a video shared via Facebook that deputies located and approached Ward in his hotel room on Friday afternoon.

As he was approached, Ward allegedly pulled out a gun and refused to put it down despite police orders.

Simmons said that Ward then fired a shot at the deputies, and the deputies responded by opening fire on Ward. Ward was then taken to the hospital for gunshot wounds sustained in the shootout, and he has since been released and taken into custody.

Ward is currently being held at the Escambia County Jail without bond. It’s not currently clear if Ward has entered a plea or retained legal counsel following his arrest.

Authorities said that as he remains behind bars on the attempted murder charge, investigators in Mississippi are working to file charges against Ward for shooting his sister.

Despite naming him as a suspect, authorities have not disclosed a potential motive in why they believe Ward killed his sister and shot at the officers.

The Escambia County Sheriff’s Office and Long Beach City Police Department did not immediately respond to Us’ request for comment regarding updates in the case.

"I'll try to maintain this at least until Valve releases official tracking support for the Steam Controller."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you own a Steam Frame and want to use your Steam Controller at the same time (perhaps even playing 2D games on a big virtual screen), you've likely had to use the passthrough, or just really know your controller. That's because, despite Valve noting that the Infrared LED in the controller makes it trackable in the Steam Frame, it has not yet implemented said tracking. However, a modder has once again come to PC gamers' rescue.

Taking to the Steam Frame subreddit, user Kalluts has shared their Controller Utils GitHub project, saying, "Valve still has not released their official tracking support for the Steam Controller, so I had to take the matters into my own hands."

Effectively, their script turns on the controller's built-in IR LED, using the Frame's tracking services to pick it up. From here, it displays a 3D model of the controller in VR, and it even has a few animations.

The Steam Controller does not work like a traditional VR controller, though one user says, "I just wanted to know if I could attempt to play Beat Saber with it if I stole a second one from my friend. I know it's stupid, but I needed to know." It turns out you can't (and with just the one LED, its tracking wouldn't be good enough for a fun time anyway).

If you're wondering why one might want to use the Steam Controller in VR if it doesn't work like a VR controller, VR headsets can also run flat games on a virtual monitor.

In the right environment, a VR headset makes playing a game feel like you've just jammed a huge TV in your room. Kallut's implementation does have the ability to control the Steam VR UI, though, which is a nice touch. It also works even if you've got a skin on the controller, as the IR shines through the regular status LED on the controller.

As of right now, this Steam Controller tracking support only works in Valve's Stable and Beta SteamOS channels, and the Preview channel has not yet been tested. Kalluts also points out that the one LED makes tracking inconsistent, so if tracking starts to drift, "just hold the controller in front of you again and it should recover eventually."

Kalluts goes on to clarify that "since this interfaces directly with the native tracking, if Valve pushes some updates to those components the tracking might break. But I'll try to maintain this at least until Valve releases official tracking support for the Steam Controller."

We don't yet have a timeline on when Valve plans to implement its own tracking, but this is a pretty good workaround until then.

#3680. Sony squeezes out a PlayStation 5 firmware update before the release of GTA 6

Sony has managed to squeeze out another PlayStation 5 firmware update before the highly-anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

Sony has been rolling firmware updates out on a fairly regular basis, and like many of those updates, this latest one - version 26.07-14.23.00 - doesn't bring any very meaningful changes. Sony repeated the same "we've made some security fixes to the system software" patch-note that we've seen many times before.

And like all those firmware updates, 26.07-14.23.00 is mandatory for all PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles, assuming you want to go online or play the latest games. That, of course, includes GTA 6, which requires the console's firmware to be updated to its latest version before you can play.

The update should download automatically the next time you turn on your console, but you can also force the download through Settings > System > System Software > System Software Update and Settings. This is also where you can tick the option for your console to automatically download and install those updates in the future.

Although Sony hasn't directly said so, the high frequency of those security firmware updates is likely related to the impending release of GTA 6, especially in light of recent gen-AI-driven PS5 jailbreaks.

Any firmware released before GTA 6's release now becomes required to play the game, which delays potential security exploits, seeing as hackers would need to find vulnerabilities in that firmware in order to play. While this may never happen, Sony is at least trying to minimise the risk as much as possible.

GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

Mormon Wives: Orange County doesn’t exactly live up to its name.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you’ve ever watched The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, you know there’s no shortage of drama. Just look at Taylor Frankie Paul, who’s had a swingers scandal, the cancellation of her season of The Bachelorette, custody issues with her children, and chaos surrounding production. But the Hulu reality series was popular and created a lot of buzz, so I was not surprised when they announced the spinoff, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County, currently on the 2026 TV schedule. However, the fact that it feels like the majority of the women in the new show are not Mormon and that some aren’t even wives is a bit weird and an interesting choice, considering the title, and viewers (including myself) have taken notice.

To catch you up in case you haven’t seen the original series, Jen Affleck, a 20-something Mormon wife and mother, joined MomTok in Utah to fight against the typical social norms and stereotypes that are common within the religion. After appearing in Season 34 of Dancing with the Stars as a celebrity contestant alongside fellow Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt, the mother of three with a fourth on the way decided to stay in Southern California, citing the fracturing of MomTok and the need for therapy to recover from everything that happened.

Seeming to instead have decided to jump right into another reality series, which again is an interesting choice, Jen has brought together a new group of friends, all of whom are mothers with their own drama and secrets, but who are not all Mormon, despite the show’s name. One has even admitted to signing on for the heightened visibility reality TV brings.

It’s hard not to notice that The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County is a cast divided into two groups, with the women who are Mormons being outnumbered by the women who are not. In the season premiere, cast member Aspyn Ovard (who's got a memorable storyline about being part of a throuple) says, “We’ve all been shaped by Mormonism in one way or another,” which is a bit of a vague statement when we don’t know all the details of the backgrounds of many of these women, and even she makes it clear that she’s very closed off to the church and its teachings.

I'm not the only one who has noticed this either, as this conversation has popped up all over social media, including places like Reddit, where fans have asked why non-Mormons are "even on the show." I get it's weird to call out someone's religious preferences, but when your show is called Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, I do think that leads to a certain expectation.

When you’re in the business of entertainment, building a franchise off of something successful and popular makes sense. But it’s hard to escape the weirdness of not really delivering on what your show’s title promises. All of this is not to say that the women who make up the OC spinoff cast don’t have compelling lives of their own, because they do, but the religious branding doesn’t entirely fit and feels like more of a subplot than a main focus, like it is in the original series.

And it all makes me wonder if the title should have just been something more reflective of Jen Affleck specifically? Just spitballing here.

For a reality show that’s supposed to be centered around Mormons, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County actually positions them to be the villains of the season. McCall DaPron, the older sister of the OG series’ Mayci Neeley, exhibits confrontational behavior. She gets into frequent clashes with other cast members, often leaving them to wonder whether it’s possible to keep this friend group together.

Her strong commitment to her faith and her efforts to share it with others, including best friend and co-star Jordan McClanahan (whom she successfully converted), rubs anyone not as devoted the wrong way. This is especially true when her need to influence others’ opinions and actions creates conflict.

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives has had a seemingly endless amount of drama and scandals over four seasons, which are streaming with a Hulu subscription, but Mayci always came across like the most supportive one of the group on that show, where McCall seems less inclined to stay neutral. It’s hard to know how much of the drama is manipulated with editing, but it’s another interesting choice on a series that already seems to be trying to break its own formula.

All of this said, if there ends up being a second season of the OC spinoff, I will still definitely be tuning in!

Between Jen being pregnant with her fourth child at the same time she decides she wants a divorce, Aspyn trying to get her ex-husband to spend time with her current throuple, and Salomé Andrea figuring out if she can reconcile with a man she began dating in ninth grade and couldn’t marry in the Mormon church before she ultimately walked away from both, it is all definitely weird, but just weird enough to make me want to see what happens next.

#3678. There’s One Thing I’ll Admit The Ocarina Of Time Remake Made Worse

I wrapped up the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake this weekend, and overall enjoyed it a lot. It was refreshing to go back to the old puzzle-driven style of Zelda after a decade of the sprawling open world of Breath of the Wild. Though thereâs been some debate within the community about whether or not Nintendo made the game too easy, I didnât really pay that much mind. In fact, only one thing in the remake really struck me as a downgrade: the updated version of one of my favorite songs in the gameâs stellar soundtrack.

The Spirit Temple is typically the last major dungeon Link fights his way through in Ocarina of Time before the endgame, and itâs in the dangerous deserts of Hyrule where the player hasnât stepped foot until now. Thereâs an air of mystery to everything youâre doing in this segment of the game, but also precariousness, as youâre in what youâve been taught up to this point is enemy territory. This is the land of the Gerudo, where Ganondorf, the embodiment of evil, was born and raised. So when you arrive here, youâre already on edge, expecting to find some kind of malevolence buried beneath the sand.Â

The music has to capture that feeling of uncertainty, trepidation, and danger, right? The evocative power of the original Spirit Temple track blaring through my CRT TV when I played Ocarina of Time is still a core memory of this game for me. The MIDI instrumentation is unlike anything else in the game, with its use of big, booming gongs, synth strings and, perhaps most importantly, what sounds like a duduk that plays the somewhat dissonant melody. Much of this remains intact in the remake, but the mix is far more ambient, with the melody blending in with the string arrangement, instead of being elevated and piercing through the soundscape.

Itâs certainly more chill, and while the composition is still lovely, the mix just doesnât hit as hard. When I played through the Spirit Temple in the remake, the song quickly became background noise, rather than something that was constantly needling away at my nerves like in the original. Thankfully, I can boot up the 1998 game at any time, but I hope newcomers who never played the original can still get that same feeling of uncertainty and ethereal awe from the remake that I felt when I first walked into the Spirit Temple all those years ago.

#3677. After GTA 6's original soundtrack, Justice probably won't work on any other video game ever again

You've probably heard at least a little bit of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack from French electronic duo, Justice: a single taken from the act's original soundtrack has been released as a standalone track, and was the accompaniment to GTA 6's launch trailer. Featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and the fantastic King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard, it's clear that the duo - and Rockstar - have spared no expense on the production of music for the game.

From what we've heard so far, it's all very good: synth-drenched and poppy, a perfect mix of modern electronica and nostalgic throwback - ideal for the Miami-based setting of Vice City. You ought to enjoy the music while you can, though, because it seems Justice won't be coming back to video games any time soon. If ever.

Via a new interview with French publication Rockyrama, Justice's two members - Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay - shed a little light about their work with Rockstar, and their inspiration for joining the project. "When [the offer to work with Rockstar] arrived on the table, we thought 'if there’s one video game we have to do, it's this one.' As soon as we accepted and started working [on the OST], we thought it would probably be the first and last score we’ll ever do for a video game."

Interesting. The duo, from the clip we can see on Rockyrama's posts, don't seem to give more information about this decision - did they have a bad time working with Rockstar? Was it intense? Or is it rather down to the fact that, if you're going to work on a game, you may as well make it what is largely expected to be the biggest game of all time.

Justice, for what it's worth, consider the work they've done on GTA 6 to be "a real album" of music - it's not seen as lesser or different to the band, just because it's being released as part of a video game. "GTA 6 gave us the excuse and direction to do it. The music always had to be listenable on its own, even if each track is tailored for [a specific] scene," the band explains.

The band's album isn't the only music connected to the game, either. There's also a 34-song album launching for the game, composed of original songs from some of the biggest artists in the world. The album features Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson and many more. The full tracklist leaked at the weekend.

#3676. Man Charged in Murder Plot Wanted Child Dead to Stop Them From Testifying

A man who’s in jail awaiting trial on child pornography charges is accused of trying to hire someone to kidnap and kill a child as part of a scheme to stop them from testifying in his criminal case.

Carlos Manuel Miranda-Berrios, of Kissimmee, Florida, now faces charges in connection with what the Osceola County Sheriff’s Office described as a murder-for-hire plot targeting the child — and the child’s mother if she tried to intervene.

Miranda-Berrios, 30, “had plans for the child to be abducted, subjected to heinous acts, and killed in a manner intended to cause extreme suffering,” the sheriff’s office said in a news release on Monday, November 16.

He’s charged with two counts of solicitation to commit murder, two counts of attempted murder, tampering with a victim, solicitation to commit a forcible sexual offense against a child and solicitation to commit kidnapping of a child, according to the agency.

Detectives learned Miranda-Berrios arranged for the child’s murder to prevent their court testimony in his separate case investigated by Kissimmee police, the sheriff’s office said.

He devised the alleged murder scheme while behind bars at the Osceola County Jail, where records show he’s currently detained.

Miranda-Berrios allegedly offered payment in exchange for the child’s killing and extra money to have their mother killed if she tried to get involved.

Authorities didn’t specify how much money was offered for their deaths.

“Investigators also uncovered evidence that he provided information about the intended victims, discussed payment arrangements, and requested proof that the crimes had been carried out,” the sheriff’s office said.

Court records reviewed by Us indicate Miranda-Berrios’ jury trial in his other case was rescheduled for December 14, after it had been set to take place on October 5.

In that case stemming from 2022, Miranda-Berrios is charged with eight counts of unlawful possession of materials depicting sexual performance by a child and one count of the use of a two-way communications device to facilitate a felony, records show.

A public defender representing Miranda-Berrios in the case didn’t immediately return a request for comment from Us on Monday.

It wasn’t immediately clear whether Miranda-Berrios had retained legal counsel in the murder-for-hire case.

The Osceola County Sheriff’s Office is continuing to investigate and encourages anyone with information to contact the agency.

#3675. "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat" - Square Enix tempts Final Fantasy 14 players back with free game-time to fill void before new expansion

"People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons."

Final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February. So, in order to keep the game populated for the next few months, Square Enix is running a special promotion in hopes of tempting players back in.

This promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies. Lapsed players who haven't logged in for over six months are to be given 30 days of free game time to hop back in and catch up with the main story quest ahead of Evercold's release.

In addition, there's an alluring character skip available too. If your FF14 character is at least level 90 on one class - the current level-cap is 100 - you can skip all the way to the final part of the latest Dawntrail expansion. You still need to grind to level 100 in preparation for Evercold, but the aforementioned free month of game time should provide plenty of time to do so.

In a producer letter written to accompany this promotion, Naoki Yoshida provided insight into why this was being implemented, stating that retaining players in an MMO like FF14 was of the "utmost importance".

"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat", Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed.

"For one, I feel that the pace of change in our lives is growing increasingly fast. Back when A Realm Reborn launched, I set policies in place based on the idea that significant changes in life usually happened in roughly three-year cycles. With that in mind, we've done our best to avoid heavy-handed attempts to secure player retention through game design, and we still maintain that philosophy even today."

Yoshida went on to explain that promotions such as this are meant as a "tiny nudge". He notes that those who have retained subscriptions continuously remain "the most important" players in the development team's eyes, and acknowledges that the process of catching up in an MMO can seem "daunting" for many.

This problem of player retention is nothing new for MMOs, especially in the tricky time between the end of a current expansion and the beginning of a new one. MMO popularity often waxes and wanes, with a new expansion acting as an exciting call to action, with the months leading up to it often serving as a natural break-point for many. Still, monthly subs pay the bills, so keeping folks around even during these quiet months is important.

Final Fantasy 14: Evercold is looking like an especially exciting expansion. On top of the new story and two classes being added, the game is getting an overhaul to combat, with both classic Reborn and Evolved action modes, as well as a new raid difficulty meant to bridge the gap between normal and savage tiers.

The game has certainly come a long way since its initial release back in 2010. Dawntrail proved divisive among fans too, though with Evercold there's a lot of hope that a new overarching storyline can bring the steal back the hearts of players old and new.

Working to a deadline is hard enough, but working towards one that can be moved if you really need it is worse. Grand Theft Auto 6 has been in the works for around a decade, including a couple of delays so devs could polish up some rough edges, and after all this time it must be really hard to step back and say enough is enough.

"They would never stop working on this game if they had the choice," Jennifer Kolbe, head of publishing, says in an interview with The Guardian.

We now know that part of the reason why GTA 6 was delayed was because of the sheer amount of NPCs that needed kitting out with dialogue and audio. Talking to Bloomberg co-head of Rockstar North, Rob Nelson, explained how the delay wasn't strictly necessary but not delaying would have meant GTA 6 "won't be the game we want to make."

Nelson expands on this with The Guardian: "It’s really hard to close it down. If you step away and get a little bit of space from it, you can look at it objectively and go: 'I'm proud of what we’ve done'. But ultimately, it is being taken away from you, and you do the best you can to finish it in the time that you’re told."

“They could have made GTA 5.5, and done it faster,” Kolbe adds. “Ultimately, that’s not what they wanted.” No, instead the devs were hellbent on creating something new, expansive, and an aviary for a few dozen bird species.

"What we have grappled with is the transition from being limited by technical constraints to being limited by human resource constraints," Nelson says. "Like, how much can we physically build? You can keep going forever … People say you can throw money at the problem, and you can to an extent, but it’s no guarantee of making something good."

"You have to take big swings. It can’t be just more of the same."

#3673. Is it time to retire Dragon Quest as a series? Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it might be

Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it may be time for Square Enix to retire Dragon Quest, while reflecting on the direction of the popular RPG series after Akira Toriyama's death. The mangaka, whose art and distinct style were foundational to Chrono Trigger and Chrono Cross - and are still used in Dragon Quest to this day - died in 2024 at the age of 68.

Today, speaking via a blog post on his personal website (hat tip, Power Up Gaming), Mitsuda - a colleague of Toriyama's back in the SNES/Chrono Trigger days - suggested that maybe it's time to retire the franchise in favour of something new. This was all triggered by the announcement of Dragon Quest RPG: The Island of the Demon Tree and the Guided Island, an iOS and Android game that uses art that is very reminiscent of Toriyama's.

"The Toriyama-style illustrations for [Dragon Quest RPG] have become a hot topic, but I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Toriyama Akira fans, and even for the late Toriyama Akira himself," said Mitsuda. "As a personal opinion, since it's impossible to create anything truly new no matter how hard you try, I feel that the Dragon Quest series should be brought to an end for now, and [Dragon Quest creator, Yuji Horii] should create a new RPG. (There have been many remakes already.)"

Horii himself seems undeterred: with the new mobile game's announcement last week, he noted that the goal of his new project is to "capture that unmistakable Dragon Quest feeling" that comes with "exploring towns, meeting new allies, gearing up and steadily growing stronger". As Mitsuda calls for the series to retire, and for something new to take its place, Horii is keen to bring "the same classic adventure" to your smartphone.

"What's important is that the game provides dreams, hope, and experiences that can only be had through games to the younger generation of children who will play it in the future," concluded Mitsuda. "But every time I see topics like this, I realise just how wonderful Dragon Quest is and how it has captivated so many people."

It's unlikely Square Enix is going to want to drop the series, of course: the Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake exceeded Square Enix's (in)famously lofty expectations, and as the company aggressively pursues its multiplatform strategy, it's hard to imagine a world in which it's going to want to move away from a series that routinely pulls in millions of sales.

Some minor spoilers from the new NCIS season follow.

NCIS Season 24 is off to a hot start, and it's been giving a lot of screen time to Michael Weatherly's Tony DiNozzo, who is currently the new NCIS director. With that storyline dominating, there's been little time to follow other fan-favorite plotlines. This has really gotten me to thinking about how the show cooled off on a potential Jessica Knight and Nicholas Torres romance. CinemaBlend recently had the chance to speak to Knight actress Katrina Law, and I had to ask her about what's going on.

I recently had a chance to speak to Law, and after talking about the recent episode marking the first time she worked with her daughter, I had to know what's going on with Torres. I wondered if fans should just give up on Knight and Wilmer Valderrama's character having a relationship. Here's what she said:

Well, as we know in the show, especially one that's gone on to season 24, nothing's ever dead. And there's always a chance for anything to come back. that being said, I feel like there's such a fun dynamic between night and tours that kind of verges on the, the, the side of brother and sister. And with mixed with a little bit of tension in there, which just makes it kind of awkward and fun and like a little sizzly underneath

Law can't just outright spoil anything she's already filmed for the 2026 TV schedule, but it's good to hear this perspective. It seems she's fine with the current situation as it stands, which has remained professional (and only somewhat spicy) so far. As a fan, it always feels like there's a chance it could escalate into something, but both characters seem to wonder if it's worth the trouble.

I actually personally think, based on her first comment, that Law might not want Knight to have a relationship with Torres. Is it because of what she said after, and the guilt she'd feel for Brian Dietzen's Jimmy Palmer? She continued:

If we do lean into that, I feel so bad for Jimmy, because, you know, Knight in Shining Palmer, and I just feel like that's just so brutal. But you know, television, we got to get the viewers in, so who knows where we're going.

I can appreciate Katrina Law's empathy when it comes to Jimmy Palmer. Jimmy and Jessica's relationship was fun while it lasted, but it feels like the door is closed on them ever reconciling and getting back together. Hear me out: Is she just supposed to ignore Torres and the obvious chemistry just because it might hurt her ex's feelings?

Personally, I think fans would say no, and I have a feeling Jimmy would say the same. He's a mature adult, and he's gone through the ups and downs of romance. Provided Nick doesn't start some feud with him sometime ahead of time, I don't see him putting his foot down and not giving this relationship his blessing. It may make work just a little awkward, but I think he'd be able to move past it.

If not, maybe we could see Brian Dietzen's character put in for a transfer, and Jimmy would join another NCIS spinoff. He was a recent guest star on the New York spinoff, so maybe that opens the door to him joining their team at a later date? I'm sure Sam would love to have a vet like him on board, and fans would love to see Jimmy get a new place to spread his wings.

All that aside, though, we'll have to keep watching NCIS on CBS on Tuesdays at 8:00 p.m. ET to see if there's any momentum between Knight and Torres. In the meantime, there's never a shortage of crimes for the team to solve, and it's been fun to see them navigate that with Tony as their boss.

#3670. Call of Duty might have swapped guns and tanks for knights and swords if an Infinity Ward experiment had panned out

"If it's a war story, sure, it can be COD."

As much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold new directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day. And it turns out a medieval Call of Duty was also explored at one time.

This latest revelation comes from Infinity Ward veteran Taylor Kurosaki, who led development on the studio's Infinite Warfare and 2019 Modern Warfare game. "Call of Duty is a massive tree with a lot of branches, right?" Kurosaki told PC Gamer. "It can be World War 2. The team at IW had prototyped a medieval Call of Duty. Where you were a knight and had a sword and all kinds of crazy shit. But if it's a war story, sure, it can be Call of Duty."

This isn't the first time we've heard of an unusual Call of Duty prototype. When Activision brought Sledgehammer Games into the fold as another lead studio for the lucrative shooter series, the team briefly worked on a third-person horror off-shoot set in Vietnam, which was referred to as Fog of War.

Activision's legal battle with Infinity Ward founders Vince Zampella and Jason West, however, caused the project to be cancelled, as Sledgehammer was roped into helping the studio finish Modern Warfare 3.

As for Kurosaki, he currently leads That's No Moon alongside creative partner Jacob Minkoff and other Infinity Ward and Naughty Dog veterans. The studio is currently working on Crossfire, a narrative-driven third-person shooter set in the universe of Smilegate's free-to-play series of the same name.

#3668. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is the US' best-selling physical game so far this year

The very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record. After selling 5.2m copies in four days and becoming the Switch 2's fastest-selling game, Ocarina of Time has now been revealed to also be a major seller at retail.

The remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November). That's according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, who revealed on Bluesky that the record also makes it the first title to surpass 1m physical sales since 2023's Tears of the Kingdom. That is, no other game - from any publisher - has managed to sell over 1m copies in the US within its first week in three years.

While Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US. In July, Piscatella revealed that just seven PlayStation games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies up to that point in 2026, and that was after all the backlash to Sony's decision to end physical disc manufacturing by January 2028.

Ocarina of Time's lead of this particular segment likely won't continue, however. That's because, as Piscatella pointed out in a follow-up post, Circana's tracking considers disc-less, code-in-box versions to be physical editions. This means Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely overtake the remake in short order, just as it's expected to break records elsewhere.

In Eurogamer's glowing review of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, Christian Donlan argued that Nintendo has done just enough to modernise a timeless classic while maintaining what made the original so special for many players.

Investigation into Megaspeed first started in 2024.

Megaspeed is a company with a lot of eyes on it at the moment, and many eyes makes many, uh, news stories. The US Department of Commerce and Department of Justice have thought it to be a good time to drop some details on its investigations into the Singaporean datacentre company, once led by one Alice Huang.

If you've already forgotten who Alice Huang is, she was the person first suspected of having an affair with Jensen Huang. The ex-Nvidia CEO later admitted to an affair with someone that has remained unnamed.

It wasn't just the affair that sunk Huang, it was the suspicion that Alice Huang may be a Chinese Intelligence asset, according to a New York Times report. That was later rebuffed by Attorney General Todd Blanche and the CCP. It was also that the company Alice Huang ran, Megaspeed, was suspected of chip smuggling; and the other two alleged affairs thereafter with Nvidia employees.

"After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential sensitive semiconductor diversion, the Department of Commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations.In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed.In June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its 'no sell' list. Based on the Department of Commerce’s investigation, agents from the Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, conducted an on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed in June 2025 and interviewed CEO Alice Huang."

There's a lot to chew on there. Megaspeed holds it was cleared of any suspicions of diverting chips to China in contradiction of US export rules. It claimed in a statement, dated December 23, 2025 (once the above Commerce investigation had taken place):

"We want to be absolutely clear: over the past six months, our company has undergone multiple on-site inspections and reviews by key institutions, including the Bureau of Industry and Security of the US Commerce Department, the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry of Malaysia, and Nvidia. These thorough investigations have confirmed that there has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities, and this demonstrates that we are a compliant and legitimate company."

Nvidia also long held that Megaspeed was in the clear, with a company spokesperson saying the accusations against Megaspeed were "thoroughly investigated and debunked last year".

That's not quite the end of US investigations into the company, however, as the agencies suggest in their joint statement:

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

"Following this enforcement action [by the Department of Commerce], the Department of Justice took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed."

That doesn't specify that it's ongoing, but the statement begins with the two agencies noting they wouldn't usually talk about an ongoing investigation, but felt it necessary to "provide facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting."

"The Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security working together will bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred. This investigation is the result of the excellent work of the Department of Commerce under Secretary Howard Lutnick and the law enforcement efforts of the Department of Justice under Attorney General Todd Blanche."

On its website, Megaspeed posted the following statement on November 12, the day Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia CEO. It is addressed from Tan Yong Pong, James, Chairman & CEO of Megaspeed:

"Megaspeed takes its compliance obligations under U.S. export control laws extremely seriously. Compliance is a fundamental priority for the company, and Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government.Megaspeed has cooperated with inspections by the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) and stands ready to cooperate fully with any other relevant U.S. government authority.To further reinforce our commitment to compliance, Megaspeed has retained a leading U.S. law firm to lead a comprehensive census of its graphics processing units (GPUs) and independently verify its export control compliance practices.Megaspeed welcomes appropriate government scrutiny and is committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operates responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable U.S. laws."

Megaspeed also said that Alice Huang officially left Megaspeed on August 30, 2025 and has no role with the company.

Singapore has agreed to continue discussions with the US about Megaspeed, which just goes to show how intently the United States is looking into this whole chip affair. The country has also tightened export controls to curb China's access to Nvidia GPUs remotely, as this has been suggested as one way many Chinese models may have been trained on cutting-edge Blackwell GPUs they should not be able to purchase otherwise.

It's an exciting time to be a Marvel fans, given the release of VisionQuest's finale for those with a Disney+ subscription, as well as the upcoming Marvel movie Avengers: Doomsday being a month and change away from its release. Just last week, Anthony Mackie went viral for seemingly spoiling Paul Bettany's role in Doomsday, but now he's defending those comments. The question is: do we actually believe him?

What we know about Avengers: Doomsday is super limited, so there are countless theories and rumors surrounding the project. The Doomsday cast list includes tons of heroes, but Kevin Feige also confirmed that more surprise heroes would be included. So when Mackie spoke about hanging with Bettany on set, fans thought he might have accidentally revealed a twist. In a clip from The Tonight Show's Instagram, the Hurt Locker actor defended himself to Jimmy Fallon, saying:

So Paul Bettany's my man. That's my homie, right? We hang out all the time. He was shooting VisionQuest next door to where we were shooting Avengers. So, me being me, you know, I steal a golf cart and I pull up. I am a pull up-er. If I hear you're there I'm pulling up.

This potentially offers some much-needed context about Mackie's viral comments about hanging out with Paul Bettany while shooting Doomsday. If the actor is to be believed, he knew that VisionQuest was also shooting at Pinewood Studios in the U.K. at the same time as principal photography for the next Avengers flick. That's how he was able to see his frequent co-star, instead of shooting the crossover event together.

Tom Holland has a reputation for Marvel spoilers, but Mackie's comments about Bettany quickly went viral, especially since VisionQuest featured the return of Elizabeth Olsen's Wanda Maximoff. If The Scarlet Witch will appear in in Doomsday, why not Vision? In the same interview Anthony Mackie went on to say:

I didn't say he was in Doomsday. I said he was next door shooting his show. Just like Tom Holland was next door shooting Spider-Man. He was next door! He wasn't in the movie... I guess.

The "I guess" certainly doesn't inspire confidence. Given Marvel's tight security, actors sometimes have to tell white lies in order to guard the shared universe's spoilers. Case in point: Andrew Garifeld lied about returning as Spider-Man for years ahead of No Way Home's release. As such, we're going to have to wait until the next Avengers movie hits theaters to find out whether or not Mackie was telling the truth about Bettany (and Holland).

All will be revealed when Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list. Anticipation for The Russo Brothers' blockbuster is at a fever pitch, luckily the wait is nearly over for its debut on the big screen.
