#3641. Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Sold 1 Million Physical Copies In Its First Week, The Most Since Tears Of The Kingdom

NintendoPhysical GamesRemakeThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

Physical games are dying, unless your game is called The Legend of Zelda. The Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time just sold 1 million physical copies in its first week in the U.S., the most of any release since Tears of the Kingdom released in 2023.

“After just one week in market, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is 2026’s best-selling physical video game in the US,” Circana senior director and video game industry advisor Mat Piscatella posted on Bluesky on November 16. “It is the 1st title to surpass 1M physical units in a US launch week since 2023’s The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.”

Nintendo previously announced that Ocarina of Time sold 5.2 million copies globally across physical and digital in its first four days, which blew the original game’s debut on Nintendo 64 out of the water. It’s a wild number when you consider it’s a Switch 2 exclusive. The newest Nintendo console has only been out for roughly 18 months and only has an install base of around 26 million units, making the attach rate for the game nearly one in five.

There are, of course, two ways to take the Ocarina of Time remake’s physical game sales milestone. The first is to see it as a sign of how strong Switch 2 owners’ attachment to cartridge-based gaming remains even as digital swallows most of the market for game sales. The other is to note that no other game has managed to sell 1 million physical copies in the U.S. within its first week in over three years.

Physical game sales in the U.S. hit a 30-year low in 2025. Back in July, amid the frenzy over Sony’s announcement of the end of PlayStation discs in 2028, Piscatella pointed out that only seven PS5 games released in the first half of 2026 had sold more than 100,000 physical copies at the time. Total spending on physical games actually bounced upward this past August, however, which appears to have been thanks to Switch 2 game key cards.

Physical games might be dying, but on Switch 2 they’re not going without a fight.

#3640. See Bruce Springsteen, Martin Scorsese, and Surprise Guest Tom Cruise Honor Steven Spielberg at MoMA

Bruce Springsteen and Steven Spielberg are good friends. They’ve vacationed together a number of times on the director’s yacht, the Seven Seas. They went to Portofino in 2019, Sicily in 2017, and to Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat in 2024—the latter time with Bono and The Edge. But when Springsteen took the stage at MoMA Thursday night to toast Spielberg at the museum’s annual Film Benefit, he had a bone to pick with the director.

“In June of 1975, I went to a small theater directly across from the Atlantic Ocean and I saw Jaws. I was 25 years old,” Springsteen said. “Now, one of the great pleasures on the Jersey Shore in 1975 was night swimming, preferably naked, on one of those 90-degree, 80% humidity August nights, preferably with someone you wanted to have sex with. There was nothing like after the bars closed, you had a few drinks in you—naked night swim.”

“Steven Spielberg fucked that up,” Springsteen continued. “He fucked it up good. Now, many times over the years, I asked myself, Why? Why would a nice man like that—why would he do that?”

Here at MoMA, a guitar slung around his back, Springsteen then attempted a bit of playful psychoanalysis. He recalled his trips on the Spielberg family yacht. Maybe, thought the guy who wrote “Born to Run,” the guy who directed Jaws is scared of swimming.

“I’ve been on that boat many times and I can tell you: Steven Spielberg does not go in that water— ever. Steven’s boat is so fucking big it has water on it. There’s a pool on it. Steven Spielberg does not go in that fucking pool—and I mean ever,” Springsteen said. “I’m not sure I’ve seen him in a bathing suit. So the reason night swimming is fucked—not just on the Jersey Shore, but every fucking place in the world—is because that nice man, Steven Spielberg, is very afraid of the water.”

“The name of that boat is the Seven Seas,” Springsteen finished. “And I guarantee you, Steven Spielberg has not been in any of the water on any of those fucking seven seas.”

Springsteen added, of course, that he loves Spielberg and his wife, the filmmaker and artist Kate Capshaw. And he wanted to sing a song for them. So he broke into “Dancing in the Dark.”Ch

The whole night was like this. I’ve been to the MoMA Film Benefit a number of times, and it’s always a celebrity-stuffed evening at the museum, always sponsored by Chanel, a highlight of the season. But this was on another level. The museum was honoring a director synonymous with the modern era of blockbuster movies: the avatar of American celluloid excellence, the closest thing Hollywood has to a Michael Jordan. What’s more, there’s a true connection between the art institution and the director. His first theatrical feature, The Sugarland Express, had its New York premiere at MoMA, in 1974, as part of a series called New Directors/New Films.

“This is where it all began, here at MoMA,” Spielberg said. “Why did you wait so long to invite me back?”

He went on to praise the institution’s herculean efforts to restore films and add them to the collection. He also thanked Chanel for dressing him in a look way fancier than his usually quite casual (but fawned over) director ’fits, and for supporting the benefit over nearly two decades.

“MoMA’s dedication, since 1935, to curation, preservation, and restoration is what makes this honor so deeply personal for me, for all of us who love film,” Spielberg said.

Earlier in the night, Spielberg caught up with Amy Sherald, showing the artist some pictures on his phone, as Jeff Goldblum, who played Dr. Ian Malcolm in a little movie called Jurassic Park, pulled up to his table. Nearby, Christopher Walken—who had a great turn in Spielberg’s Catch Me If You Can—was wandering toward his seat, looking a bit lost, when another slightly older man came up to say hello. It was Robert De Niro.

The artist Taryn Simon and her husband, Jake Paltrow, were chatting with Christy Turlington Burns at the bar when Stephen Colbert went up to get a drink. Studio Museum director Thelma Golden was chatting with MoMA board president Sarah Arison, and Jennifer Lawrence strolled in with her husband, the art dealer Cooke Maroney. Michael Ovitz, the collector and MoMA board member for nearly four decades, who happens to also have a long history with Spielberg—“Michael Ovitz, my former agent from a long time ago!” Spielberg said onstage—invited the artist Nicolas Party and the novelist Sarah Blakley Cartwright to his table, with Larry Gagosian sitting nearby.

Lorne Michaels was chatting with collector Ray McGuire—though when everyone sat for the opening remarks, the seat across from Michaels remained mysteriously empty. Soon, a montage of iconic Spielberg clips filled the room. As the lights came up, a figure walked across the stage, mouthing the word “wow” over and over. Surprise: It was Tom Cruise. A MoMA rep, sitting near me, confirmed that Spielberg had no idea that the star of Minority Report and War of the Worlds would be attending the event.

“Since I was a young man, you were very generous with me, always on movie sets—and at your home with Kate, the meals that we had together, the hours that you shared talking about your films and what inspired making them,” Cruise said from the stage. “The stories about you as a young boy with that eight-millimeter camera. You were gracious enough to listen to my stories about the jobs that I took, so that I could buy the tickets to go see your movies.”

Cruise later waded into the crowd to hug his director and take that empty seat across from Michaels. MoMA director Christophe Cherix then got up to gush about his favorite Spielberg movies before introducing the next speaker: Martin Scorsese.

“The films he has made have changed the world. So art does matter. It always will,” Scorsese said. “We’re here tonight surrounded by art in the museum, and it’s really the appropriate setting all the more to honor Steven. And so Steve, I don’t want to… Listen, we’ve known each other since 1972, and how do we get to be in our 80s? What happened?”

To introduce Spielberg himself, the museum managed to rope in Steve Martin and Martin Short, who have never been in a Spielberg-directed movie. Actually, they have no obvious connection to the honoree, except for the fact that they’re two of the funniest people alive.

“You know Steven is very proud that he has never used AI in any of his films. By the way, AI is Steven’s nickname for us,” Steve Martin said.

“I’ll never forget the first time I saw Saving Private Ryan,” Martin Short said. “I found the film so mesmerizing that, halfway through, I whispered into my phone, ‘I’m going to have to call you back.’”

Spielberg was dying in his seat, just losing it laughing, and then had to follow up Martin and Short, which he compared to playing after a Taylor Swift concert. “Marty and Steve, I’d happily follow you anywhere, except up here,” the director joked.

Michelle Pfeiffer, Steven Spielberg, and Michelle Williams

He looked even more moved as Springsteen ripped through a no-bullshit, full-throated performance of “Dancing in the Dark,” which is not something you usually get to see at a museum that’s got The Starry Night and Les Demoiselles d’Avignon hanging upstairs. And then it was time to leave the museum, to go back to the reality of a stormy New York where you can’t catch a cab. In the coat check line, Spike Lee turned to Donna Langley, the studio head at Universal, for whom he’s made a number of pictures.

Then Lee bounced outside, giving a fist bump to every single security guard working the door at MoMA, greeting each of them with what’s going to be a lifelong mantra: “Knicks in five.” “Knicks in five.” “Knicks in five.”

I've had my eye on TCL CSOT—CSOT being a TCL subsidiary responsible for OLED production—for a while now. It might just be the company that brings OLED monitor prices down thanks to its use of the inkjet-printing (IJP) process in manufacturing. TCL CSOT had already said it was moving in equipment for IJP manufacturing and expected production in the fourth quarter of 2027, but the company is now showing off some pretty impressive panels made using the process.

According to Display Specifications (via TechPowerUp), at the Display Tech-Ecosystem Conference 2026 (DTC2026), TCL CSOT showed off a 27-inch, 1440p, 500 Hz gaming monitor made using IJP tech. Apparently, the company describes this monitor as having the "world's first high-refresh-rate in-panel compensation system."

You already knew what that was, right? No, me either. According to Display Specification's understanding of the announcement, it's tech that "continuously adjusts image performance in the background without requiring periodic compensation cycles while the display is powered off."

OLED pixels can degrade at different rates, which is what causes pixel burn-in. The usual method for solving this is to run compensation cycles while the display is off, which takes a few minutes and boosts underperforming pixels up a bit back to where they should be.

It sounds like TCL's new tech will somehow allow this to happen without turning the monitor off, and will just happen as it's being used. Which might compensate for pixel burn-in without as much hassle. Just bear in mind that the word here is "compensation", not "prevention", as it's technically not stopping the burn-in, just, well, compensating for it.

The company also reportedly showed off an ultra-thin 14-inch notebook display prototype using an IJP OLED. I'm not sure how much IJP specifically contributes to the ultra-thinness.

IJP involves printing OLED materials directly onto a substrate rather than having evaporated materials go through a mask. The main benefit is that there's less material wastage, which should, in theory, mean cheaper production and hopefully cheaper costs for the OLED displays made using it. I certainly wouldn't turn my nose up at a 500 Hz OLED that's made much cheaper than it otherwise would be. Roll on 2027, I say.

The world has been waiting with bated breath for the announcement of who will be the next actor to take on the role of James Bond. The rumors have been swirling for months over who would take on the role in the upcoming Denis Villeneuve-directed Bond flick. They've really heated up in the last few weeks as auditions and screen tests have been underway for the upcoming 26th installment of the Bond franchise. Now we know, and it turns out it’s one of the biggest names in Hollywood: Robert Pattinson.

I’m actually a little shocked by this cast, but I’m not mad about it. I was leaning into the Jack Lowden or Callum Turner casting rumors, because I actually didn’t think it would be a star as big as Pattinson stepping into the shoes of the eight men who have previously played Bond. Pattinson has a huge year on the 2026 movie schedule, and this ensures the next couple of years will be busy too, after the announcement was made on social media this morning.

Of course, Pattinson is no stranger to iconic roles. Filming is (hopefully) coming to a close soon on The Batman Part II, in which Pattinson is reprising his role as the Caped Crusader in the second installment of the Matt Reeves Batman franchise. Production on that film has been a slow go, with Reeves recently stepping aside temporarily and Steven Soderbergh joining to finish the principal photography.

Major franchises are also nothing new for Pattinson. Not only did he have his breakout in the Twilight franchise, but he's also joined the cast of Dune: Part III, which is coming to theaters in about a month on what many are calling "DunesDay," as it coincides with the release of Avengers: Doomsday. It is the culmination of the Dune trilogy, also directed by Villeneuve. It certainly bodes well for the next Bond movie that the two clearly have a good working relationship.

I do think the choice of Pattinson to play 007 will come with some controversy, but that’s to be expected. There was never a chance that Amazon/MGM, who own the Bond franchise now, were going to avoid it, no matter who they chose. Pattinson is probably the biggest star to ever be cast in the role for the first time, rivaling when Pierce Brosnan got the role way back in 1994 before GoldenEye. The fact that he is such a big star has caused some blowback, but I think it was to be expected now that Amazon controls the franchise. They are going to invest a lot of money in this. A safe choice of a big star was probably inevitable.

There is still a lot to learn about Bond 26, like who will be the next "Bond Girl" and the rest of the characters we all love, like M and Q. We’ll be busy keeping you updated on all the developments.

#3637. A Look Inside the Scorpion Ball, Princess Grace Kelly’s Scorpio-Themed 40th Birthday Party

Grace Kelly always had a deep passion for astrology. Born on November 12, 1929, she was a Scorpio, and very proud of it. To celebrate her 40th birthday on November 15, 1969, the Princess of Monaco organized a party themed by her astrological sign, resulting in the extravagant Scorpio Ball, held at the Hôtel de l’Hermitage in Monte Carlo. For the occasion, she only invited celebrities who were also Scorpios. Among the 60 or so guests were Swedish actress Hjördis Paulina Genberg, American actor Rock Hudson, and Italian actress Virna Lisi.

Actor Richard Burton was also in attendance, accompanied by his wife Elizabeth Taylor, even though she was born under the sign of Pisces. An exception was made for the actress, who was granted special permission thanks to her husband’s astrological sign—Scorpio, born on November 10. For the occasion, Taylor chose to dazzle, wearing a Cartier diamond necklace with an estimated value of $1 million around her neck—a gift from Burton two weeks earlier. She also wore a spectacular evening cape by Tiziani, made of black velvet and adorned with two rhinestone scorpions on the front and a third on the hood.

Guests were required to adhere to a dress code devised by Kelly, inspired by the colors associated with the sign of Scorpio. Red, black, and white were therefore strongly recommended. The princess, for her part, opted for an off-the-shoulder black velvet dress by Balenciaga from the fall-winter 1967 couture collection. Two ruby brooches set with diamonds—a wedding gift from Prince Rainier III—completed her ensemble.

The decor also reflected the evening’s theme. Red candles, portraits of famous Scorpios, and a lavish cake adorned with golden scorpions set the tone. No detail had been left to chance: The waiters, wearing powdered 18th-century wigs, dressed in velvet suits embroidered with sparkling stars and held silver candelabras adorned with red candles.

Princess Grace was seen on numerous occasions alongside Carroll Righter, an astrologer and Hollywood columnist nicknamed “the astrologer to the stars.” According to People magazine, the princess’s birth chart also revealed a Scorpio ascendant, while her Midheaven was in Leo. In astrology, the Midheaven is associated with career, public image, and reputation. Some attributed her commanding presence and magnetism in the spotlight to this configuration.

Kelly embodied the mysterious aura that her admirers associated with her astrological sign. Unfortunately, that light was extinguished on September 14, 1982, when the Princess of Monaco lost her life in a tragic car accident on the hills above the principality.

#3635. Will 'The Good Daughter' Return After Book Changes? Season 2 Future Revealed

Peacock’s The Good Daughter kept viewers guessing its entire first season — but could the show return for more episodes?

Based on Karin Slaughter‘s book of the same name, The Good Daughter picks up 20 years after a violent attack on a family — with sisters Charlotte (Meghann Fahy) and Samantha Quinn (Rose Byrne) still living with the trauma. Charlotte, who has followed her father into the legal field, is the first witness on the scene when another brutal attack takes place in their hometown, and ultimately the investigation brings back old memories and family secrets.

In addition to Byrne, 47, and Fahy, 36, the show stars Brendan Gleeson, Harper Steele, Paula Malcomson, Jake McDorman, Olivia Williams and Michael Dorman. Despite there only being one book in the series, executive producers Bruna Papandrea and Steph Green addressed the show’s future beyond season 1.

“I just don’t think when we do anything now. If you’d asked me when we made Big Little Lies if there would be more, I would have said no. It’s like you’ll never get this group of people together again. It was a one-off, right? Cut to where we are now,” Papandrea exclusively told Us, referencing the HBO series developing its third season. “This was definitely built as a limited series, that’s for sure. There is a prequel book that Meghann just did the audiobook for that is just centered around Charlie.”

Papandrea noted that she wouldn’t mind keeping The Good Daughter a limited series.

“I very much like to live in the show we’ve made and let the audience discover it in all its kind of glory. You never discount anything because you know TV shows are so hard to get made and built,” she continued. “I always say if someone wants to make more, you always have to be open because it’s such an exciting thing to really fall in love with your own characters and the world and the team. I mean, it’s such a beautiful thing to go back again for more.”

The creative team also spoke about the onscreen book changes. “This one was an odd process because normally what would happen is I would get sent a book and decide to option it and then find a screenwriter,” Papandrea shared with Us. “Karin decided to take a crack at adapting [The Good Daughter] herself and wrote a pilot.”

Slaughter went on to write the scripts for every episode.

“It was the most amazing process because it was a book I immediately fell in love with. But then one of the things that really impressed me is you don’t meet Rose Byrne’s character in the book until 100 pages in,” Papandrea noted. “Obviously you can’t do that in a TV show.”

She continued: “Also, in terms of the way we were telling that story and the sisters came back together, you had to find a structural way to change that, which somehow at the end of the first episode she did. For me, that was one of the biggest structural shifts that happened in adaptation.”

Papandrea promised that the show is still “very faithful to the book,” adding, “But also I think the filmmaker becomes a massive part of that and builds the visual language around that, and we were all in from very early on in terms of developing the scripts.”

The Good Daughter is streaming now on Peacock.

#3633. Jensen Huang’s Potentially Seismic Art Retreat

Welcome to True Colors. I’m in Manhattan. Lots to get into this week. There’s the matter of what to do about a major new San Francisco arts institution that was set to be named after Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori Huang. Understandably, it’s a question whether that renaming will still happen given…everything. There’s my ode to the death of the Cybertruck. And there’s all the details from the star-studded MoMA Film Benefit honoring Steven Spielberg. Tom Cruise shocked the crowd with surprise remarks, and Bruce Springsteen roasted the director. It was a whole night.

MENTIONED IN THIS ISSUE: Donald Trump, Jason Calacanis, Brendan Dugan, Siniša Mačković, David Zwirner, Lorenzo Amos, Kate Capshaw, Zohran Mamdani, Jessica Craig-Martin, Dean & DeLuca, Indochine, Stanley Whitney, Marina Adams, Will Whitney, The Beverly Hills Hotel, Elon Musk, Lana Del Rey, Grimes, Travis Scott, Pharrell Williams, 21 Savage, Tyler, the Creator, Bad Bunny, Julia Wachtel, Todd von Ammon, Frieda Toranzo Jaeger.

The major arts institution named for Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori, appears to be—shocker!—very much in jeopardy.

Just months ago, Huang was getting a phone call from President Trump while onstage at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles. “I’m here with the besties, Mr. President,” a laughing Huang said, putting his phone up to the mic. “Tell him I say hi!” said All-In cohost Jason Calacanis.

But Huang’s recent weeks have not been marked by good times with the besties. First, the Democrats took over Congress, throttling all the goodwill he built with the administration. Then he admitted to having an extramarital affair with a woman suspected by the US to be a Chinese spy—and then news of another affair, this time allegedly with a subordinate, came via a shocking New York Times bombshell. Amid rumors that yet another affair would soon break, he stepped down as CEO and, according to Forbes, has watched nearly $20 billion of his estimated net worth vaporize since Monday.

What’s unknown is the current state of his relationship with his wife, Lori Huang—and their ambitious plans for an arts organization that was set to bear their name. Earlier this year, the Huangs pledged $75 million to Vanderbilt University in order to help transform the soon-to-be-closed legendary San Francisco art school California College of the Arts into part of Vanderbilt’s SF campus. Vanderbilt announced that it planned to name a portion of its SF campus the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design.

Which is now a bit awkward, given the multiple alleged affairs, and the whole Chinese-spy thing. Plus, Huang is no longer affiliated with Nvidia, which teamed up with CCA in 2025 to form the CCA-Nvidia Incubator for Creative Intelligence. Will Jensen and Lori Huang still put their names together on arts organizations after all that’s happened? And if there is no Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design, what will happen to Vanderbilt’s SF campus when it opens next year?

The CCA was started in 1907, and Huang and his wife were expected to support its transition to a new chapter. It would be a shame if this is how it ends. Reps at Vanderbilt didn’t get back to me.

It’s a new era in Tribeca. Tonight, Karma, a burgeoning mega-gallery with spaces in New York’s Chelsea and LA’s Hollywood, opens its new gallery at 38 White Street. Founder Brendan Dugan and director Siniša Mačković took me on a tour earlier this week, and it’s easily one of the most generous spaces anywhere in the neighborhood. Plus, an outpost of Karma Bookstore—a much needed bookstore for a neighborhood shockingly lacking in one—is coming in right across the street.

This will be the latest big-tent blue chipper to take a space in the Triangle Below Canal, as they used to call this neighborhood. Something to consider: In the last few years, mega-galleries such as David Zwirner and Hauser & Wirth have shut their uptown townhouses and opened downtown.

Also opening tonight is a White Street outpost of Gratin gallery, which has a roster of incredibly exciting young stars, including Lorenzo Amos (whom we wrote about a year ago). I’m hearing about other younger dealers grabbing spaces in the neighborhood. The art market isn’t exactly on fire, but dealers are betting on one thing: the enduring power and capital of New York City.

Speaking of New York, guess who’s lived here full-time for almost a year? Steven Spielberg, that’s who. On New Year’s Day 2026, the GOAT American director—who is married to the artist Kate Capshaw—moved his official residence from California to New York, and has made the apartment in the San Remo his home base. You will not be surprised to hear that, post-move, Spielberg is doing extremely cool stuff in town. He’s walking around with a script and a Tracy Kidder book while slugging down an iced McCafé. He’s getting lunch at Benvenuto Cafe. He’s having Mayor Zohran Mamdani over to the crib.

The only thing left was for one of the city’s great museums to throw a big party for the Hollywood-royalty-gone-Gotham. Last night, Spielberg got just that: He was honored at the MoMA Film Benefit, sponsored by Chanel. I was there. Read the full report—with fun pictures!—here.

Also on VF this week: an exclusive excerpt from an uproarious new memoir by artist Jessica Craig-Martin, I Regret I am Able to Attend. Craig-Martin is a real treasure of the art world, a great photographer—and, as it turns out, a hell of a writer. The whole book is a compulsively readable blast. The chapter where Craig-Martin recalls working as an extremely inexperienced, occasionally larcenous teller at Dean & DeLuca is one of the funniest, most satisfying New York vignettes I’ve read this year. And of course, all the scuttlebutt from the ’80s art scene is fabulous. Read the excerpt, in which our narrator spills all the tea—and, um, stuff stronger than tea—about working as a waitress when Indochine opened.

Happy 80th birthday to the great painter Stanley Whitney. His wife, the artist Marina Adams, and son, dealer Will Whitney, threw Stanley a party to celebrate his octogenarian status on Nine Orchard’s roof, overlooking Dimes Square. Writers, artists, dealers, old heads, everyone was there. A fabulous Wednesday night.

#3632. Miley Cyrus Reacts to 2027 Grammy Nomination With Godmother Dolly Parton

Miley Cyrus is reflecting on her lifelong bond with her late godmother and mentor, Dolly Parton, following their joint 2027 Grammy Award nomination.

“My Aunt Dolly is one of the greatest songwriters the world has ever known,” Cyrus, 33, said via a Monday, November 16 tweet. “She never made music for recognition but to make the world a happier place through her songs.”

Cyrus and Parton received a Best Country Duo/Group Performance Grammy nomination on Monday for their remake of “Light of a Clear Blue Morning” alongside Lainey Wilson, Queen Latifah and Reba McEntire. Parton was also nominated a second time in that same category for her and the Zac Brown Band’s duet, “Butterfly.”

The 2026 reinterpretation of Parton’s inspirational 1977 single “Light of a Clear Blue Morning” was released to raise money for pediatric cancer research at Nashville’s Monroe Carell Jr. Children’s Hospital at Vanderbilt.

Reflecting on her latest Grammy nomination, Cyrus shared that it was particularly meaningful since Parton gifted her a vinyl copy of her 1977 album New Harvest…First Gathering — featuring the original version of “Light of a Clear Blue Morning” — “a couple Christmases ago.”

“To be nominated alongside her, Lainey Wilson, Queen Latifah and Reba McEntire for Light of a Clear Blue Morning is a beautiful way to honor her enormous heart,” Cyrus tweeted on Monday. “This cover supported pediatric cancer research at Vanderbilt’s Monroe Carell Jr. Children’s Hospital, a cause close to her heart.”

She added, “I miss her calling on big days like this but feel her in every moment. Love you Aunt Dolly. Congratulations to these beautiful women and all the other nominees.”

Cyrus publicly mourned her mentor when Parton’s rep announced the legendary country music singer-songwriter’s death at age 80 following “a brief battle with cancer” in August.

“The feeling of losing my Aunt Dolly is beyond what feels right to share. Our most sacred moments were private and they’ll stay there behind the stage, beneath the glamour & between our hearts,” Cyrus wrote via Instagram on August 25. “What I KNOW is Dolly would want me to feel it, write a song about it, and then continue on and be strong. I have an angel by my side. I always have. One of our last conversations was about music and metamorphosis. 🦋.”

The “Wrecking Ball” singer continued, “I will always love her and want to make her proud. My heart breaks for the world, her family and friends who will miss her deeply. We’re in this loss together and we will see her in all of the most beautiful things.”

Cyrus broke down on stage during an October show at the Hollywood Bowl, revealing she’d only ever seen Parton perform “live in concert one time in my entire life” — and it was at the very same historic Los Angeles area venue.

“Now, I spent a lot of time backstage and … if she was playing the show, I’d be standing right beside her in a matching costume,” she beamed.

The 69th Annual Grammy Awards will air on ABC and Disney+ Sunday, February 7, 2027, from Los Angeles’ Crypto.com Arena.

#3629. How To Play GTA 6 A Day Early

Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6PS5Rockstar GamesXbox

Grand Theft Auto 6 isn’t out in the U.S. until November 19, but if you want to play a day early, there’s a way. Here’s what you need to do.

The global launch for GTA 6 starts at 12:00 a.m. in New Zealand on November 19, which is actually 6:00 a.m. ET on November 18 in the U.S. Yay, time zones! In order to start playing at that time, however, you’ll need to do different things depending on whether you’re playing on PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S.

On Xbox Series X/S, the method for unlocking GTA 6 a day early is relatively straightforward. Just go to your settings menu, scroll down to “System,” Â and select “Language and Location.” From there, choose New Zealand and choose the option to restart your console. When it boots back up, your system will behave as if it’s in the New Zealand time zone, right down to the Microsoft store that decides when your games go live. Easy!

A similar New Zealand trick is possible but not nearly as straightforward on PS5. On Sony’s console you need to create an entire new PSN account and select the country during the setup process. You then need to purchase GTA 6 through the New Zealand version of the PlayStation Store.

Assuming you don’t have a bank account or credit card registered to that country, you’ll need to purchase New Zealand PSN gift cards online for the total amount ($80 for the standard edition or $100 for the deluxe version). If you already purchased a U.S. version and pre-installed, sorry, that won’t be good enough. Is buying an entire second copy worth it to you to play roughly 18 hours early? Maybe!

The good news is that you don’t have to play your New Zealand version of GTA 6 only on your New Zealand PSN account. Instead, you can go to the settings menu on your NZ PSN account, open “Users and Accounts,” choose “Other,” and then select “Enable” in the “Console Sharing and Offline Play” section. This will let your regular U.S. PSN account access the game so all of your save data and trophy progress sticks with your main account.

If you chooseÂ not to jump through all of these hoops to play early, you can start playing GTA 6 at midnight tomorrow along with the rest of us.

#3628. GTA 6 And These Other Games Can Justify An $80 Price, Expert Says

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases on November 19, and you'll have to pay at least $80 for it. That's a full $20 more than what GTA 5 cost in 2013 and $10 more than many other big AAA games today. Is $80 going to become the "new normal" for AAA games, or is it, along with Nintendo's Mario Kart World and Tears of the Kingdom for Switch 2, an outlier at $80?

According to Alinea Analytics researcher Rhys Elliott, $80 won't be an across-the-board new price for all games. Some developers will purposefully price their games lower to draw in more consumers--he pointed to games like Expedition 33 ($50), Phantom Blade Zero ($60), and Oblivion Remastered ($50) as examples.

Elliott said that when GTA 6 inevitably becomes a huge success with its $80 and $100 editions, some publishers will be "jumping for joy" because they'll take this as a signal that the market will indeed accept these higher prices.

However, Elliott said he hopes the industry doesn't learn the wrong lessons from GTA 6 and its $80 price point. "GTA 6 is as inelastic as things get in entertainment. People will pay anything to get their mitts on this one, which makes it seem like the perfect Trojan horse for an industry-wide price rise," he said.

"The $80 price point will be a Godsend to some publishers, but it’ll be a snowball's chance in hell for others. After all, this kind of stuff can be zero-sum. When a player spends $100 on GTA 6, their remaining budget shrinks," he added.

Elliott went on to list off some of the studios and game franchises that could likely get their fanbases to buy in at $80. He said these include the next big God of War game after Laufey, the next Naughty Dog game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, and future Forza titles (assuming Xbox strips them out of Game Pass). Additionally, Elliott said From Software "has the cache" to charge $80 for its new games, while Hogwarts Legacy 2 could also up the price to $80. Elliott added that some of the top sports games could charge more, but that might be a tougher sell considering those games are full of microtransactions already.

"So not all games were created equal, and mid-tier AAA publishers--and also bigger publishers offering smaller games or remakes--will price downward at $40-$60," Elliott said.

There are a lot of factors at play here. For starters, GTA 5 launched at $60 back in 2013, and that same $60 is worth $86 today after inflation, making GTA 6--at least its $80 edition--effectively cheaper than GTA 5.

At the same time, many people are acutely aware that their pay has not kept up with inflation, while the federal minimum wage hasn't moved up since 2009. GTA 6 is also coming out at a rough time for many people, with gas and grocery prices surging, and the cost of everyday goods generally spiking due in part to increasing inflation. And anyone heading to a store to buy a console to play GTA 6 on is in for some serious sticker shock, as game consoles today are more expensive than ever due to the AI craze.

New video games generally staying the same price over the years has had serious negative effects on the entire industry, experts have said. It's part of the reason why publishers now try to squeeze people more with DLC, battle passes, microtransactions, collector's editions, paid early access, and more. Recently, an Xbox advertising chief said price increases would be a hard sell, so the company is turning to ads to help offset ballooning budgets and keep the business healthy.

Director Martin McDonagh has become as well-known for making memorable films as he is for writing the complex male friendships within them.

"I like mining down into the sensitivity that I think a lot of male relationships do have, but aren't as – especially in American films – explored sensitively," he said about the subject during a panel conversation at the inaugural Vanity Fair Screening Room at LACMA on Friday. "It's not just a buddy film, and it's not a romance, and it's not just about cool CIA guys," McDonagh continued. “It's sort of the opposite in other ways. The acclaimed dark comedy follows two CIA agents (Malkovich and Sam Rockwell) who are not only behind the plan to overthrow the Chilean government in 1973, but have also had a hand in several other significant historical moments in the US and abroad.

Maria di Girolamo, John Malkovich and Martin McDonagh, in conversation with Rebecca Ford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on Friday, November 13, 2026.

Malkovich and Rockwell's characters engage in pithy, often hilarious banter throughout the film, and their onscreen chemistry is a highlight.

John Malkovich at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

He is a great student of film and of theater, and he's great fun, very hardworking, and just an ideal colleague. I couldn't imagine a better colleague than Sam and I've had some excellent colleagues.”

"He's one of the best actors of his generation, if not the best," adds McDonagh of Rockwell. "He's always surprising, always dangerous, always sensitive, always smart, always coming up with new stuff. And I think there's a danger to him that's lovely to write for. We always hope the characters will always be surprising, and with Sam's voice in the head, that really helps."

Mariana di Girolamo at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

For rising star Mariana di Girolamo, a Chilean actress making her English language movie debut with Wild Horse Nine, she was excited and only slightly intimidated to be a part of the cast.

"It was quite a challenge to perform for the first time in English," she said. "I prepared myself with a coach and we rehearsed with John, Sam and Parker [Posey] and Ailin [Salas] in a public theater in New York where I heard the script for the first time. That was amazing for me, for us." di Girolamo, who is very familiar with the fraught period of Chilean history depicted in the film, said she appreciated how McDonagh put it all in context. "It was my first time approaching that period of time in this way with this very beautiful dark humor. I was laughing about these things and feeling empathy with these CIA agents that committed a lot of horrific, horrific things. I've never read something like that, and the arc of my character is so beautiful, unique, I really wanted to be part of this."

Martin McDonagh at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

#3626. Stars Who Have Broken Grammy Records: Beyonce, Taylor Swift and More

Beyoncé and Taylor Swift are just a few of the big names who have broken Grammy records over the course of the awards show’s history.

In 2023, Beyoncé became the most-awarded artist in Grammys history with the 32nd trophy of her career, taking home the trophy for Best Dance/Electronic Album for Renaissance. It was her fourth win of the 2023 ceremony.

Two years later, Beyoncé added even more Grammy wins to her resume thanks to Cowboy Carter, becoming the first Black woman to win Best Country Album. She also won Album of the Year and Best Country/Duo Group Performance for “II Most Wanted” with Miley Cyrus.

Another Grammys favorite, Billie Eilish, swept the 2020 awards show with wins in the biggest categories of the night, including Album of the Year, Song of the Year, Record of the Year and Best New Artist, when she was just 18 years old.

“[Billie] was very grateful, obviously, and a lot of her friends were there,” her brother, Finneas O’Connell, told Vogue in February 2020. “She has more ‘go with the flow’ than I do, but we were both kind of embarrassed to win so much; you hope that it will be kind of equal, but after the third in a row … Well, we love all our fellow nominees.”

The producer noted that he was pulling for Lizzo or Lil Nas X. “If I’d bet on anyone, I would have lost money in us winning everything,” he said.

We've gotten glimpses of Lithgow in the role of the Hogwarts Headmaster in previously released Harry Potter footage, but this new clip puts more emphasis on his mannerisms and I am loving it.

The clip opens with the newly sorted first years seated with the rest of their houses and chanting for Dumbledore. Once they're tucking into their feast, Dumbledore and Professor McGonagall have a chat about Harry being sorted into Gryffindor. "The cat that got the cream" is a clever idiom from the headmaster, when taking into account McGonagall's animagus abilities. For such a brief conversation, it really tells us a lot about the headmaster. He's playful and thoughtful all at once.

When Minerva comments on how much Harry looks like his father, Dumbledore's response is:

Looks can be deceiving, Minerva. His nature is entirely his own.

I love that Dumbledore isn't quick to assume Harry is everything like his father. McGonagall's tone is affectionate of course, but still softly suggests some expectation from the 11-year-old that Dumbledore seems quick to gently shut down. There are so many sides to Albus Dumbledore, and I love how this clip shows Lithgow grasping more than one of them.

Beyond Lithgow's words in this scene, there's also his mannerisms. Before he sits down, Dumbledore snaps his fingers to prompt the food to appear on the tables. Then, when it's time for dessert, I'm assuming that little flourish of his fork as he's about to grab some meat, is the prompt to turn dinner service into dessert for the kids. It's little details like that that I can't wait to see more of.

On the less positive side, I'm not entirely sure I love the way the food appeared. There was something slightly off -- or maybe slightly too perfect? -- about the way the food snapped into reality that bugged me. I'm trying to keep an open mind as we see more magic in use in this series, and it's possible my brain is just too familiar with the sight of the plates appearing in the movie -- which is admittedly a wide shot from very far away before we see the food close up -- to accept this new version quite yet. (Considering some of the food featured in the movie had apparently spoiled after sitting out for days of filming, maybe I shouldn't cling so much to memories that scene.)

I will say that when the dessert appeared, my brain flashed back to that scene in Hook when Peter finally sees all the food at the table. Dumbledore may have conjured dessert for the students, but he conjured instant childhood memories over here, and my stomach growled.

We're a little more than a month out from the premiere of Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone. It seems likely that HBO will give us another glimpse or two between now and then, but nothing will compare to sitting down for the first episode when it debuts on Christmas. Between what we know and love from the books and scenes that weren't straight from the page, there will be a lot to dive into as Season 1 gets going.

Kelly put her life-long love of movies, TV and books to greater use when she joined CinemaBlend as a freelance TV news writer in 2006, and went on to serve as the site’s TV Editor before joining the staff full-time in 2011 and moving over to other roles at the site. At present, she’s an Assistant Managing Editor who spends much of her time brainstorming and editing features, analyzing site data, working with writers and editors on content planning and the workflow, and obsessing over the best movies and TV shows. She graduated from SUNY Cortland with BA in Communication Studies and a minor in Cinema Studies. When she isn't working, she's probably thinking about work, or reading (or listening to a book), and making sure her cats are living their absolute best feline lives.

#3624. Official Zelda Website Raises Eyebrows By Labeling 3DS Game As Playable On Switch

Nintendo is celebrating The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversary in many different ways, but one detail on the company's official website raised confusion--and curiosity-- about a classic 3DS Zelda game.

A "History" page on Nintendo's website lists every mainline Zelda game in release order, including the release date and which platforms you can play for each entry. The site marks every game that's playable for Nintendo Switch Online subscribers--and the 2013 3DS game The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds was marked as such. The NSO icon has since been removed from the site.

Currently, the Nintendo Classics library allows NSO subscribers to play select NES, SNES, and Game Boy games, while the Expansion Pack subscription includes access to Nintendo 64, Game Boy Advance, GameCube, and Virtual Boy games. There's currently no way to play 3DS games on Nintendo Switch, prompting the question of whether this was an error on Nintendo's website or an accidental leak that A Link Between Worlds will somehow be playable on Switch. GameSpot has reached out to Nintendo for clarification on the matter.

The site appropriately labels the Zelda games featured on Nintendo Classics if they are only playable with the Nintendo Switch Online Expansion Pack subscription, which applies to Ocarina of Time (the original), Majora's Mask, A Link to the Past/Four Swords on GBA, The Wind Waker, and The Minish Cap.

If this labeling for A Link Between Worlds were true, it would be surprising if the Expansion Pack were not required to play it. Nintendo Classics also lacks any Wii or DS games, so jumping straight to 3DS would be a bizarre move for the service.

Whatever the case, A Link Between Worlds is a magnificent entry in the Zelda series that deserves to be experienced. GameSpot's 9/10 review of the game called it an "absolute treat to play" with some of the "best Zelda dungeons in years."

#3622. You Can Probably Guess WoW: Forever’s Most Popular Race, Class, And Faction

World of Warcraft: Forever has been in the wild for one week, and now we have all kinds of stats to sink our teeth into as they relate to the most popular races, classes, and faction in the latest version of developer Blizzard's MMORPG.

Forever launched November 4, becoming the biggest launch in WoW history by concurrent and returning players. Aside from that fact, Blizzard hasn't shared additional information on exactly how many characters have been made or what classes are most popular.

For that, we turn to Raider.IO, a WoW stat-tracking website more commonly used in the modern version of the game to provide rankings and details related to raids and Mythic+ progression. 

According to the site, close to 3.9 million characters have been created across all regions and rulesets so far. Around 48% of those characters are on the Alliance, with nearly 52% being on the Horde.

The most popular two races aren't all that surprising--undead and humans. Despite being the most boring choice imaginable, humans have always been a popular choice in WoW Classic thanks to their strong passives and the ability to be most classes. In Forever, they currently make up 37% of the Alliance population. Undead, on the other hand, are getting a massive boost from being the only Horde race to currently have access to Paladin. They make up nearly 40% of the Horde.

It won't shock you to learn then that Paladin is Forever's most-played class, with undead Paladin being the most-played race-and-class combo.

Skyborne elves are WoW's newest playable race, available to both factions. Around 10% of all characters are Skyborne, and faction-wise they are fairly even. Around 10% of Skyborne are Alliance and close to 11% are on the Horde. Consdiering how popular blood elves are in other versions of the game, the number of Skyborne feels low by comparison, though the fact they cost $30 to access probably has something to do with that.

As for what rulesets are most popular, the normal (PvE) server is far and away the biggest, with over 2 million characters. The PvP ruleset isn't too far behind with around 1.5 million characters. Those two rulesets dwarf the size of the game's two RP rulesets, which combined have around 250,000 players. 

With the exception of standard RP, every ruleset has a larger Horde population, a subject Blizzard recently commented on officially. In a forum post, Blizzard announced its goal is for PvP servers to be as close to 50/50 faction balance as possible, and would be placing restrictions on creating Horde characters on PvP rulesets in an effort to make that a reality.

"World of Warcraft: Forever's PvP is at its best when the Alliance and Horde are on equal footing, and we are dedicated to helping maintain that balance so that we can all witness battles at the epic scale that has made WoW: Forever PvP so memorable thus far," Blizzard said.  

One week after WoW: Forever's shockingly smooth launch, we've been impressed how visual updates and Blizzard's changes to the classic WoW formula have made the MMO feel brand new again. Forever received its first major class and dungeon changes earlier this week.

#3621. Andrew Scott On What Makes Elsinore “So Moving”

Although the emotional core of Elsinore is centered around beloved actor Ian Charleston dealing with terminal illness, its star Andrew Scott says the film has as much heart as it does humor.

“The most singular thing about our film I think is the humor in it,” he said during a panel conversation at the inaugural Vanity Fair Screening Room at LACMA on Friday. “The tragedy in some ways is a little bit like Hamlet itself, but you can't make a film about Ian Charleston without having gags in it. He was incredibly funny. Every person [who knew him] said he was just wickedly funny, and flirtatious, and he was always looking towards the light, and he had a certain degree of courage. So that is something I think that we all share as a sense of humor.”

Andrew Scott, Billie Piper, Stephen Beresford and Rebecca Ford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

Elsinore tells the story of Scottish actor Ian Charleson (Scott) who attempts to perform Hamlet at the National Theatre while secretly living with AIDS. Scott has received early acclaim for his powerful portrayal of Charleson. Before the film began Vanity Fair’s West Coast Editor John Ross warned the audience that "first you're going to laugh, then you're going to cry," while watching Scott’s performance.

“I think … why the film is so moving is because [Charleson’s] not wallowing at any point. He was insanely courageous,” continued Scott. “So that to me was the thing that we were the most

insistent on in some ways. And that's really all down to finding actors who in this extraordinary ensemble have a really terrific sense of humor. And we kind of knew that we could, with the screenplay, get the best actors in the country. And I feel we did.”

The panel conversation featured Scott, costar Billie Piper, and writer Stephen Beresford, moderated by VF's Senior Hollywood Correspondent Rebecca Ford, following an exclusive screening of the film.

Billie Piper at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

For Piper, who plays Charleston's close friend Patsy, she relied heavily on Beresford's script for her prep, as well as information she gleaned from those who actually knew Patsy, and Charleston.

“I've spoken to a few members of the family, their friends, and then I sort of cherry-picked things from people I'd known in the beginning of my career, the louder figures in our industry,” she said. “And then I did my own interpretation and just had a good time. It's a very moving story, but I had a lot of fun playing that part. She's a really joyful character to play, I enjoyed the comedy. And I understand that a lot of her jokes are coming from a place of despair.”

Beresford, who has known Scott for 25 years, said he didn't initially think of his longtime friend for the role, but should have.

“The story of Ian, and Ian's Hamlet [performance] is legendary in the British theater,” he said. “So many people said it was the greatest Hamlet they'd ever seen, and that it had this incredible quality. So I knew about the story, and then it was brought to me actually as an idea by a producer who said, ‘What about writing about Ian Charleston, and what about Andrew playing Ian Charleston?’ And then I just thought, ‘Well, why didn't I have that idea myself five years ago?’ So yeah, that's really how it happened, and I started to research it, the details of the story were so incredible, and so moving.”

Stephen Beresford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

Scott, who famously played Hamlet onstage 150 times beginning in 2017, prior to filming Elsinore, closed out the panel conversation by reciting his favorite line from the classic tragedy.

“When Hamlet says the line about the war that was going on—and this was written 400 years ago—it just seems so relevant to what he might have been experiencing at the time, which is: ‘I see the imminent death of 20,000 men who for a fantasy, a trick of fame, go to their graves like beds.’ The idea that that was written 400 years ago, and that he was watching 50 percent of his friends die for no reason and be neglected by governments, and derided by the public. And it was just happening, and happening time and time again.”

Scott continued: “The reason that I love it so much is that when I was doing Hamlet myself, of course I wasn't thinking about the AIDS crisis, but the enduring nature of art, something that was written 400 years ago by Shakespeare, could actually be of use to somebody in 1989 and then be reproduced again in 2026 and be of use. And that idea of art being useful down the lines is so moving to me.”

Vanity Fair's Global Editorial Director Mark Guiducci, Elsinore stars Andrew Scott and Billie Piper and writer Stephen Beresford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

Spoilers ahead about the most recent episode of The Great British Baking Show.

I love reality TV, although most of the shows I watch are cutthroat like Survivor, The Traitors, or the Real Housewives. I decided to watch The Great British Baking Show for the first time this year with my Netflix subscription, and have loved how charming and wholesome the series is in comparison. As such, I was surprised when the latest episode legit made me cry, largely thanks to how much Moyin was crying over Connie's elimination. Luckily there is a silver lining with this heartbreak.

Bake Off has been a joy to watch, from Nigella Lawson's passion for eating to the kindness the contestants extend to each other. Last week's Pastry Week had my mouth watering, but for Caramel Week it was my eyes that was producing the moisture. I was bummed to see Connie eliminated, but it was the way Moyin was weeping that had me feeling misty. I mean, just look at these two.

While the cast of Bake Off all formed sweet bonds (pun intended), Moyim and Connie were on another level. Throughout the season they were shown getting close, forming a mother/son relationship in the process. They'd also help each other's bakes when needed, despite competing against each other.

Moyim's emotional reaction to Connie's elimination was moving, as he was devastated despite winning Star Baker. I was left in a puddle by the time the latest episode ended, but luckily the franchise cheered me up thanks to some delightful content of their reunion. Case in point: the following video from Bake Off's official Instagram account. Check it out for yourself below.

A post shared by The Great British Bake Off (@britishbakeoff)

I mean, how adorable are these two? Clearly their bond extends outside of the Bake Off tent, and they've remained close in the time between filming and the current season airing. It would have been heartwarming enough to merely see Connie and Moyin reuniting, but the fact that they showed off their dance moves in the above video is even more delightful. So while the latest episode of The Great British Baking Show made me cry, I'm back to enjoying the show's immense charm.

From the premiere of Bake Off's season, it seemed like the cooling process was going to be a challenge for the bakers in the midst of a heat wave across the pond. That proved challenging for Connie during Caramel Week, and after fumbling both the Signature and Showstopper, Connie was ultimately eliminated. Cue the tears.

New episodes of The Great British Baking Show air Fridays on Netflix as part of the 2026 TV schedule. We'll just have to see if the remainder of the season makes me cry again, or if it'll stay charming and wholesome.

#3619. GTA 6 Could Sell 55 Million Copies By Early Next Year, Report Says, And Average Selling Price Could Be $90

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, and it's expected to be a gigantic commercial success, but just how big will the launch be? Investor's Business Daily compiled data from a series of analyst reports about the game and its owner, Take-Two, and the consensus is that it's going to be a juggernaut.

In terms of sales, Brian Pitz of BMO Capital Markets said GTA 6 could sell 55 million copies during Take-Two's fiscal 2027, which ends on March 31, 2027. He said the game could sell 45 million units alone during the game's launch quarter, which is well ahead of the estimates of 34.2 million that IBD compiled.

 "This is an outlier in every respect," Circana's Mat Piscatella told the publication. "There have been some big game launches in the past, but nothing quite at this scale, not only in terms of the investment, but in terms of the anticipation. It's in its own league."

GTA 6 is launching with an $80 standard edition and a $100 Ultimate Edition. Raymond James analyst Andrew Marok said he's forecasting 50 million unit sales for the fiscal year 2027, and that the blended average selling price will be close to $90. According to Sensor Tower, early data suggested preorders were skewing toward the $100 edition, but by launch, it could be around 50/50.

Matthew Cost of Morgan Stanley, meanwhile, said if GTA 6 does indeed have strong sales out of the gate, this could create a "large potential audience" for the next iteration of GTA Online. Rockstar has not said anything yet about an online mode for GTA 6, but given the huge success of GTA Online for GTA 5, it's all but guaranteed that GTA 6 will incorporate online multiplayer as well.

Cost said this is a big deal for investors and may represent "the next major catalyst" for Take-Two's stock price. Take-Two's share price is down about 10% so far in 2026, and currently trades around $228/share..

A new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 would no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways to spend more money, and that could be frustrating for fans but great news for investors who want to see bigger returns.

D.A. Davidson analyst Wyatt Swanson said Take-Two's share price could surge to $300 in part because he believes Rockstar will release a PC edition of GTA 6 and usher in GTA Online 2.0. These releases would "enable structurally higher margins" for Take-Two, he said.

According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has already sold 12 million copies and generated $1.2 billion in revenue. GTA 5, meanwhile, took 72 hours to clear $1 billion in revenue--GTA 6 reached that a week before release, apparently.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

#3618. Is Scola Saying Goodbye to 'FBI'? John Boyd Weighs In After Nina's Promotion

FBI revealed a major twist in Scola and Nina’s love story — but does it mean that actor John Boyd is leaving the series?

Warning: Spoilers below from season 9, episode 7, of FBI.

“I don’t want to rob the fans of their worry, you know, that experience. But there’s no plans on paper for John Boyd to leave FBI that I know of,” Boyd, 45, exclusively told Us of his career trajectory after his character, Special Agent Stuart Scola, revealed he plans to put in his papers for a transfer to their San Diego office.

The actor teased, “But we’re certainly testing the waters here to see what it means to be an FBI agent who’s married to the love of his life and has a child and is not willing to live across the country from his partner. I mean, that’s where we’re at with the story now.”

During the Monday, November 16, episode, Scola and his wife, Special Agent Nina Chase (Shantel VanSanten), teamed up for one last case in New York City ahead of her move to California with their son, Dougie, after she secured a big promotion.

At the end of the episode, Scola revealed, “I think I’m going to put in for the transfer.”

Nina was shocked by his declaration, telling him, “No. I can’t ask you to do that. You can’t leave behind everything that you’ve built. Your team. Your life.”

Scola stopped her, saying, “You’re my life. You and our son are my life. And I’m going to be wherever you are.”

The pair kissed while looking at the Big Apple skyline, hinting that Scola will be making his way to California once his paperwork gets approved.

Boyd told Us that as an actor, he isn’t leaving the CBS show anytime soon — but that doesn’t mean the series won’t toy with the idea of Scola moving the remainder of the season.

“As an actor, it would be fun to get to play it all the way to the end of like, you know, ‘See you guys later.’ But I don’t know what they’re gonna do with that,” Boyd told Us. “We just explored a whole you know [Special Agent] OA leaving [briefly]. So you know maybe it’s not time for that yet.”

VanSanten, meanwhile, joked with Us that Boyd’s desire to stay on FBI has thwarted any spinoff plans fans might want.

“OK, ‘So dear CBS, please cancel a request for Scolina spinoff. John does not want to leave FBI.’ Cool. I just wrote the email,” VanSanten, 41, told Us, pretending to type a letter to the powers at be.

The actress noted that if a spinoff happened, Scola and Nina would “have to be willing to work on cases together,” which is something they promised not to do after welcoming their son.

“Unless you’re going to be my boss. Or I am your boss?” VanSanten said with a laugh.

Boyd confessed that Scola in California doesn’t make sense in his mind.

“My whole thing is Scola as a guy from New York is San Diego seems like the last place a New Yorker would ever want to go,” he explained.

VanSanten chimed in, asking, “Don’t they have, like, a Lego museum? It’d be great.”

Boyd teased that “maybe” a spinoff could work “as long as it’s like he’s miserable there and doesn’t get it. Like, ‘I don’t get the deal with San Diego.’”

While a spinoff has not been confirmed, Boyd told Us that the next few episodes of FBI will focus on Scola’s “secret” transfer request.

“Scola has this secret that he’s carrying, and the longer we go without him talking about it with anyone, the more and more it’s becoming a secret,” he said. “He’s not talking about it, so when it does come out and he starts discussing it with his teammates it’s gonna be interesting.”

VanSanten added, “It’s kind of the slow burn, right? That’s the show. The show goes on. Like a case happens in a day, the next day there’s this case. You don’t have time to talk about it, but everybody knows that it’s simmering and that it’s there.”

#3617. GTA 6 Owner Take-Two Is Not Interested In Selling Itself After EA Goes Private For $55 Billion

Recently, the gaming giant Electronic Arts was taken private in a $55 billion sale to an investor consortium led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. Could GTA 6 owner Take-Two be the next big company that gets acquired? Don't bet on it, CEO Strauss Zelnick says.

Speaking to David Rubenstein, Zelnick said Take-Two's business results have proven that it "can do very well as an independent company."

He said Take-Two's business is already "at scale" and healthy enough financially with a "terrific balance sheet," as he put it.

"We are not in a place where we need to be part of a bigger organization to be competitive. And in the entertainment business, scale matters," he said.

Zelnick said companies that do less than a billion in annual revenue might have issues with developing, marketing, and distributing games at scale. Not only that, but companies that don't generate a lot of money might not be able to survive the realities of the creative business, in which sometimes your product flops.

"But once you're over a billion dollars in annual revenue, and we're way beyond that point. Our guidance is $8 billion to $8.2 billion this fiscal year, additional scale doesn't seem to help you succeed."

In early 2008, Electronic Arts privately pursued a buyout of Take-Two, but after the GTA and BioShock company rejected it, EA went public in an attempt to get a deal done. Later that year, EA abandoned its plans to try to buy Take-Two after the GTA company said it was worth more and EA refused to increase its bid.

In 2019, it was rumored that Sony was attempting to buy Take-Two, but that was ultimately deemed to be unconfirmed market chatter and not a formal bid.

Take-Two has a market cap of more than $42 billion, and that is expected to grow in the year ahead, so it would seemingly take a lot of money to convince Take-Two to sell. Going forward, Zelnick has teased that new GTA games could release even faster, and that could be a positive for the company's financials.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Preloading is underway now, and that's good news because the game has a massive file size.

#3616. Hillary Clinton Showed Up For Dinner at Gloria Steinem’s Townhouse

It’s a dark and stormy November night at Gloria Steinem’s townhouse, and Hillary Clinton has something to say about the 2026 election. “One of my most anticipated moments will be watching Donald Trump walk into the State of the Union through the now more than one hundred women members of the House of Representatives. I just want them all to stare at him and say, ‘You fired us from jobs we were qualified for. You insulted us. You demeaned our ambition. You undermined our place in government and society. And we’re here.’”

Huma Abedin, Busy Philips, and Paloma Elsesser.

The former Secretary of State and 2016 presidential candidate is a last-minute but highly anticipated arrival to this dinner honoring Steinem, the late activist. She passed away in September, but the feminist pathfinder was known for throwing these salon-type events (she called them “circles”) at her Upper East Side townhouse, which she bought for just $30,000 in the late ’60s. It’s overflowing with books (I spy Marilyn by Norman Mailer, Jane Fonda’s War by Mary Hershberger, and several Eleanor Roosevelt biographies on the shelves), pictures (there’s one framed of Steinem alongside Mariska Hargitay) and Indian art. (Steinem spent two formative years in the country.) There are magnets in her kitchen of Wonder Woman, Frida Kahlo, and a cloth finger puppet of Hillary Clinton. A political button is pinned to it that says “Another Bitch for Hillary.” The whole place smells like a Cire Trudon candle, and everyone’s drinking negronis. (Which actually isn’t technically very Steinem—her favorite cocktail was a margarita—but the negronis go with the night’s dinner, prepared by Lilia chef Missy Robbins.) Yet this is one of the first events at the townhouse that Steinem herself isn’t here to lead.

Jihae, Lux Pascal, Naomi Watts, and Bethann Hardison.

Amy Richards, a feminist activist whom many consider to be the daughter Steinem never had—a title Richards rejects because her mentor “didn’t want kids”—stood up at one point to tell the crowd that this is what Steinem would have wanted. Growing up with a transient father and a mentally volatile mother, the late activist took near-obsessive care in maintaining a welcoming home she could share with others. “As long as I knew Gloria, she always said, ‘I just want my home to be the way it’s always been.’ She wanted it to be filled with people,” Richards says. “She didn’t grow up with a home. She was traveling the country for the first 10 years of her life and then lived with her mother, who was not very stable.”

At least Steinem’s still here on the wall: Months before her death, she posed for a series of portraits by Paola Kudacki for Weldun, a platform that offers physically adaptive and functional fashion. It was a bit of a small miracle that Steinem said yes. “I will say, Gloria did not always love to be photographed,” Richards says. “Especially in her later years—not because of wrinkles or aging, but she was just like, ‘Aren’t there enough pictures of me?’” Weldun and the Gloria Steinem Foundation are presenting tonight’s dinner, and mementos of Steinem are everywhere. On the fireplace mantle sits a pair of her signature Ray-Ban aviators. But Gloria’s stuff isn’t the same as Gloria herself.

Former secretary of state Hillary Clinton hugging Melissa McCarthy.

Which is probably why, in a crowd of women that include Huma Abedin, Mariska Hargitay, Padma Lakshmi, Melissa McCarthy, and Bethann Hardison—who, at the ripe age of 84, shows up wearing Gucci—Clinton’s unexpected arrival feels seismic, like Gloria sent someone in her place. (Hardison tells me she thinks Steinem used whatever divine power she’s got up there to launch the Blue Wave: “She’s probably saying she helped it happen!”) Whatever your views on Clinton’s politics, she was the first woman to receive a presidential nomination from a major party. Paloma Elsesser and I sit crouched in a corner of the room, glued to the window. “There’s mother,” the supermodel whispers to me as Clinton exits her car into the pouring rain and walks up to the townhouse door.

Guests at dinner honoring the late Gloria Steinem.

“Hi, everybody,” Clinton says as she walks in. The entire dinner comes to a silent halt. “Hi,” the room responds in unison. Madame Secretary doesn’t seem to like the fuss, probably because 30 or so people intensely staring at you when you arrive at a party is objectively unsettling. “Go back to eating!” she says, motioning to the Missy Robbins meal on the table. Clinton sits down next to Naomi Watts and warmly greets Busy Philips, who stumped for Clinton back in 2016. Hargitay blows her a kiss across the table. All anyone wants to do is talk to Clinton about the 2026 election, in which Democrats won at least 55 seats in the Senate and 256 in the House to take both majorities in the US Congress. At the end of the meal—and after a proper catch-up with Shonda Rhimes—Clinton tries to leave, but she can’t. Guests block the door, clamoring to chat her up.

Amid the Clinton traffic jam, I ask Hargitay about the photo. She can’t remember exactly what it is from. “Was it Bravo? Was it with Andy…what’s his name?” But she can guess what she thinks Steinem might say about the blue wave: “There is a God!”

I watch Clinton finally make her exit. It’s late, so I wait several minutes before I descend the stairs to leave too. (I wait for Elsesser, Watts, Hardinn, and Lux Pascal to finish taking a selfie on the steps.) But I spoke too soon: Clinton’s stuck waiting for the coat check, another group of women crowded around her hoping to say something—or, more likely, hoping she says something. With the way this night is going, Clinton might be the last one at the party.

I thought I'd made peace with saying goodbye to James Gunn's Guardians of the Galaxy. The third movie wrapped things up beautifully, and with Gunn running DC Studios, I figured there wasn't much chance of getting the old gang back together. Well, Hollywood has a funny way of changing plans. Gunn is leaving his leadership position at DC, and Chris Pratt is already talking about the possibility of making another Guardians movie with him. Let me just state for the record that I'm right there with him.

With Avengers: Doomsday approaching on the 2026 movie schedule, Pratt's future as Star-Lord has been on my mind lately. During a recent interview with MovieZine while promoting Way of the Warrior Kid, the actor was asked whether he'd be interested in reuniting with Gunn for a fourth installment. He hadn't spoken to the filmmaker since the DC news broke, but his answer was encouraging:

He directed all three movies, and that's pretty rare… so if he wanted to come back and bring it back, I would love that.

Well, now I want it too. Gunn spent nearly a decade building one of Marvel's strangest superhero teams into something audiences genuinely cared about. Somehow, he also made me cry over a talking raccoon more times than I'd care to admit.

This conversation is considerably less cheerful for DC fans. Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-heads of DC Studios following the Warner Bros. ownership shake-up, with former Marvel executive Jeremy Latcham taking over Dec. 1, raising plenty of questions about the DC Universe's future.

Gunn isn't exactly sitting at home waiting for Marvel to call. He's still involved with Man of Tomorrow, his follow-up to 2025's Superman, which is scheduled for July 2027. He also has other DC-related work on his plate. Still, stepping away from running an entire studio should eventually give him more freedom to choose what he wants to direct. But does he want to direct a fourth GotG?

Pratt's comments are especially interesting because he previously had some pretty specific thoughts about returning as Star-Lord. Last year, I covered his concerns about finding somebody who could fill Gunn's shoes. At the time, it seemed unlikely the filmmaker would ever be available. Suddenly, that possibility doesn't sound quite so ridiculous.

There's also the matter of where we left Peter Quill. At the end of Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3, he returned to Earth to reconnect with his grandfather, while Rocket took charge of a new Guardians lineup. The movie's closing credits promised Star-Lord would return, though the powers that be haven't said in what capacity or which new Marvel flick he might show up in.

Pratt recently confirmed there have been conversations about bringing him back, which is encouraging. Although returning for another Avengers movie and reuniting with Gunn for a fourth Guardians adventure would be two very different things. There's still no indication that Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 4 is actually happening. Gunn spent years saying the third movie would conclude his trilogy, and he may have no interest in revisiting those characters. I certainly wouldn't blame him for wanting to move on from comic book and superhero fare to something completely different. At this point, he's been helming superhero content for more than a decade. Maybe he wants to spread his wings and take on a different type of movie, which I would be stoked for as well.

Still, I love the idea of Pratt and Gunn finding their way back to each other, especially after everything they accomplished with the first three movies. Maybe it's wishful thinking, but if Gunn ever decides he's ready for another trip into space, I hope Marvel answers the phone.

The first three original Guardians of the Galaxy films are available to stream with a Disney+ subscription.

#3613. “Physical” GTA 6 Copies Might Be Vulnerable To A Very Stupid But Serious Trick

Grand Theft Auto 6 ditched traditional discs for its "physical" launch, with Rockstar's game being sold as a digital code-in-box at retailers beginning this week. However, it appears a packaging choice may have accidentally left the game vulnerable to thieves--assuming they have a flashlight.

As shared on the forum ResetEra, users who received a physical version of Grand Theft Auto 6, at least in PEGI regions, report that the game's download code is printed directly on the inside of the cover rather than on a card or separate insert. When a flashlight is focused on the cover from the outside of the closed game case, the download code is visible in reverse.

In other words, there's a serious risk people could go into a store, do this trick, redeem the code, and leave the poor soul who actually buys the game off the shelf without GTA 6.

At this time, the trick does not seem to work on North American copies of GTA 6, as the code is intentionally obscured. Why Rockstar would not use this strategy on all regions is unclear. We've reached out to Rockstar for an explanation and will update this post if and when we receive a response.

If you happen to get your GTA 6 code stolen after paying $80, you can at least sleep soundly knowing that the thief can't play the game yet. Code-in-box copies, as well as digital preorders, all unlock for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.
