#3612. GTA 6 Is Like The Olympics – “A Rare Cultural Moment” With Massive Ripple Effects

After years of development, multiple delays, and what can only be assumed to be one of the biggest production budgets ever, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19. The game is poised to "blot out the sun," some experts believe, and its release looms so large that other gaming companies are shifting dates for their own games to stay out of the blast radius. 

Francis Lawrence, the director of the new Hunger Games movie Sunrise on the Reaping, which comes out a day after GTA 6, has said he hopes people can find the time to play the game and watch his movie. In short, GTA 6 is seen by some as a black hole that will suck up time, attention, and money from the broader gaming economy--and even workplaces, as people dive into the 80-hour game they've been waiting a decade to play. 

To help make sense of, and contextualize, the enormity of GTA 6's looming launch, GameSpot caught up with Bart Spiegel of the global professional services and research company PricewaterhouseCoopers, or PwC. He told GameSpot that GTA 6 is "something much bigger than a traditional entertainment launch," and is more akin to an event like the Olympics.

He believes GTA 6 is a "rare cultural moment" that "commands extraordinary attention and creates economic activity well beyond the event itself."

Spiegel said he foresees potential shifts beyond gaming, in places like TV viewership, music consumption, social media engagement, and even travel. "In an increasingly fragmented entertainment landscape, it's rare for a single release to command this much attention across so many industries simultaneously. That's what makes this moment so significant," he said.

An economics professor recently claimed that about 1.5 million people plan to "call out sick" to play GTA 6, and this could come at a "cost" of $1 billion to the US economy. Spiegel said people should remember that GTA 6 isn't anything new or special as it relates to taking time off work. "People regularly plan time off around major cultural and entertainment events, and this is another example of consumers prioritizing an experience they're excited about," he said.

That being said, Spiegel remarked that PwC has observed estimates suggesting time-off requests near GTA 6's release could be 9% to 17% higher than normal. "But what's more interesting to me is what happens outside the workplace. If millions of people are spending additional hours gaming, they're potentially spending less time watching television, going out to restaurants, or engaging in other activities," he said.

"And unlike a sporting event that lasts a few hours or a few weeks, this experience could keep people engaged for months. So the broader economic implications may extend well beyond a single day of missed work," he added.

"Huge net positive"

GTA 6 is expected to be an enormous success commercially--it's reportedly already sold 11 million units through pre-purchases, and that could rise to 25 million at launch. That would work out to $2 billion in revenue, which would cover the game's entire development budget and most of its marketing spend, Sensor Tower said. But many are also saying that GTA 6 represents the last of a dying breed, and that other publishers might learn all the wrong lessons from its success. Spiegel said GTA 6 is going to be a "huge net positive for the gaming industry as a whole," in part because its success will reiterate to the broader entertainment and media landscape that games are culturally significant. At the same time, Spiegel said he doesn't foresee a world in which other publishers try to replicate a blockbuster of this magnitude. 

"Very few organizations have the capital, expertise, and intellectual property required to support investments on this scale. These are extraordinary events, not necessarily repeatable business models," Spiegel said. 

If GTA 6 is the huge success it's projected to be, it could positively uplift the broader gaming ecosystem in a lot of ways, Spiegel continued. 

"It could attract new audiences, renew investor interest, and create opportunities across advertising, payments, technology, and content creation. The real lesson isn't that everyone needs to build the next billion-dollar game. It's that gaming is an increasingly powerful part of the entertainment economy, with opportunities that extend well beyond the games themselves," he said.

Some companies, like Ubisoft, see GTA 6 not as something to be strictly afraid of. CEO Yves Guillemot says, that's because the rising tide that is GTA 6 could help drive more people to gaming overall. In fact, Ubisoft is putting out a big new update for one of its biggest games, Rainbow Six Siege, right around GTA 6's launch.

Mat Piscatella of Circana reminded people that not everyone wants to play GTA 6, and he pushed back against the theory that it's a bad business idea to launch a game near GTA 6.

"The fear of many teams to put their game in the same window as GTA is completely overblown. GTA is going to be a massive game. Of course it is. It’s going to be a huge cultural event, but not every one of the 49 million people who own a PS5 or an Xbox Series in the US is going to be interested in that," he told GamesBeat.

Could GTA 6 lead the push to more in-game ads?

Spiegel went on to say that one additional follow-on effect from GTA 6 could be something that gamers might balk at but publishers and investors might salivate over. He said that if GTA 6 succeeds in the way people expect it to, and draw people into its world for tens--or even hundreds--of hours, that could demonstrate to the wider market that it's time for gaming, as an industry, to do more with advertising. 

"When millions of people are spending substantial amounts of time in interactive entertainment environments, it's natural for advertisers and investors to consider how they might participate," he said. 

Advertising for mobile and social games is already commonplace, but it's less present in the PC and console gaming market. There are examples, of course, as companies have already undertaken efforts to put ads into gaming with mixed results. Gamers quickly revolted when EA put ads in a UFC game, prompting EA to pull them quickly to help quell the backlash. Despite that, EA recently announced the formation of a new EA Advertising division that will seek to put ads "directly into gameplay." That announcement didn't go over well, either, as fans pushed back against the idea of having to see ads in yet another place in their life. Other examples have been received more positively, or at least ambivalently, with a trucking company buying ad space in the American Truck Simulator series to help recruit staff. 

Xbox, for its part, has big plans to put more ads in gaming. Xbox CSO Matthew Ball said advertising in console games could help with the "two-sided problem" that AAA gaming faces today. Development costs keep going up and up, and Ball said ads--as long as they're not overly in-your-face--could be a way to help developers make more money and solidify their business fundamentals. Of course, if these companies insert more ads into gaming, that doesn't mean they'll stop hawking things like DLC, microtransactions, and battle passes; they'll likely both happen in concert. As Spiegel sees it, though, if executed correctly, advertising could be a big boon for gaming.

"What's particularly interesting is that the opportunity extends beyond placing advertisements inside games. There's an entire ecosystem of digital advertising infrastructure, technology, and services that could benefit as gaming continues to grow. I expect we'll see increasing interest in those opportunities, particularly from investors looking for exposure to gaming without taking on the considerable financial risks associated with developing blockbuster titles," he said.

More investment

During the COVID years, the gaming industry saw massive revenue and player growth as people, forced to stay inside due to stay-at-home orders, turned to games to pass the time, have fun, and connect with friends. At the same time, interest rates were historically low. The cost to borrow money was so attractive that publishers ramped up significantly. 

The COVID-era boost to gaming did not last, though, and the industry is now challenged, to say the least, with numerous developers cutting staff, cancelling projects, and scaling back in other ways. If GTA 6 is indeed a massive success, it could trigger renewed interest in gaming as an investment vehicle, Spiegel believes, but not necessarily exclusively for funding new games and studios. Instead, Spiegel said he foresees big investment growth for discrete elements of gaming, including advertising, payment services, and AI buildouts.

"I absolutely think a release of this magnitude will get the attention of investors, corporate executives, and private equity firms. But I don't necessarily think that translates into another wave of billion-dollar game development," he said. "The economics of producing games at this scale are incredibly challenging, and very few organizations have the resources, expertise, and intellectual property necessary to justify those investments."

"Instead, I think investors will increasingly ask how they can participate in the broader gaming ecosystem," Spiegel added. "That could mean opportunities in advertising, payment infrastructure, technology services, mobile gaming, or artificial intelligence applications that support game development."

On the subject of AI, Spiegel said he believes it's a "particularly interesting variable" because it could, at least in theory, allow developers to work more efficiently and bring down costs. There is debate about whether or not this is a genuine reality or wishful thinking on the part of AI companies trying to sell their products and services. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, for example, recently told Business Insider that, despite Take-Two adopting AI products for some of its workflows, the company has not seen a material decrease in its cost structure. In fact, many theorize that AI-supported workflows will only make work more intense. For his part, Spiegel said AI in game development remains only an "emerging opportunity rather than a guaranteed outcome."

"The longer-term impact may be less about creating another generation of massive blockbusters and more about directing investment toward the businesses and technologies that support the gaming economy," he said. 

Who should be afraid?

A lot has already been said and written about publishers moving their release dates to avoid GTA 6, and Spiegel said he foresees dramatic possibilities for how GTA 6 could take the wind out of the sails of other entertainment near its launch. He said GTA 6 is not just a major gaming launch. Instead, he thinks it's an "event that could temporarily reshape how millions of consumers spend their time and money."

"Streaming could be particularly vulnerable. Every hour someone spends gaming is potentially an hour they're not watching a television show or movie. And because this launch falls just before the holiday season, it could make it difficult for streaming services to match the exceptionally strong viewership numbers we saw last year," he said.

Movie theaters could be tested, Spiegel said, and one highly anticipated film, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, will be one to watch in particular. It comes to theaters on Friday, November 20, which is one day after GTA 6 releases. Director Francis Lawrence said he hopes fans find the time to play GTA 6 and go see his movie, but it remains to be seen what effect, if any, GTA 6's release will have on that film's performance at the box office. Spiegel said movie studios are banking on the belief that the theatrical experience "offers something consumers can't get from their living rooms." 

There is a Thursday Night Football game happening on the same day that GTA 6 releases, with the Indianapolis Colts taking on the Houston Texans. Spiegel said the live-sports category overall could be "more resilient" because of its nature as an event happening live that fans of those teams, or fans of the NFL in general, feel compelled to watch live as it happens. A movie or TV show, meanwhile, is on-demand entertainment. 

GTA 6 is a hugely anticipated release, and it's poised to bring lapsed gamers back into the fold, but anyone who doesn't already have a PS5 or Xbox Series X|S should prepare themselves for sticker shock. That's because, for a variety of reasons, new consoles today are actually hundreds of dollars more expensive than they were when they launched in 2020.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has frankly acknowledged, "The rising cost of hardware is not a good thing." At the same time, Zelnick isn't shaking in his boots about what this means for GTA 6. He thinks GTA 6 will be so good and so compelling that people will buy in no matter what.

"I don’t think it will slow us down any because, you know, we’re delivering, we believe we’re delivering experiences that people want,” Zelnick said. “However, a lower price point for hardware would be a good thing because there’d be more hardware in people’s hands."

Who benefits?

In terms of companies, products, people, and services that could benefit from the ripple effects of GTA 6's release, Spiegel said music associated with the game could surge in listening activity. This has already happened, as streams of Tom Petty's "Love Is A Long Road" surged after the first trailer for GTA 6 used the song back in 2023. More recently, Cliff Richard's 1976 hit "Devil Woman" showed up in the GTA 6 Extended Look on Netflix, helping the song reach more people, including young people who maybe never even knew about the song. Spiegel said social media platforms could benefit from GTA 6's release as well, thanks to fans uploading gameplay clips, livestreams, and other forms of user-generated content inspired by GTA 6. Beyond this, the world of food delivery could see an uptick in activity as people opt to stay in to play GTA 6 (while in-person restaurants and other nightlife venues could take a hit). 

"The broader point is that the impact could extend into parts of the economy we don't traditionally associate with gaming," Spiegel said. "For business leaders, the question is whether they're competing with this cultural moment for consumer attention or finding ways to participate in it. That's what makes this launch so much more interesting than simply tracking how many copies are sold."

#3611. 'SNL' Alum Heidi Gardner's Boyfriend Ray Tintori Dead at 43

Saturday Night Live alum Heidi Gardner‘s boyfriend, filmmaker Ray Tintori, has died. He was 43.

The New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner confirmed to Us on Monday, November 16, that Tintori’s death is currently under investigation, and the “cause and manner of death are pending further study.”

Us has reached out to Gardner’s rep for comment. TMZ was first to report the news.

Tintori was an accomplished music video director, having worked with major music acts such as Solange Knowles, The Killers, Arcade Fire and MGMT. He was credited as a special effects unit director on the 2012 fantasy movie Beasts of the Southern Wild, which received four Academy Award nominations and won the Grand Jury Prize at that year’s Sundance Film Festival.

Ray’s father, John Tintori, was a film editor who worked on Eight Men Out and Mr. Wonderful while his mother, Mary Cybulski, was as a script supervisor and photographer on Life of Pi, Syriana and The Ice Storm, among other projects. (Cybulski died from glioblastoma at age 70 in November 2025.)

It is not clear how long Gardner, 43, and Ray were together, though he posted a loving tribute to the comedian in honor of her 42nd birthday in July 2025.

“Prettier and more graceful than the moon and by far the coolest person I’ve ever met,” he wrote via Instagram alongside a carousel of sweet photos. “My favorite song in the world is you singing softly in my ear. My favorite color is the gold at the center of your eyes.”

Ray recalled “falling so fast” for Gardner the “second [their] eyes met” while she was “laughing with [her] whole body.”

“I’ve just been falling faster every day. You are the sexiest woman who ever lived, in every single manner of clothing, hair, and old age makeup,” he added. “I’m crushing on you so deep, endlessly. You hold my heart perfectly and love me so proper. You carry the party in your eyes and move like a modern dancer everywhere you go.”

The director concluded, “You are the most genius at making art and surfing the wave with the purest flow I’ve ever seen. The world is a love letter to you. I am your boy forever.”

Prior to her relationship with Ray, Gardner was married to Marvel Comics writer Zeb Wells from 2010 to 2023.

The former SNL cast member opened up about her divorce on “The Liz Moody Podcast” in 2024, indicating that Wells, 49, “will always be in [her] life and it will transform in a different way.” (She did not directly reference Wells by name.)

Acknowledging that their breakup was “very painful and uncomfortable,” she noted, “I will say the biggest thing I learned in that time is lean on the women in your life and your girlfriend.”

“I already had amazing friends and family, but I will just say that women showed up in such an incredible way and showed me that in future relationships, my romantic partner, I learned does not need to be my emotional rock,” Gardner added.

#3610. Avril Lavigne Welcomes Her First Child At Age 42

Avril Lavigne is now a mom. The 42-year-old Canadian might count songs like "Here's to Never Growing Up" among her hits, but in news posted to Instagram Friday, Avril Lavigne revealed a very grown-up milestone.

Beneath a carousel of three black-and-white photos, Lavigne wrote “Our Mini Fucking Princess has arrived,” followed by emojis depicting a baby bottle, a crown, and a pink heart and bow. One photo shows Lavigne cradling an infant dressed in an animal-print onesie and matching headband, while another shows three pairs of Vans on a skateboard. No other details, including information on the baby's name or if Lavigne has a co-parent, were provided.

Avril Lavigne at the Viper Room in the early 2000s.

A spokesperson for the singer told People that “Avril has been enjoying time with her family while working on her new album and wants to thank the fans for all of their love!”

Lavigne has been married twice: once to Canadian guitarist Deryck Whibley and then to Chad Kroeger, the Canadian frontman of the band Nickelback. That latter partnership ended in 2018, but in 2022 she almost tied the knot a third time, with rapper Mod Sun. That relationship ended in 2023.

Mod Sun and Avril Lavigne attend the 2022 MTV Video Music Awards on August 28, 2022

One constant in Lavigne's life has been strong bond she shares with her parents. When, in May 2025, she brought her mother on stage at Madison Square Garden, she wrote on social media: “Ever since I was a little girl, both my mom and dad saw something in me and encouraged me to practice very hard and pursue my dream of becoming a singer/ musician. They made a lot of sacrifices for me and I could not be where I am today without them.”

Continuing, she wrote, “I am grateful to both my parents. Thank you for everything, I love you both!”

Lavigne was still a teenager when her parents allowed her to leave high school to pursue her dream, and her debut at age 17 was a smash hit. Her success continued with singles including 2002's chart-topper “Complicated" and 2021 song “Bite Me.”

Though Friday's announcement was a surprise to most, Lavigne has never been quiet about her desire to become a mom when the time is right. Speaking with E! News in 2013, she laid out her plan: "I want one or two [kids], but not right now," the then-29-year old said. "Like, in the future. Eventually."

#3609. Xbox Project Helix Is A Console That Plays PC Games, Not The Other Way Around

Xbox has revealed more details about its next-gen device, Project Helix, describing it as a "console capable of playing games from your PC."

Prominently featured in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine, VP of next-gen Jason Ronald said the Xbox Series X|S successor is designed to build on the successes — and hard lessons — of previous Xbox generations, with fewer barriers to play.  "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine--one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," Ronald said. "My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games."

Ronald added that the Project Helix family of devices isn't purely focused on traditional next-gen themes like better graphics, but on thinking ahead to create "innovative" experiences. "We don't think the next generation is defined by 8K, or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metrics--it's really about gameplay innovation," Ronald explained. "We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."

Project Helix will also let "hardcore" gamers customize their gaming experience, but how much will all of this cost? Xbox isn't revealing a ballpark figure for Project Helix yet, but Ronald did mention the company is aiming to balance state-of-the-art gaming with an "affordable" price tag. Game preservation will also play a key role, letting users bring their Xbox library with them, and Ronald teased Project Helix as a brand that spans multiple facets of gaming, from living room experiences to handheld sessions and cloud streaming. As a sign of things to come, the Xbox mode on the recently released ROG Xbox Ally was mentioned as the direction the gaming division is headed.

The news on Project Helix comes at a time when Xbox has had several highs and lows throughout 2026. This year saw several first-party games release and earn plenty of acclaim, while the anniversary celebrations included a special-edition Xbox Series X that few people could get their hands on — for retail price, that is. At the same time, the rise of Asha Sharma as Xbox CEO has seen scores of jobs and studios slashed from the Xbox family as the company undergoes a "reset" aimed at making it more profitable.

#3608. Sony Defeats $2.6 Billion Class-Action Lawsuit Over Claimed PlayStation Store Monopoly

Since 2022, Sony has been facing the British equivalent of a class action lawsuit that could have cost the company as much as $2.6 billion had it lost. It, however, did not. As reported byÂ The Game Business, the lawsuit brought by consumer advocate Alex Neill claimed that Sony was operating a “near monopoly” via the PlayStation Store, and sued the Japanese company on behalf of nine million UK PlayStation owners, but today the claims were rejected, and the case has been dismissed.

The reported financial goal of the lawsuit has wildly swung about over the years, cited as $5.9 billion in 2022, then $7.9 billion by 2023, and then down to $2.6 billion in May of this year. Whatever the number, the case being made was that by not allowing third-party stores to sell digital PlayStation games, Sony effectively has a monopoly from which it extracts 30 percent of every sale. This, said Neill and the PlayStation You Owe Us campaign, was an “abuse” of Sony’s “dominant position,” forcing customers to pay “too much for digital games and in-game content purchased through the PlayStation Store.”

A previous attempt to have the case thrown out was rejected in 2023, and then things looked far worse for Sony when it lost a very similar case in California in May of this year, to the tune of $7.8 billion. And there’s the rather pertinent point that Sony absolutely does dominate sales of digital games on PlayStation, and that’s only going to get a whole lot worse as the megacorp phases out physical media entirely. Yet, following May’s trial, London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal has rejected the argument and ruled that, as reported by TGB, “the claim failed to establish that PlayStation infringed competition law.”

The argument against a monopoly was based on the wider competition of Xbox, Nintendo, and PC, alongside the (current) option to buy physical versions of games. Allowing third-party stores onto the PlayStation could, the court said, impact security, which interestingly was the failed argument Google made in its battle against Epic. The tribunal also said Neill had failed to prove that Sony’s profits were “excessive,” likely given that 30 percent cuts are pretty much an industry standard.

However, Sony is still facing similar cases in Holland, Portugal, and Mexico, and it seems they could fall either way.

#3606. Los Javis Are “Living a Dream” As La Bola Negra with Penélope Cruz, Guitarricadelafuente, and Miguel Bernardeau Collects Honors

While La Bola Negra continues to amass various accolades and early awards, like the Best Director award at this year's Cannes Film Festival and the Audience Award at the Toronto International Film Festival, directors Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo are extra grateful and overwhelmed by the film's reception and success in their home country of Spain.

Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

“You can't plan the miracle,” Calvo said during a panel conversation moderated by Ricky Martin at the inaugural Vanity Fair Screening Room at LACMA on Friday. “We’ve done many projects and each one of them has, they've all been good, but you never know when it's going to happen. And with La Bola Negra, we thought it was a very specific story and we thought that our audience was going to like it, but we never knew it was going to hit everyone. I think it's about to become the second highest grossing movie in the history of Spain. For me, the most beautiful part of it is the videos of the people hugging after the screenings, giving tissues to each other, comforting each other.”

La Bola Negra follows several gay men whose lives are bound together by their identities, love and loss, and the looming presence of the Spanish Civil War. The acclaimed Spanish language drama spans nearly a century and stars Miguel Bernardeau, Álvaro Lafuente Calvo (the singer known as Guitarricadelafuente) in his first major acting role, Carlos Gonzalez, Milo Quifes and Penélope Cruz.

Guitarricadelafuente at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

Following an exclusive screening of the film on Friday, Martin moderated a panel conversation featuring directors Ambrossi and Calvo, and stars Cruz, Guitarricadelafuente and Bernardeau. Calvo said they are all riding high on the positive audience reactions and reception. “Creating this sense of community and hearing people saying, ‘This movie changed me. It really made me understand things about me.’ The power that art has, we forget it, but then this happens and … the rest is a dream. The rest we're living is a dream.”

The directors also consider having Cruz play a small but pivotal role in the film to be part of their living a dream. When Martin asked Cruz how her longstanding allyship to the LGBTQ+ community shaped her intention or performance, she said, “I don't even ask myself that question because it's such a part of me, of the way that I was raised. My very young parents, my parents had me when they were 21. It was a house where the values were about respect and it was just like breathing. They didn't even have to sit us down and give us a lecture about it, it was the way my family was living by example. And on top of that, then I had my other master Pedro Almodóvar who I've worked with for seven movies. And I always remember growing up thinking, why is he not the president of our country? Because he was huge in a time where his presence was really necessary, not only through his films, but also by the things that he was saying. So I feel like all of that has shaped me.”

Miguel Bernardeau, Guitarricadelafuente, Penélope Cruz, Javier Calvo, Javier Ambrossi and Ricky Martin at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

She continued: “So when I have in my hands the possibility of playing somebody like Nené Romero, that is a reminder that unfortunately not everyone in the world feels the way we feel about everyone having a right for respect, everyone having a right to be themselves.”

Ricky Martin at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

For Martin, a Bola Negra superfan who admitted he was nervous to be asking questions instead of answering them, the actor and musician said he found out about his hosting opportunity only the day before and despite the nerves couldn't pass up the opportunity to help celebrate the film.

“I usually answer the questions, I never ask the questions, but I needed to be here,” he told the audience. “I saw this film and for a while I was in the movie. I was really touched. The acting, the way it was written, people are crying because that's just the way it is, [really moving].”

#3603. Xbox Is Looking For Smarter Ways To Stop Its Next Console From Costing A Fortune

No one knows yet exactly what the next-gen Xbox console, Project Helix, will be, but most people are convinced it won't be cheap. The ongoing memory shortage has driven current-gen console prices skyward since 2024, with the Xbox Series X rising from $500 in 2020 to $800 in 2026. Project Helix is projected to cost as much as $1,800 at launch, but Microsoft aims to keep the price down when it eventually releases the device.

According to VP of next-gen Jason Ronald, techniques like neural rendering could help manage costs. "It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it's also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable," Ronald said in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine. "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years."

In a nutshell, neural rendering uses AI to predict and generate high-quality video game frames while using only a portion of hardware power, similar to upscaling technoligies like PSSR, DLSS, and FSR. This could enable next-generation visual leaps while keeping the console accessible and reasonably priced for consumers. The other benefit is that the AI software models can improve over time through updates, as console hardware remains fixed over its lifespan, hence Ronald's quote about improvements reaching Project Helix over a few years into its run.

It remains to be seen how these breakthroughs will be spread across Project Helix, which Ronald teased as a family of devices that can address home, mobile, and cloud gaming needs. Xbox suggesting that it's working smarter to deliver an affordable gaming experience is an idea that Shawn Layden touched on recently, as the former PlayStation boss spoke about how Sony should be less concerned with chasing improved graphics and rather focus on making a cheaper PS5-level console instead.

Meanwhile, Sony is squeezing more life out of the PS5 generation with AI-guided upscaling technology, and the base model PS5 got its own version of this in the form of Quick Spectral Super Resolution. Originally available for only two games, QSSR is coming to more titles in the future, like Control Resonant, Arc Raiders, and No Man's Sky.

The next big question on a lot of James Bond fans' minds, now that Robert Pattinson has been named the next Bond, is who will play the next “Bond Girl”? Though the rumors and anticipation haven’t quite reached the fevered pitch that the Bond casting rumors did, there is still plenty of speculation out there. My feeling on it is that it could be one of the frontrunners, like Sydney Sweeney or Margaret Qualley, but it’s just as likely to be a name we’ve not heard yet. With all that said, let’s get into some of the rumors.

Looking at the prediction markets like Kalshi, the leader right now to be the next Bond Girl is Margaret Qualley in the yet-untitled Bond 26. As of today, she’s sitting at about 60% odds to nab the role. This is after coming on strong in recent weeks, after Sydney Sweeney had been the favorite for months. Sweeney’s odds have dropped to about 10% recently, but I still think she should be considered a serious contender, given her trajectory over the last few years.

The only other actresses above 20% are Ana Taylor-Joy (25%) and Florence Pugh (20%). These rumors make a lot of sense, actually. Like Pattinson, they have both worked with Bond 26 director Denis Villeneuve in the Dune series. Until just recently, Pugh wasn’t among the speculation, really, but she’s a big part of the upcoming Dune: Part III, so perhaps Villeneuve may keep the band together.

That goes for Zendaya, too, who is currently sitting at 17% on Kalshi, but she seems less likely to me. Other names who appear on the list include Daisy Edgar-Jones, Jodie Comer, Emma Mackey, Alicia Vikander, and Vanessa Kirby. The final name on the current list is also an interesting one: Ana de Armas. She worked with Villeneuve on Blade Runner 2049, and she’s been in a James Bond movie before, playing a fellow spy in No Time to Die. That could make for an interesting dynamic.

So those are the top names on the prediction markets, but could it be someone else completely? Possible. These are pure speculation on my part, but how about Inde Navarrette? Her star is on the rise after her excellent performance in the surprise smash Obsession earlier in the 2026 movie schedule. She’s definitely someone to watch and could definitely draw some attention from the Bond producers, though she is scheduled to play Rogue in the 2028 X-Men movie, so she might not be available.

What about Jenna Ortega? She’s quickly becoming one of the biggest stars in the world (despite a recent stumble with Klara and the Sun) with her roles in Wednesday and the Scream franchise and could be a great fit for the role. Chloë Grace Moretz, someone else who has played Wednesday Addams, is another possibility. Someone like Sadie Sink would make a great Bond Girl, too. Though, like Navarrette, she may be tied up in the MCU franchise for the foreseeable future.

So what does the future hold? Let the speculation begin!

Zara Tindall didn’t let the cold snap stop her from enjoying a day at the races on Friday. Accompanied by her close friend Dolly Maude and country-set favorite fashion designer Jade Holland Cooper, the daughter of Princess Anne and granddaughter of Queen Elizabeth II brought a dash of regal glamour to the proceedings following a glitzy night out in support of Prince William.

And while the sun may have been out, the Olympic equestrian still needed to wrap up against the chill. Tindall opted for a long plaid coat from L'Agence, a Purdey roll-neck jumper in brown, and a fascinator from Sally-Ann Provan. She accessorized with a new pair of Hector Lion earrings, a new Fairfax & Favor handbag, and completed the look with leather boots, also from Fairfax & Favor.

Zara Tindall joined in the action at Cheltenham Racecourse on Friday

Dolly, on the other hand, wore an avant-garde feather coat with knee-high boots and what looked to be a pair of emerald tights.

The pair were last spotted together in October, when they attended the William Hill Showcase Meeting at Cheltenham, but their friendship goes way back. Long considered Zara’s best friend, Dolly became Princess Anne’s lady-in-waiting in 2024. Jade Holland Cooper and Zara Tindall on day one of The November Meeting at Cheltenham racecourse

Having worked as a maternity practitioner in the NHS in Gloucestershire for 13 years, Dolly also did some philanthropic work using her maternity expertise, working in the unit of a hospital in Kambia, Sierra Leone for a month in 2013. At Kambia, she taught staff basic nursing skills. Before qualifying as a nurse, Dolly studied fashion and Cordon Bleu cookery at Eastbourne College of Food and Fashion, graduating in 1989.

Zara Tindall also braved the stormy weather for a day at Cheltenham with Dolly in October

Dolly Maude is known for her love of horses—a passion she shares with Zara and Princess Anne—and is often seen in Ascot’s royal box alongside the Princess Royal. The royal confidant has four children with her husband Chris: Billy, who studied at Swansea University; Nell, who trained at the Central School of Ballet; a keen skier, Ted; and Mary.

Princess Anne's daughter wrapped up in a warm plaid coat and roll-neck jumper

While much of Zara Tindall’s time this season has been spent touring the country’s most prestigious racing meets, she still found time to support her cousin, Prince William, at one of his treasured annual traditions. The Prince of Wales helped to put together the Tusk Conservation Awards at Raffles on Wednesday night and invited Zara to the celebration of conservation, alongside Lady Amelia and Lady Eliza Spencer and the Marchioness of Bath.

Dolly Maud made her debut as lady-in-waiting for the Princess Royal at the 2024 Commonwealth Day Service in March

Zara showcased her characteristically elegant style, donning a sapphire-blue Rebecca Vallance short-sleeved midi number, aptly named the “Crown Jewel” dress, which she paired with Kiki McDonough earrings. It is not the first time that the royal has lent her support to Prince William’s second-longest patronage: she also joined the crowd at the Tusk Awards in 2025, donning Rebecca Vallance again, and tearing up at the Prince of Wales’ speech in honor of those who gave their lives as rangers.

Anyone planning to eat fried food and play video games should be mindful of what might happen to their controller ... unless you got your hands on the limited-edition "greaseproof" controller that Microsoft put out years ago. Audra McDonald spoke about this moment of representation.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Spoilers ahead for the most recent episode of The Gilded Age.

Shortly after its debut, Julian Fellowes' The Gilded Age joined the ranks of HBO shows that got the world talking. The show's fourth season began a few weeks ago on the network (and streaming with a HBO Max subscription), and there have already been a number of memorable moments. The third episode featured Peggy's marriage to Dr. William Kirkland, and Audra McDonald as well as executive producer Erica Armstrong Dunbar spoke about the importance of having the newlyweds jump the broom onscreen.

While The Gilded Age fans are concerned over Marian and Larry, Peggy and William have officially tied the knot. In a conversation with People, McDonald spoke said "it meant everything" for the series to show the new pair jumping the broom onscreen, highlighting similar opinions to her character Dorothy. In the Broadway legend's words:

We’re honoring those traditions. We’re celebrating those traditions. We are shouting into the world who we are. I think that’s why it was important to Dorothy and Arthur [John Douglas Thompson], and especially because that was their broom, the one that they jumped over.

For those unfamiliar, jumping the broom is a wedding ceremony that goes back antebellum period in the United States. While enslaved people couldn't legally get married, couples would jump over a broom together to symbolize their union. It's remained a tradition for Black Americans in the years that followed, continuing to this day.

Jumping the broom became a point of contention leading up to Peggy's wedding, with her mother-in-law Elizabeth Kirkland (Phylicia Rashad) protesting its place in high society. Later in the same interview, Audra McDonald spoke more about why Dorothy and the entire Scott family was so passionate about it being included in the wedding ceremony, offering:

[It meant that] our family is going to continue. That’s another thing. We didn’t know about the Scotts, how we were going to make it, especially with all the trauma that they went through, that we’re going to continue as a unified family. Now we have the possibility of future generations.

Indeed, the Scott family has come a long way since Season 1 of The Gilded Age. Despite trauma and issues, Peggy and her parents have found their way back to each other throughout the last three seasons. It was actually the same broom that Dorothy and Arthur jumped over before they were able to legally marry, making Peggy's use of the ceremony a full circle moment for the entire family.

In the official Gilded Age podcast, Dr. Erica Armstrong Dunbar spoke about having Peggy and her husband jump the broom in Episode 4. As she put it:

We had lots of conversation about jumping the broom. Julian Fellowes was very invested in the idea of showing what's become a very kind of popular connection to the past. And if you go to Black weddings today people jump the broom. I jumped the broom at my own wedding. But I'm a historian. And so we had lots of conversations because in the 1880s nobody's really jumping the broom.

Season 4 of The Gilded Age has been changing the dynamics of various characters, and Peggy is no exception. On top of being published writer, she's now a married woman in good standing with society. Having her jump the broom honored the character's history, and also had the opportunity to educate fans who might not know about this tradition. As she the show's EP continued:

Arthur, who was enslaved and we established that since Season 1, and Dorothy did jump over a broom in their wedding. So there's a world in which it could have been passed down to Peggy. And knowing who Peggy is, of course she would want to honor that tradition no matter the discomfort that it gave to her soon-to-be in-laws... It was for the Kirklands a reminder of slavery that they found undignified and unwilling to have in the wedding of their son.

Ultimately the Kirklands ended up relenting, and Peggy and William jumping in the broom in a beautifully shot sequence of their nuptials. We'll just have to wait and see how Peggy's relationship with her in-laws changes now that they're officially family.

New episodes of The Gilded Age air Sundays on HBO as part of the 2026 TV schedule. The season's drama is heating up, and I can't wait to see what comes next for this ensemble cast.

#3598. We Got A Grand Theft At Disney World Before GTA 6

The "We got X before GTA 6" meme continues as a Grand Theft has been reported at Walt Disney World's Epcot theme park just days before Rockstar's open-world crime game releases, and the meme comes to an end.

The Walt Disney World: Active Calls account, which tracks police reports in the Disney World area, said a Grand Theft call at Epcot came in at 9:52 PM on November 14.

There are no further details to go on here, but Grand Theft, known as Grand Larceny in some states, involves stealing something valuable. Epcot and Disney in general has lots of items that would be considered valuable.

This is the closest that Disney World might come to GTA 6, as Rockstar already confirmed that GTA 6 won't have its own version of the park. That makes sense, too, considering Walt Disney World is located in Orlando and GTA 6 takes place in its own version of Miami, which is more than 200 miles away.

Calls for Grand Theft are not uncommon at Disney World. In October 2026 alone, the County Sheriff's Office received at least seven Grand Theft calls.

One of the most infamous heists at Walt Disney World took place at Epcot. In 2018, thieves nabbed the multi-hundred-pound Buzzy animatronic from the Cranium Command attraction, which was housed at Epcot's shuttered Wonders of Life pavilion.

It has never been recovered. A documentary, Stolen Kingdom, was released in 2025, chronicling the heist and the wider black market for Disney props.

More recently, the Paddlefish restaurant at the Disney World entertainment district, Disney Springs, was robbed by someone who swam up to the waterside restaurant in frogman gear, forced two workers into a corner, obscured the security camera with foam, and made off with cash. This case has not been solved.

In other Disney news, the entertainment giant is teasing "major" announcements for The Game Awards next month. As for GTA 6, the game finally releases on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

The "We got X before GTA 6" memes have been among the most popular and hilarious over the years as fans waited and waited for the game to release. Even Take-Two's own CEO, Strauss Zelnick, is aware of the memes.

#3597. As Hollywood Battles AI, Pedro Pascal Says Making Behemoth! Filled Him with “a Tremendous Amount of Hope”

Pedro Pascal says that the character he plays in Behemoth!, his first leading film role, is the “closest thing to me that I’ve ever done.” And because of this, “the experience on set felt surreal in a sort of physically tangible way,” Pascal told the audience during a Q&A at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room at LACMA on Saturday.

Directed by Tony Gilroy, Behemoth! tells the story of Alex, a prodigal cellist who returns to Los Angeles and the world of Hollywood film scoring after decades performing symphonic work around the country.

“The mixing of my own life and this person's life, I've lived a very nomadic one. Don't ask me where home is. And so that felt like it was crossing personal lines for me in a way,” he continued during a post-screening discussion about the film, which featured Pascal and writer-director Tony Gilroy, moderated by VF's West Coast Editor John Ross.

Tony Gilroy and Pedro Pascal  at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

But according to Gilroy, their collaboration on the film almost didn't happen, thanks to an alleged missed connection at a Star Wars event.

“We went to a Star Wars convention in Tokyo where we took Andor,” recalled Gilroy. “There was this big Disney dinner so all the Star Wars people are there and [Pascal] was kind of busy and flighty.”

“I had the flu! I flew from London to Tokyo!” Pascal countered.

Gilroy continued: “He seemed like he was so hip that he didn't come to the dinner. I thought, 'Oh he's got such a great thing going on he's going to some better party; he's not going to a boring dinner.'”

As the audience laughed, Pascal was quick to set the record straight: “I cannot believe that you thought that I ditched that dinner. I was doing re-shoots of Fantastic Four!” he said. “They flew me to Tokyo that night and flew me back and I was on a set. [Turns toward the audience] Can you believe this?”

“Oh my God. I'm calling Kathy Kennedy [the President of Lucasfilm] right away,” Gilroy joked.

Luckily, the moviemaking stars (and schedules) aligned and the pair was able to make their personal, moving film with Pascal serving as Gilroy's “exclamation point. He has all the sadness and all the covering that this character needs to have and the nomadic life.”

Pedro Pascal, Tony Gilroy and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Pascal and Gilroy formed a genuine bond and are very comfortable making playful jabs at each other, keeping things light but also expressing their gratitude for being able to make Behemoth! their way, in Los Angeles, where the film and television industry has been struggling to regain a foothold. Despite the challenges, past and present, they are holding out hope for human-made storytelling to foster further human connection.

“People's natural resistance to the robot takeover is clear,” said Gilroy when asked about the rise of AI. “I don't know what's going to happen. I really don't. The music scene out here is the coral reef of what's happened. It's been dying out here for the last 15 years… It's grooving a little bit now. I think people want humans. I don't know what's going to come back, but this is this incredibly humanizing element of movies that's happened. Can it be replaced by AI? Probably, quite shockingly, simply. There's probably an emotional amplitude knob on some f—ing algorithm, but this movie is organic.”

Pedro Pascal and Tony Gilroy  at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Pascal walked away from Behemoth! feeling optimistic. “The experience of shooting this movie definitely injected me with a tremendous amount of hope,” he said. “We weren't making money on this movie. Nobody was. And you had the most expensive people involved in this film because of their talent and their experience. So there was just this purity of love in the work from every single department, and that was incredibly contagious. And it was primarily locations, and so Los Angeles was just constantly revealing itself in all of these magical ways because we were so location-based. I had shot a series in Colombia for three seasons, and I would argue that the primary character of that series, Narcos, was shooting it in the country of Colombia because there was only one way of capturing that energy and that physical story. And LA did that as well. And then it's so tender. I think the story is incredibly tender. Would you ever expect it from this guy [gestures to Gilroy]?”

“Oh my God. What a cold, weird thing to say,” the director joked.

“There are other movies this year that I think in their own way, movies that I've seen this year that I love so much, that fight for humanity and the storytelling,” Pascal continued. “So I think that there is a sort of pushback that could be really, really thrilling as far as [creativity] is concerned, as far as politics is concerned. We want to be human beings and we want to be connected to one another and we want to tell each other's stories and witness each other's stories and we want to look after each other and all that shit. That's my hope.”

Tony Gilroy at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Gilroy had another suggestion: “Blow up the AI centers, man," he joked. “I don't mean to blow them up. I mean blow them up at the voting box. Go and vote and blow them up. Go see the Musk documentary, man. Go see that, watch the whole four hours. I'm pitching my movie [here], but watch that movie.”

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

#3596. Xbox Game Pass Gets Even More Games In November

The second half of November is usually quiet for several reasons when it comes to new game releases–and one other big reason–but Xbox Game Pass subscribers can look forward to several new titles to close off the month.

Microsoft has announced a handful of new additions to the Game Pass library, including a kid-friendly game to kick things off and a sneak peek at some sporty fun for the first week of December. These announcements typically come in two waves, with a sneak peek split between them, so this list isn't complete yet.

As soon as the rest of the lineup is announced, we’ll update this post with a closer look at what you can download and play soon.

Ideal for younger members of the family who definitely shouldn't be playing GTA 6 right now, this family-friendly game revolves around the PAW Patrol working together to round up lost and scared dinosaurs. November 17

#3595. Hayden Panettiere's Mom Reveals Why She Didn't Attend Daughter's Funeral

Hayden Panettiere‘s mother, Lesley R. Vogel, is breaking her silence about why she did not attend her late daughter’s celebration of life in September.

“I just didn’t want to rock the boat; it was probably for the best,” Vogel, 70, revealed during the Monday, November 16, Inside Edition episode.

It was previously reported that Panettiere’s Nashville costars Connie Britton and Charles Esten, Evan Ross and Ruby Rose were among the 80 mourners to attend a September 19 private service in Malibu. Both of Hayden’s parents, Vogel and Skip Panettiere, were reportedly invited to the memorial though Vogel chose not to attend.

“I knew that some of the people there wanted to believe I was the horrible mother because Hayden was angry and made statements,” she explained to Inside Edition on Monday.

Vogel claimed that she’d last spoken to Hayden in “September [or] October of 2025,” adding of their notoriously complicated relationship, “It was a roller coaster ride, for sure.”

“She was very happy and we did spend a tremendous amount of time together up until the age of about 16, and then once she became the face of this major hit TV series Heroes, that’s when things started to change,” she alleged.

The Nashville star exclusively opened up to Us about where she stood with Vogel in 2025, revealing that they did not “have a relationship” at the time.

“That doesn’t mean that I don’t leave the door open for the opportunity to present itself one day,” she added. “It’s hard for me to say, but I’ve chosen to be brutally honest. So that’s the honest truth of it.”

Hayden acknowledged that some of the strain came from Vogel managing her early career as a child star before the two cut professional ties when she was 19.

“It’s so ingrained in me to be a people pleaser. I went on set, and it was all about being professional, nailing it and always hitting my mark. I had to be perfect. It was nice to hear positive feedback from people like the directors or producers, but without [my mom’s], nothing else mattered,” Panettiere told Us in May. “I felt like I had an identity crisis at 12 years old. I didn’t know who I was.”

Hayden was found unresponsive at an apartment in Greenville, South Carolina, in August, with investigators later determining that her death was accidental and caused by “toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol, and Quetiapine.”

Following her daughter’s death, Vogel told the Daily Mail in August that she was “not abusive by any stretch of the imagination” while managing Hayden’s career.

“I think that Hayden put a pressure on herself,” Vogel argued. “I know that she has mentioned, you know, [that she] ‘always had to please Mom,’ or make sure it was, you know, I succeeded or whatever. I didn’t put that on her. I think she put that on herself.”

Hayden shot her first commercial just three months after Vogel signed her up with the famed Wilhelmina modeling agency at 8 months old. She landed her first recurring TV role as Sarah Roberts on One Life to Live at age 5, ultimately appearing on the soap from 1994 to 1997.

Before Hayden’s death, Vogel’s son, Jansen Panettiere, died at age 28 in February 2023 from “cardiomegaly (enlarged heart), coupled with aortic valve complications,” per a family statement.

#3594. Shooting Suspect In Custody After Opening Fire Near Xbox Dev’s Studio

A drive-by shooting in Southern California ended with no injuries and an arrest after the gunman reportedly opened fire near a business and office campus that houses Xbox subsidiary InXile Entertainment.

According to Aftermath and local affiliate KTLA5, the shooting occurred on November 11 at an office building on the former Marine Corps Air Station in Tustin, California. The police department posted on Facebook that, after uncovering "multiple shell casings in the area," local detectives worked "around the clock" to locate the suspect.

Sergeant Christopher Peterson told Aftermath on November 13 that although the investigation is still ongoing, an unnamed suspect had been apprehended "less than 48 hours" after the shooting.

"Officers got there [on November 11]," Sergeant Peterson said. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."

An InXile Entertainment spokesperson corroborated the incident with Aftermath, expressing relief about the situation.

"We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office,” the spokesperson said. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."

Founded in 2002, InXile Entertainment has been under the Xbox Game Studios umbrella since 2018. Since its founding, the studio has developed several games, from the 2004 ARPG The Bard's Tale to the 2011 action-adventure Hunted: The Demon's Forge to the 2014 post-apocalyptic RPG Wasteland 2. Currently, the team is working on Clockwork Revolution, a steampunk ARPG not too dissimilar from immersive sims like BioShock and Dishonored. It has no release date right now, but InXile Entertainment is targeting a 2027 window for PC and Xbox Series X|S.

Another storied CBS News program is now making headlines.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Bari Weiss’ tenure as the editor-in-chief of CBS News has sparked a myriad of responses from media pundits and the general public, who’ve taken issue with the organization’s content. While Weiss has received praise in some circles, she’s also been critiqued for some of her decisions, including those made in regard to 60 Minutes. Even now, some continue to chastise her editorial and staffing choices for the news magazine show. All the while, it seems Weiss is embroiled in some reported drama involving another news program.

Just recently, Weiss was at the center of a report involving Face the Nation, one of CBS News’ key political programs. According to this update, Weiss apparently planned to part ways with the aforementioned show’s moderator, Margaret Brennan. The media newsletter Status (via The New York Post) didn’t specify why Weiss opted to retain Brennan. At this point, Brennan has headlined FTN since 2018 and, in addition to that she serves as the network’s chief of foreign affairs and fills in as an anchor on CBS Evening News.

Although Brennan is still with the show, it just lost two key members of its team. Senior executive producer Mary Hager recently announced that she would depart CBS News after 25 years with the network. Another key detail about this move is that since 2022, Hager has served as the executive director of politics for the Eye Network and has overseen its Washington Bureau. FTN executive producer Anne Hsu is leaving the show but, unlike Hager, she’ll remain with CBS and will head up its Hong Kong bureau.

These major exits mark the end of another era for Face the Nation, which debuted back in 1954 and, as of right now, it’s unclear just how Weiss will proceed in regard to filling those posts. With this, the Free Press founder finds herself in another staffing situation just months after her overhaul of 60 Minutes. And that series of personnel changes is still being discussed as part of the backlash that 60 has received as of late.

Ex-60 Minutes EP On His Biggest Concerns Amid Bari Weiss’ Leadership: ‘That Would Have Freaked Me Out’

Earlier this year, Anderson Cooper exited his correspondent post at 60 Minutes after nearly two decades, citing a desire to have more time to spend with his loved ones. It was subsequently reported, however, that Cooper’s departure was partially due to disagreements with Weiss. Shortly after Cooper’s move, Weiss and series EP Nick Bilton fired correspondents Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi along with former EP Tanya Simon and several others. Correspondent Scott Pelley was also fired days later after reportedly accusing Weiss of “murdering” the show.

In the aftermath, Weiss brought in a roster of new talent to join series veterans Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker and Jon Wertheim. Pundits like Ross Douthat, Ariel Levy and Sir Trevor Phillips were brought in to fill out the staff. All the while, Weiss continues to receive backlash for those staffing changes, and she’s also been on the receiving end of news bias allegations (which she’s denied). Additionally, 60’s low ratings amid Season 59 have also been a point of contention among critics.

Bari Weiss addressed the 60 Minutes concerns just weeks ago and claimed the show had been doing “tremendously well.” Several staffers including Tony Dokoupil and Norah O’Donnell have also defended Weiss against backlash. In terms of Face the Nation, it’ll be interesting to see how Weiss plans to tap for those big producer jobs. Time will also tell whether Weiss chooses to revisit her reported plan to cut ties with Margaret Brennan.

#3592. NBA 2K27’s GTA 6 Crossover Includes A Whole GTA-Inspired Limited Edition Of The Game

Ahead of the GTA 6 release this week, publisher Take-Two Interactive and 2K Sports have announced an NBA 2K27 crossover with the game. Starting November 27, Vice City will take over the digital basketball courts, and a special-edition NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition will also be released to promote GTA 6.

The $80 digital-only NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition features Miami Heat player Bam Adebayo on the cover, and for that GTA 6 touch, the art also includes the signature Vice City neon glow. This is something of a first for Take-Two Interactive--and possibly, the rest of the industry--as releasing a special edition of a game that promotes another game isn't something that we've seen before. This version also includes bonus Vice City-themed content and several benefits for GTA+ subscribers.

For Season 3 of NBA 2K27's live-service league, Vice City-themed content and rewards across The City social hub and MyTeam mode will be available to unlock. This three-week promotion will include bonuses and access for GTA+ Members, and Take-Two says players can expect themed apparel, including Vice City and Los Santos jerseys, Burger Shot and Cluckin' Bell Employee Outfits, and more.

Vice City-themed limited-time events will run throughout the season, with players competing in Conquer Leonida and Vice Run. Wednesdays will offer a chance to earn extra reputation by wearing Rockstar Games collaboration gear in Wear & Earn events, and one of the new modes is Neon vs. Noir, a 5v5 full-court clash pitting a Vice City team against a Los Santos lineup. MyTeam will also feature Vice City-themed cards, a powerful new Premier Exchange card, and limited-time modes.

The new gear will cost you some bucks, as the Season 3 Pro Pass--which offers access to the premium track with Vice City rewards like the Burger Shot gear, Cluckin' Bell outfit, Cactus Jack jersey, and Macca the Gator--will cost $10. The Hall of Fame Pass, which includes everything from the Pro Pass, 10 instant Level Skips, an extra 15% XP booster, and 15,000 VC, is priced at $20, and to get all the GTA-themed cosmetics, you have to grind through the 40-level season track. If you purchase the Vice City edition, the Season 3 Pro Pass is bundled with your copy.

GTA+ members on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S can also play the standard edition of NBA 2K27 for free from November 27 to January 15, 2027. If they like what they see, they'll get 20% off the game if they choose to purchase. GTA 6 preorders also include a one-month trial of GTA+.

Finally, GTA+ members can also download a Vice City bonus content pack featuring a Vice City-styled blue boat hat and oversized T-shirt, 30 skill boosts for five games, and 15 Gatorade boosts for five games.

GTA 6 marketing has been heating up as the game gets closer to launch, and this isn't the only basketball promotion on the table. For one night only, the NBA's Miami Heat will wear GTA 6-inspired jerseys when they host the Milwaukee Bucks on November 18, and the match will take place on a court inspired by Vice City.

#3591. Kate Middleton Announces First Major Trip Since Her Cancer Diagnosis

In unexpected news, Kensington Palace has just announced that Kate Middleton will accompany Prince William on his upcoming three-day official visit to Mumbai, India. The trip, which commences on Monday, will mark their first joint tour outside the United Kingdom in the past four years and represents a new milestone in Kate Middleton’s gradual return to public duties since she was diagnosed with cancer in early 2024 and began scaling back her official engagements.

Last May, the princess made a brief solo trip to Italy to learn about early childhood development, but this trip to India (a nine-hour flight from London) represents her first long-distance journey and her highest-profile diplomatic engagement since the Caribbean tour she undertook in 2022 and the Earthshot Awards gala she attended in Boston that same year.

"So proud, I'm very, very proud. She's been amazing. She's been through so much in the last couple of years, particularly," William shared on UK radio show Heart Breakfast in May, pleased to see that Kate was “gradually resuming” her travels. Still, the heir to the throne wanted to be cautious and warned that these visits are very taxing. "Away trips like that take a lot out of you," he explained. "So we have to balance that, make sure she's, she's OK and rested, but she's in good form."

The royal couple at the 2022 Earthshot Prize ceremony in Boston, their most recent joint trip abroad to date

The reason for the visit is the sixth edition of the Earthshot Prize, an initiative spearheaded by the heir to the British throne that each year awards one million pounds (about $1,323,249) to five innovative environmental projects and which, after making stops in other cities abroad such as Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro, is now taking place in the country that has produced the most finalists and winners in the competition’s history.

Standout finalists this year include Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, for its fleet of electric motorcycle taxis designed to reduce urban pollution, and Mahila Housing Trust, which installs reflective roofs capable of lowering the temperature inside homes by up to five degrees during extreme heat. The awards ceremony will be held this Tuesday evening at the Jio World Centre in Mumbai and will feature a performance by the band Take That and be attended by celebrities such as actor Rami Malek.

William and Kate during their 2016 visit to the Taj Mahal

Hours before the main event, the Prince and Princess of Wales will also preside over the first edition of the Earthshot Children’s Awards, a competition in which 15,000 schools from 24 Indian states have participated with environmental proposals designed by young people aged 9 to 17. The itinerary also includes a solo appearance by Kate Middleton, meetings with the Bollywood film industry, cricket-related celebrations, and a possible meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

In addition to being a positive sign regarding the princess’s health, this return to India holds strong symbolic significance for the couple, who last visited the country in April 2016. On that occasion, the then-Duke and Duchess of Cambridge visited the Taj Mahal and posed on the same white marble bench where Princess Diana was photographed alone in 1992—an image that has gone down in history as a reflection of the breakdown of her marriage to the now-King Charles III.

#3590. Rockstar Could Have Released GTA 6 Sooner As GTA 5.5, But “You Have To Take Big Swings”

After years of development, multiple delays, and loads of hype, Rockstar Games is finally releasing Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19. What took so long?

According to Rockstar publishing executive Jennifer Kolbe, the team at Rockstar "could have made GTA 5.5, and done it faster." However, "Ultimately, that's not what they wanted," she told The Guardian.

Rockstar boss Rob Nelson, meanwhile, said it was important for the studio to go above and beyond with GTA 6, and that takes time. "You have to take big swings. It can’t be just more of the same," he said.

GTA 6 looks to be a big step up from GTA 5 in a number of ways, including the visuals and technical improvements. Beyond that, the story this time around is a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style narrative about a crime-loving couple--Jason and Lucia. It's also the first time Rockstar is releasing a GTA game with a playable female protagonist.

GTA 6 took so long to come out because Rockstar is seeking "perfection," according to Take-Two. “The team at Rockstar really does seek to do something that’s never been done before. That’s really hard and it takes a long time,” he said.

Rockstar and its owner, Take-Two, stand to benefit greatly from what's expected to be a commercial blockbuster with GTA 6. But could future GTA game releases come at a faster pace? According to Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick, the "nature and velocity" of GTA releases will look "dramatically different" over the next decade, but he didn't share more or commit to any specific timelines.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. People in Australia can attend a funeral at KFC to get the day off work to play it.

GTA 6 unlocks at midnight local time and not simultaneously around the world. This means people in the US will be among the last in the world to get to play.

#3589. Jennifer Lawrence Reunites With 'Hunger Games' Costars at NYC Premiere

The odds are in Us’ favor because Jennifer Lawrence just staged an epic Hunger Games reunion.

The Oscar winner was joined by cast members from the original Hunger Games movies — including Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson — at the New York City premiere of the latest installment in the franchise, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, on Monday, November 16.

Lawrence, 36, who played protagonist Katniss Everdeen, was photographed posing with Hutcherson (who played Peeta Mellark), Harrelson (Haymitch Abernathy) and Elizabeth Banks (Effie Trinket), all of whom first brought Panem, the devious Capitol and heroic District 12 to life in the first four Hunger Games released between 2012 and 2015.

The actress wore a long black coat with a fur trim and floral detailing, in keeping with the movie’s floral promotional artwork.

Joining the family reunion were fellow Hunger Games OGs Willow Shields, who played Katniss’ sister Primrose Everdeen, Jena Malone, who played Johanna Mason, and Amandla Stenberg, who shot to fame with her epic turn as Rue in the first film.

Sadly, there was no Liam Hemsworth — who played Hutcherson’s love rival Gale Hawthorne — on the red carpet to complete this epic reunion.

However, the original cast was joined by the stars of the 2023 prequel The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes: Rachel Zegler, Tom Blyth, and Josh Andrés Rivera.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is a sequel set after the events of The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes and features an all-new cast taking the deadly Hunger Games, led by Mckenna Grace as Maysilee Donner. Joseph Zada plays a younger version of Haymitch, while Elle Fanning takes over the role of a younger version of irreverent stylist Effie Trinket.

Lawrence, Hutcherson and Harrelson will also reprise their respective roles in the movie more than a decade after they were last seen together in The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2.

The actress spoke about her cameo during an October appearance on the “Call Her Daddy” podcast.

“Oh my, unbelievable. It was so crazy because it was the same crew. It was the same camera guys, the same AD who I’ve worked with a million times too, because I love him, and Josh and Woody,” she said. “It was so emotional. It was like, Josh and I didn’t walk to the bathroom without our arms around each other. It was so beautiful.”

As for Harrelson, Lawrence joked, “And Woody obviously came through the window of my hotel room uninvited because it would not be the same. It wouldn’t be the same if he listened to boundaries and used a door.”

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters on Friday, November 20

Danny Kilby showed on Survivor that he had guts after threatening to go to rocks to keep ally Lewis Kelly safe. That was bold, but I never would've imagined he'd be so bold as to execute that exact strategy in a bid to win back all his belongings after Season 51. Unfortunately, his attempt to recreate Storage Wars ended in disaster, but it makes for a hilarious story.

Kilby posted on TikTok about how he moved out of his apartment before Survivor and put all his furniture possessions in a storage locker. Unfortunately, just before leaving, he got a new debit card and realized he forgot to change his billing information with the facility. He said:

So I call them, I spam them, I send emails. There’s no way to get a hold of them on the weekend, and they’re like, oh, you can transfer that details on Monday. Well, I’m like, I’m flying to Fiji before then, so I kind of just rolled the dice and hoped it worked out.

It feels like there were more options on the table than "see what happens," especially since he was staying with his girlfriend, who might've been able to call on his behalf. I guess I shouldn't be surprised that the same guy who gave a guy a case of beer to teach him to swim would have this kind of casual attitude about all of his things.

Kilby goes on Survivor, has a memorable run, gains a love of aquadumping, but ultimately gets voted out next to Kristin Flickinger. Of course, as a part of the jury, he didn't return home until Season 51 was over. Kilby picked up things from there:

I get back to Canada, the first email I read was, hey, we were not able to reach you, so your stuff is going up for auction unless you pay like $2000 in storage fees or whatever. And I went, I can’t afford 2000 bucks right now, so that sucks. But then I was like, wait, what if I bid at an auction on my own stuff? I made my own Storage Wars, you know what I mean?

He had just gotten off of one of the best reality shows, and he wanted to recreate the experience from another show. Granted, the stakes were much higher on Storage Wars, as Kilby planned on trying to outbid competitors on all of his belongings to get a discount.

Unfortunately, he didn't win that Survivor money, and as such, didn't have a ton to spare for the auction. Readers can guess where things are headed, but it's great to hear him recap how it all went down:

It goes up to 400 bucks. And that’s about as much as I had…Part of me had this whole like after Survivor, I’m just like a minimalist now, man. I don’t need stuff. I lost the bid to my own stuff, so somebody named Prince C now owns all of my belongings, my couch, my cheetah painting where he’s dressed as a general. I called him 'General Cheetah.'

The wildest part of this story is that Kilby only had $400 dollars, and according to a photo he shared on TikTok, the winning bid was $442. Couldn't he have found a friend or family member to float him an extra hundred? I can't imagine losing everything in my apartment over less than $50.

Learning this makes me think Kilby had a worse exit from Survivor than both Rhode Island Rob and Brady. How can you go on a reality show to win money and leave with a lot less than you started with? Maybe this story will convince Jeff Probst to bring him back sooner rather than later, so he can get a new couch or a portrait of a cheetah dressed as a general.

Kilby is like the poster boy for Survivor's changes to casting in Season 51, and I'm here for it. Finding people who were capable of risking it all to win was a good call, and it's resulted in some real chaos. So chaotic, in fact, people were discussing eating corn from poop, but fortunately even the wilder players shied away from that.

Catch new episodes of Survivor on CBS on Wednesdays at 8:00 p.m. ET. With these latest eliminations, I'm not sure who will end up winning it all. I will say I have no shortage of favorites, however, and wouldn't mind seeing a few people take home the grand prize.

Mick Joest is a Content Producer for CinemaBlend with his hand in an eclectic mix of television goodness. Star Trek is his main jam, but he also regularly reports on happenings in the world of Star Trek, WWE, Doctor Who, 90 Day Fiancé, Quantum Leap, and Big Brother. He graduated from the University of Southern Indiana with a degree in Journalism and a minor in Radio and Television. He's great at hosting panels and appearing on podcasts if given the chance as well.

#3587. EA Begs You To Not Delete Madden 27 For GTA 6

We all know what's coming: Grand Theft Auto 6. Whether you're ready for it or not, the most anticipated game of the decade is preparing to launch on November 19, and ahead of its release, EA is begging you to please not ditch footballs for guns.

According to Push Square, EA added a "don't delete" pop-up message to Madden NFL 27. The pop-up says there's an update coming to the football simulator on November 17, just before GTA 6 drops.

"Don't delete," the message reads. "[Encrypted Signal] The target is locked. The crew is assembling for a high-stakes run. Await the signal from our insider on 11/17 ... do not leak this transmission!"

In a November 10 post on Madden NFL 27's official X account, EA said that a throwback Madden 97 update is coming on November 18 with old-school playbooks, 16-bit gameplay, and the All '97 Team. Underneath that post, EA had asked that you stick around a little while longer.

This is in reference to the humongous amount of storage space that Rockstar Games' GTA 6 will take up when it launches. Start clearing out your hard drive now because you need at least 212GB of free space to download GTA 6. In comparison, Madden NFL 27 needs approximately 60GB to install the game.

If you're like me and you still have the base PS5, this means you have approximately 667GB of usable space. Sure, you can fit both GTA 6 and Madden NFL 27 on the same console. However, if you have any other recent releases like The Blood of Dawnwalker (~50GB), Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen (~81GB), Phantom Blade Zero (~135GB), and Valor Mortis (~60GB), then you can see how quickly you'll run out of space--especially since you have to leave a little wiggle room for game updates, too. That's not to mention the games dropping in 2027, such as Final Fantasy VII Revelation, which game director Naoki Hamaguchi said could be around 200GB.

EA has recently gone through a restructuring that saw 400 employees across the company get let go and the legendary studio BioWare get shut down. In the midst of this, the publisher reiterated its commitment to the Madden franchise with a new title currently codenamed Project Gridiron. While filled with potential, we do fear that EA's plan for the series may lean into everything that the company itself does wrong.
