#3586. Sam Altman Is “Still Unknowable” to Andrew Garfield, Even After Playing the OpenAI Co-Founder in Artificial

In Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial, the director follows the rise of OpenAI and a few of its pioneers: Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Ilya Sutskever and Mira Murati. The result is one of the most talked-about and timely films of the season.

“The topic is not the artificial intelligence for me, but it's the people who imagined it, who created it, who exploited it and who are still in the mix of doing all these things,” Guadagnino said during a discussion led by VF's Global Editorial Director Mark Guiducci, at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room at LACMA on Saturday. “I was very much into trying to decipher, understand this world of this new generation, let’s say tech bros, that were somehow behaving in a way that was not exactly as you could see the previous generation doing … So it was too attractive not to try to meet these people in the eyes and too attractive not to do so with this incredible group of performers who were going to go and jump the cliff of this.”

Luca Guadagnino and Andrew Garfield at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Guadagnino was joined by cast members Andrew Garfield (who plays Altman), Yura Borisov (who plays Sutskever) and Monica Barbaro (who plays Murati) for a post-screening conversation. The actors were challenged with preparing to play real people who they were not able to interact with ahead of time, instead relying on interviews, video recordings, and other research in order to get into their characters.

Andrew Garfield at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

“[Sam Altman] still is unknowable to me and I'm fascinated by him continuously and exponentially, for here until eternity," Garfield said about OpenAI's co-founder and CEO. “And it's important to try to understand because as Luca said, these are the kids that have the reins of the future and we've somehow allowed them to just hold onto them. And we've kind of given our autonomy over or it's been taken from behind our backs.”

He added: “It's a remarkable thing to have the resilience to go and sleep every night, knowing that you're really doing a lot of damage.”

Barbaro said the fact that Murati is very private helped her understand the former OpenAI CTO. “That is indicative of a kind of behavior and personality type and it pointed me in a certain direction as far as her values were concerned,” she said. “And we also had a lot of wonderful consultants, people who worked with them at OpenAI, but who were no longer with the company, kind of telling us what jokes and things that they would make.”

Yura Borisov at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

For Borisov, he hopes his portrayal does Sutskever justice and that people will want to know or understand him more. “I started to watch videos about him and looked at his social media, trying just to understand what he's talking about in his interviews,” the actor explained. "And step by step, as much as I discovered him, it was more and more scary for me because I started to respect and love him more and more."

Monica Barbaro, Andrew Garfield and Yura Borisov at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

The conversation had its own meta moment of sorts, when Barbaro posed a question to Guiducci about his decision to profile and feature Altman on the cover of Vanity Fair’s New Establishment Issue.

"You faced heat for presenting, maybe some people would say pedestalizing Sam Altman on the cover of Vanity Fair, what is your take on that?" Barbaro asked.

“I think that the magazine is an arena where these things have to play out,” Guiducci said. “It's so interesting to me to...have the [forthcoming] feature about this film in the issue that was preceded by one where I got to ask Sam about it." Guiducci continued: "Something about [taking Sam's] picture makes people feel, ‘Oh, that's the trophy.’ But photojournalism is journalism too. And I want people to be able to look back at the magazine and see a document of the time that we lived in," he said. "And also, if the photo is what helps me get the interview where we get to know more about these people, I'm going to take it.”

Monica Barbaro at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Other panel highlights included the subject of ChatGPT, which only Guadagnino admitted to using occasionally to ask about what’s ok to feed his dogs. He also addressed parting ways with the film's original studio partner Amazon and the fortuitous partnership that emerged with new distributor NEON.

“I think there is some kind of honor in the decision because they could have written off the movie and that's it,” he said about Amazon dropping the film from their slate. “And then they allowed us to find a partner and we found the best partner possible… They really believed in the movie.”

“They really made everything to get us to make the best movie we could,” he continued. "I only have good feelings toward my friends at Amazon. And in a strange way, I kind of understand the decision. Conflict of interest is a big thing.”

Luca Guadagnino at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

#3585. GTA 6 Should Help Boost PS5 And Xbox Sales, But Their Astronomical Prices Could Hurt

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, and it's expected to help boost console sales for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. But the uptick in hardware sales might not be as dramatic as you might think--and there is a good reason why.

According to Circana's Mat Piscatella, there will be "probably" be a boost to PS5 and Xbox Series X|S sales when GTA 6 comes out, but the uptick could be muted due to the recent PS5 and Xbox Series X|S price hikes. Piscatella said anyone who is excited for GTA 6 and needs a new console might think twice when they see how astronomically expensive new consoles have become today.

Historical prices

When GTA 5 launched in 2013, the average price paid for a new PS3 was $252 and the Xbox 360 was $232. Adjusted for inflation, that would be $363 for the PS3 today and $334 for the Xbox 360. Those prices are significantly below the average price of a new PS5 ($646) and Xbox Series X|S ($663) today.

"Not a good thing"

Earlier this year, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick, who oversees the company launching GTA 6, said, "The rising cost of hardware is not a good thing." At the same time, Zelnick isn't worried about the impact on GTA 6, in part because he believes the game is so good that people will find a way to pay for a new console.

 "However, a lower price point for hardware would be a good thing because there’d be more hardware in people’s hands," he said. "Probably the most relevant thing is the world continues to move to open systems, and that will continue.”

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. People in New Zealand get to play first, and if you're planning a trip to the land of Hobbits, here are some tips for safely packing your PS5.

#3583. WoW: Forever’s Dungeons Have Gotten Yet Another Big Change

World of Warcraft: Forever's dungeons have changed once again, with developer Blizzard's most recent adjustment requiring an emergency hotfix to address players' outcry.

Dungeons, specifically how much experience points players earn from them, have been one of Forever's most debated topics going back to the game's beta. Make them too lucrative, and players will just stay inside dungeons instead of questing out in the world. At the same time, Blizzard doesn't want dungeons to be one-time affairs, with players completing all their quests in a single run and never going back.

Blizzard opened a new front in the dungeon wars on November 13, making a change so that nobody in a dungeon group would receive any experience if enemies were considered "trivial" to to any player in the group. The idea behind this appeared to be an effort to prevent high-level players from running low-level ones through dungeons, in the process curtailing players from selling character "boosting" services to lowbies.

Unfortunately, far too many players playing the game normally were caught in the crossfire. Many of Forever's dungeons have double-digit level ranges, meaning even if a player might find enemies early on in the dungeon trivial, enemies and bosses later on won't be. It also created a scenario where players were leveling up mid-dungeon, only to suddenly find themselves fighting trivial enemies and bricking the experience gains for everyone in the group.

As it turns out, committing to a multi-hour adventure, only to suddenly find nobody is earning experience points and everyone is mad at you because you happened to level up, is not a great social experience. Blizzard was at least quick to admit the change "missed the mark" and made adjustments a day later on November 14.

"With hotfixes that are now live, we've just deployed a further change to this restriction, making it so the XP nullification only kicks in when the high-level player is more than 12 levels above the level of the enemies," Blizzard said in a forum post. 

At least judging from forum comments, that seems to be a more reasonable compromise, even if it still does prevent higher-level players from coming to help their lower-level friends.

It's just the latest chapter in what has become one of the biggest ongoing discussions in the Forever community. During the Forever beta, Blizzard made changes to experience earned from dungeon quests, nerfing them significantly. 

Come launch day, it became apparent Forever's dungeons weren't worth running more than once, as after completing quests, experience earned from kills was extremely low. Blizzard agreed, and issued a change on November 8 to increase the amount of kill experience earned in dungeons by 50%. It was a sizable increase, but is still lower than the experience amount players earned from doing dungeons in WoW Classic.

Forever's launch broke WoW concurrent-player records, and after one week of adventuring through Azeroth once more, classic WoW feels fresh again. Despite the record-breaking launch, Blizzard hasn't released official stats, but fansites have already pieced together the game's most popular class, race, and faction.

#3582. Tallulah Willis: I Stayed Out Past My Bedtime to Celebrate My Mom at the Baby2Baby Gala

The whole endeavor began as it usually does, with a search for the perfect dress. Turns out it would be a yellow Carolina Herrera column-shaped confection (if you care), teetering on yellow satin pointed peekaboo-toe platforms, with my first press pass thudding around in my corresponding yellow duchess satin clutch.

Stylist Brad Goreski and his assistant Clarke, who work with my mother, Demi Moore, sourced the ensemble after finding Mom’s beautiful black ruffled two-piece (adorably also Carolina Herrera).

Around 6:50 p.m. on Saturday, my older sisters, Scout (in cocoa-brown beaded Elie Saab) and Rumer (in whimsical archival Vera Wang), florist Eric Buterbaugh, Brad, my mom and I are about to leave her house for the Baby2Baby Gala, an annual fundraiser for the non-profit that dedicated to providing diapers, clothing, and other basic necessities to children and families in need across the country.

Demi is taking photos against a pale brown backdrop when I hear her say, marginally worried, “Yes, the outfit is amazing, but they didn’t give me pockets.” I cannot fault her. A pocket, particularly in an evening gown, creates an entirely different architecture for one’s night.

When we make it to the Pacific Design Center in West Hollywood, Rihanna is blasting and a gorgeous electric General Motors car, part of the silent auction, is parked out front. I’m holding the bottom of my dress to avoid any “yard sales” on the carpeted floor when I hear, “Is it you? I hope it’s you!” It’s my very new, lovely friend Jackie Tohn, whom I met at a Nobody Wants This premiere party.

Inside, beautifully dressed people laugh and chat. I spot Miranda Kerr, who is both a Baby2Baby board member and major donor, and pass Nara Smith leaning over a dolled-up Elsa Hosk while “Espresso” blasts from overhead speakers.

Table 4 is front and center. Some could say the best seats in the house. Fitting, as Baby2Baby is honoring my mother with the Giving Tree Award tonight. The scene around our table is a frenzy of joyful energy. I make a beeline for Paris Hilton to thank her for the facial I received at her spa this week, while Dancing With the Stars alums Rumer and Jenna Dewan immediately pull out their phones to compare pictures of their kids.

Then I spot Sofia Richie Grainge and her husband, Atlantic Records CEO Elliot Grainge. I snake through throngs of elegant people and poke Elliot’s back twice. “Elliot, it’s Tallulah! We went to Wildwood together!” He instantly remembers me. “Tallulah was the cool girl in class,” he tells Sofia. I blush, but don’t feel the need to correct him.

Scout approaches and says, almost incredulously, “Hi, I’m Scout…you guys just signed me at Atlantic Records.” Elliot grabs her shoulders. “We’re so happy to have you. Are you happy with us?” She can’t say “yes” fast enough.

The program begins with Keke Palmer, who completely owns the stage, telling hilarious stories about her son before shifting into heartfelt candor about the gift of watching him grow. Kerry Washington thanks the sponsors and announces Baby2Baby’s new permanent headquarters, “a promise to millions of children. Not just for today, but for decades to come.”

Then Kelly Sawyer Patricof and Norah Weinstein, the organization’s CEOs, come to the stage, sharing the work—no, the magic—they have created over 15 years. Their first gala in 2012 raised $1 million. Last year’s raised $18 million. To date, they’ve distributed an astonishing 850 million essential items to people in need across all 50 states, responded to over 150 disasters, developed their own diaper production line during COVID, and expanded into mental health support for new mothers. The mission remains the same, but the scale is impossible to comprehend.

Now Rumer, Scout, and I are all crying during a short video about two families impacted by Baby2Baby. The feeling is palpable for the rest of the room.

As the live auction begins, I catch my mom discreetly reading over a printout of her speech. I don’t feel nerves coming off her, but a desire to match the elegance and integrity surrounding us.

Andrew Garfield takes the stage and speaks directly to my mom about the woman he knows. “She is a miracle,” he says.

Then it’s Demi’s turn. Holding her gleaming award in two hands, she thanks Andrew for carving out time amid his Artificial press tour. My mother adores Andrew, a feeling shared across our family.

Alone on stage in her Carolina gown (sans pockets), she asks everyone to breathe. “Inhale. Exhale.” That breath, she says, is the relief Baby2Baby provides when a mother no longer has to choose between dinner and diapers. “Your child matters, you matter, and you are not alone.” She leaves us with the idea that the essence of this work is to be remarkably human. Baby to baby, mother to mother, soul to soul.

Then Cardi B takes the stage and the atmosphere shifts with a jolt. Everyone is on their feet dancing. The official after-party begins, but I’m turning back into a pumpkin in towering satin stilettos. It was a remarkably beautiful night, and I’m left with the overwhelming desire to do more—to show up for someone who may not have the ability to show up for themselves or their precious loved ones.

But for this on-scene reporter’s inaugural correspondence, it was ultimately Baby2Baby2Bedtime.

#3581. The Head Of GTA 6’s Parent Company Helped Make One Of The Best Christmas Movies Of All Time

One of the most memorable and beloved Christmas movies is 1990's Home Alone, but it almost didn't happen, and the head of GTA 6's parent company played a role in bringing the movie to market.

Strauss Zelnick, the current CEO of Rockstar Games owner Take-Two, was the president and COO of 20th Century Fox at the time--he was among the youngest-ever Hollywood CEOs at the age of 32.

Warner Bros. was originally backing Home Alone and had actually begun production on the movie until budget concerns prompted the studio to pull the plug. "Four days into production, they shut down the picture and canceled it. That never happens," Zelnick told David Rubenstein.

Fox, under the leadership of chairman Joe Roth and Zelnick as president, swooped in and gave the filmmakers--including director Christopher Columbus and writer John Hughes--the money to make Home Alone.

That turned out to be a fantastic investment for Fox, as Home Alone ranked as one of the top five highest-grossing movies of the year in the US. It grossed more than $476 million globally against a $13 million budget, and it picked up two Oscar nominations. Home Alone also helped launch the career of Macaulay Culkin, and his role of Kevin remains his most memorable part.

So why didn't Zelnick keep making movies?

Zelnick was on top of the world as a film executive after Home Alone. However, he said he saw a bright future in the interactive entertainment business, so he left Fox in 1993 to join Crystal Dynamics where he served as president and CEO.

"I left Fox voluntarily, which no one ever does, to move to Silicon Valley, take a 95% pay cut and become the pre-revenue CEO of a little tiny video game company called Crystal Dynamics in 1993," he said in the Rubenstein interview.

After Crystal Dynamics, Zelnick shifted to the music business in the role of CEO as BMG Entertainment from 1994 to 2000. During that time, BMG started a gaming unit, BMG Interactive, which published the original GTA in 1997.

After that, Zelnick and an investor group took over Take-Two, which was in a tough financial spot at the time and was sued by the US government for accounting fraud.

Since the takeover, Take-Two has thrived. Its share price exploded from about $10 in 2007 to more than $220 today, and Take-Two today has a market cap of over $40 billion. The GTA franchise is a juggernaut at Take-Two, but it actually only accounts for 15% of the company's revenue in a non-release quarter. Take-Two today owns and operates a number of big non-GTA franchises, including NBA 2K, Borderlands, Mafia, BioShock, Civilization, and more.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It's reportedly already sold close to 15 million copies and generated nearly $1.5 billion in revenue.

Below Deck Mediterranean‘s Gael Cameron is speaking out for the first time about Nathan Gallagher‘s alleged abuse that led to his arrest for domestic violence.

Keep scrolling for the biggest revelations:

Flashing back to their first meeting, Cameron clarified that she didn’t immediately plan to explore a romance with Gallagher, saying, “I spent a lot of time where I really did just see him as a friend, and things move very fast on a boat. He would be very playfully flirty with me, and I was very like, ‘Stop it! No, stop.’ Like, I would say it in a funny way, but I’d be like, ‘You need to stop.’ And I would even push him towards some of the other girls.”

Cameron slammed the insinuation that she was unfaithful with Gallagher.

“So there is a scene where we hug and we’re hugging on the stairs and he kisses me on the neck. I was still technically with my partner,” she explained. “And so that’s where people do the whole ‘She cheated. She cheated.’ So technically, in that scene, I didn’t physically cheat. I didn’t actually ever have an intimate relationship with him until after my ex and I had broken up.”

She continued: “But in saying that, the reason why I carry it and I don’t bother trying to change everyone’s minds on it is because I’d be lying if I said I didn’t have an emotional connection to him before I had fully broken it off. … Things had ended with my ex. So I do carry so much of that guilt because it’s not something I’ve ever done before. I carry a lot of that guilt.”

Cameron broke down the timeline between her and Gallagher leaving season 9 in a good place to them calling it quits off screen, saying, “It’s not like it wasn’t official but we traveled together for six weeks after. I think we went like two weeks without a call and essentially he ghosted me for like five days and then he said like he’d spoken to his ex and they wanted to make it work.”

The pair got back together when Cameron made an appearance in season 10.

“Ultimately I guess they got their fairytale ending from that,” she added. “I guess, I fell in love.”

Cameron accused Gallagher of making her feel “love bombed.” After she found out she was pregnant, Cameron claimed Gallagher made her feel guilty for questioning their future plans.

“But if I ever said‘I don’t know if I can do this. Like, I don’t think it’s the right time.’ He would make me feel very bad about myself. He would tell me, ‘Abortion is wrong and bad.’ He would make me feel very guilty and just terrible about myself. Like I was a bad human being for thinking that way. … I have quite a conservative mum. I couldn’t talk to anyone. So he was kind of my only sounding board because I was so afraid to tell anyone.”

“It was a very rough pregnancy. Like, we were very up and down. We were fighting a lot over very simple things that I did that would seem to trigger him. I think I spent 90 percent of my pregnancy in tears and I think it was very hard for my parents to see,” she recalled. “At first it was very emotional isolation. I would be told that what I said was wrong. And even if I apologized, it was like, ‘You’ve already made me feel this way. So I now will retract my love.’”

Cameron recalled confiding in her mother, adding, “What I learned and what I was told multiple times [by Nathan] is you’re not allowed to speak about your relationship to other people. … We had another really big fight and things had escalated and he’d got on the drink. I was running around Sydney very pregnant, having just finished a full day at work. … I called my best friend and I said, ‘Hey, can you just stay on the phone with me? Nathan’s upset with me at the moment. Can you please just stay on the phone to me?’ And he jumped out of the car. The moving car. So he opened the door, I slammed the brakes and he jumped out.”

She continued: ”The way that I was treated, I would be told to shut the f*** up, I’d be called a bitch, a s***, and all these horrible things. There were multiple times when I was like ‘No no no, this cannot continue because my son cannot grow up thinking that this is how you speak to women.'”

After giving birth to son Kayden, Cameron was asked to move to Croatia while Gallagher filmed Below Deck Med.

“Obviously, I didn’t think it was a good idea to go [to Croatia]. In a perfect world and with a supportive partner, I would 100 percent say, ‘Yep, we can do this, no problem.’ But obviously the situation wasn’t that,” she noted. “And DCJ, which is essentially Child Protective Services, had gotten involved.”

Cameron recalled trying to get help. “The social worker deemed the situation to be unsafe,” she recalled. “I had even gotten onto the phone to one of the producers, and I couldn’t tell him everything. But I was just saying, ‘Look, I’m in a really bad situation and I don’t think it’s a good idea if I go [to Croatia].'”

She continued: “It felt as though he was very worried about who I spoke to or who I was around when he wasn’t around. So it did feel like there was this element of control that he would lose over me if I wasn’t in the same country as him.”

While watching season 11 back, Cameron wasn’t thrilled to serve as the “scapegoat” for Gallagher, sharing, “It was kind of like he was not treating everyone on the boat quite so nicely and the excuse was he was getting a hard time at home, when we were just all getting a hard time.”

Cameron ultimately had to find a way to get her friend to Croatia after Gallagher allegedly isolated her.

“They did offer me to have someone there. They said we will pay for a flight for someone to come and help you [production]. And in discussions with Nathan about me coming there, I was told that I couldn’t have any one of my family or my friends come because he has to feel comfortable also. My options were his sister or his mom,” she noted. “I had to essentially devise this thing with my best friend. … She can’t take too much time off work so I said, ‘OK, how about I get there and then I say that I can’t do it on my own and then maybe ask him in front of people that maybe I need a little bit of help. I know this sounds really bad but it was the only way that I could get the help that I needed.”

Cameron tried to alert a producer to her issues, to which Gallagher responded by “crying.”

“He said, ‘I’m so sad that I made her feel this way.’ And I just sat there in absolute shock and awe,” she recalled. “This was the first time he had ever cried or ever showed any remorse to my sadness or to my hurt. He’s never ever shown. It was always anger towards my sadness.”

Following a tense day, Cameron claimed Gallagher was “angry” she spent time with her family.

“He started calling me certain names. I put my foot down and said I don’t want you sleeping in this room tonight. He came back in, pushed past and he was recording, and this wasn’t the first time he’s done this to me,” she said. “So it wasn’t a surprise where he was shoving himself into the room.”

Cameron alleged that Gallagher would fake being on the receiving end of her abuse on footage he captured, adding, “When he was behind me, holding me, I had a moment where I was like, ‘Why am I allowing this?’ Like, I couldn’t breathe, I couldn’t [do] anything, and all I could do was throw an elbow behind me as fast, as hard as I could just to get out of it. And obviously in this scenario that made him see red and that just escalated things so much more.”

She continued: “When I was in the bathroom and he had his hands around my neck and attempted to lift, my son was in my arms. At that moment, all I could think of was, if I fall, so does he. So in that moment I step up and do anything I could and thank God there’s a toilet behind me. That’s probably the biggest part that I’m like from that moment, I should have known there’s no return.”

Cameron said she was worried she wouldn’t survive the harrowing moment.

“There was a moment when he had me pinned down and he was striking me on the jaw… I actually sat there and I asked if he was going to kill me. There was a moment where I actually asked that question. The reason I say this is because if things had not gotten that bad, I would never have gotten out. That’s the scary thing. As bad as that night was, it wasn’t the worst,” she added. “Me being me, I would have scraped, crawled, gotten myself out of there so much earlier. But the reason I couldn’t was because if I had pushed past and my son would be collateral from that, I would never forgive myself. So I was stuck. When I was able to get out, I ran barefoot down the fire stairs. He chased me all the way down until we got to the first floor. And after that, there’s cameras and he stopped there. I ran straight to my brother’s house who lives just a block away.”

Amid Gallagher’s legal issues, Cameron recalled “paying for hotels” for her then-ex-boyfriend.

“He didn’t have any money,” she claimed. “I was paying him money from what I had to pay for my mortgage and my bills and things like that. But he would still come back to my house anyway. I tried to get out. I tried so hard. The amount of times I said, ‘This is over.’ And the threats that I was met with, I was told that he would destroy me publicly.”

She added: “He chose not being able to come back to the same country that his son lives in over facing the court system. And the thing is, if he had faced this court system, and this is what I’m very shameful to admit, I would have had his back. I did try to change my statement to the police. The police wouldn’t speak to me.”

Cameron “tried everything to support” Gallagher, saying, “Shamefully so, I would have stuck up for him in court. I would have given the police nothing from me as a witness. How sad is that? It’s so sad. And the thing that got me out was him leaving, and it was the biggest weight off my shoulders. All of a sudden, I could have my family over to help me look after my son when I went to work. I could breathe again.”

For Cameron, life has now “felt so bright” without contact with Gallagher.

“I haven’t been in contact with him since he left the country,” she concluded. “I know that he is not afraid to do anything to throw me under. He’s not afraid to lie. He’s always had this idea that he has ownership or control over me. And you know what? I still feel that. And I am still scared of him. And that’s why I’ve not said anything, even though he’s thrown all these accusations out there.”

#3579. Delete GTA 6 For A Chance To Win Another Game

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases this week. The game looms so large that other companies are using it to market their own games, including Devolver Digital.

The publisher has announced that people can enter for a chance to win their upcoming game, Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, by reposting the message below with a video of themselves deleting their GTA 6 pre-load. Of course, anyone who deletes their pre-load can install it again, though it might take some time given the game is 212GB.

Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, priced at $5 (or $3.74 until launch), releases on November 19, which is the same day that GTA 6 comes out. "There is no doubt GTA 6 will have the spotlight before, during, and after November 19, but it’s not for everyone, or releasing on Steam the same day, so we figure there’s a bit of counter-programming that may work in Volvy’s favor," Devolver told Kotaku.

GTA 6 has reportedly already sold nearly 15 million copies and generated about $1.5 billion in revenue.

#3577. How To Play GTA 6 Early On Xbox Using This Trick

Due to GTA 6's non-simultaneous release, people in New Zealand will be the first in the world to play the highly anticipated open-world crime game when it releases at midnight local time there.

If you want to become a Kiwi for a day and you plan to play on Xbox, you can trick your console into thinking it's in New Zealand to play early.

The following trick has worked before, but there is no guarantee that it will work for you this time with GTA 6, or you might not want to do it at all. After all, Microsoft's own policy says people should only change their region if they have moved to a different country or are already in a new region.

If that all sounds OK to you, here's how to change your Xbox region to New Zealand (via Insider Gaming).

  • Go to Settings
  • Click System, then Language & Localization
  • Switch your location to New Zealand
  • Restart your console

The process of changing regions on PlayStation 5 is not as straightforward and involves numerous other steps--Insider Gaming has a rundown. However, it's also been reported that players changing their PS5 region have begun receiving account suspensions without warning.

GTA 6 launches on November 19, but midnight in New Zealand on November 19 is 3 AM PT / 6 AM ET on November 18. So people in the US will have to wait a very long time to play GTA 6 compared to the people who live in New Zealand.

For more on GTA 6, including preload information, preorder bonuses, and release times, check out our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

#3576. Penélope Cruz Says She and Husband Javier Bardem are “Very Careful” About Choosing When to Work Together

Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem are very selective about when they work on a project together, but the opportunity to costar in director Florian Zeller's timely psychological thriller Bunker was too enticing to pass up.

"When [Zeller] came to us with this powerful, very necessary story to tell, we looked at each other and there was no way to say no to this," Cruz said during a post-screening discussion at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room on Sunday. "I'm very, very happy that we did it."

Bunker revolves around a married couple, Miguel (Bardem) and Sofia (Cruz), whose 17-year marriage is tested when Miguel, a famous architect, is presented with a life changing work opportunity.

“I really wanted to work with them because I truly believe they are [two] of the greatest actors working today,” Zeller said during the panel discussion moderated by VF's West Coast Editor John Ross. “I was also very excited and interested to have them together onscreen because they are also a real couple. I thought it would be an interesting and unique opportunity to approach something that has to do with authenticity, with the truth. Not to say that this is their story, because of course this is not their story.”

Florian Zeller at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026

Cruz said she felt a kinship with her character's concerns. “We have so many things in common in terms of this sadness and frustration and anger that you feel in terms of where is the world going if we don't wake up soon,” she said. “I hope it's not too late, but especially the experiment that is being done on younger people, children, teenagers, it just makes me very furious.

“It's something that affects me so much as an actress, as a mother, as a citizen of the world, that I felt completely a need to play Sophia,” she continued. “And of course it was not the only reason, but it was a big privilege to be able to say those lines. And [Zeller] is such a master of writing and I am a fan of all his work. And same for Javier, who is not here with us today, he's doing theater, but we are very careful in terms of choosing when to work together.”

Pénelope Cruz, Florian Zeller and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026

Cruz praised Zeller’s ability to provide a supportive, safe working environment and his strong point of view. “We felt really, really safe with him, he's so talented. He doesn't need any kind of manipulation and he never treats the audience as not intelligent because the audience can feel everything,” she explained. “And that has become really the most important thing for me. Don't over-explain, don't underestimate the audience ever because the thermometer is really working. And also with young people more and more and more. That is my hope to continue to go to see films on a big screen. They're coming back thank God. So let's create more possibilities so they can keep doing that.”

Cruz also said that she and Bardem have similar approaches to their work and the preparation it requires. “It's true that we share the same passion and we have done this since we were teenagers,” she said. “We love exploring and studying and feeling that healthy fear of the unknown because every time you begin a project, in a way, it's really starting from zero. So it's a really good thing to share.”

Zeller called his collaboration with the couple “a fascinating journey. It takes a lot of courage or fearlessness to do that, I think, for actors.” He also revealed that he initially referenced Stanley Kubrick's seminal thriller Eyes Wide Shut as a point of reference for Bunker, but realized it might not be setting the proper tone, given the circumstances.

“I remember that the first time I spoke with [Cruz] and Javier about this project, I mentioned a film that was somewhere in my mind, Eyes Wide Shut. Not to say that there is any kind of connection between the two films, but as you remember, Eyes Wide Shut at the time, Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman, they were together," he said. "And I remember as a viewer that it was so interesting to be in a position where you do not know exactly what you're invited to watch… but Javier [later] told me, ‘You should not mention this film too often because remember at the end of the shooting they broke up.’ And then I realized that the director, Kubrick, died soon after. So I was like, ‘Okay, I'm going to stop mentioning this film.’ But the real difference I would say is that we knew that the destination of that film was the last image of the painting that you saw, which means that it was about how to reconnect with the other.”

Pénelope Cruz, Florian Zeller and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

I Have A Theory About Dexter: Resurrection And His Downfall. Why I Think Season 2 Could Address It

#3574. GTA 6 Has Teamed Up With The Weather Channel To Show How Dynamic Leonida Can Be

Rockstar Games has found an unexpected partner to show off one of GTA 6's most impressive features: The Weather Channel. The US broadcaster has shared an exclusive look at Leonida's weather system via six new screenshots and forecasts that make the fictional destination sound like somewhere you'd need to check the weather before visiting.

It's an unusual collaboration, but a very fitting one. GTA 6 takes place in Leonida, a fictional state inspired by Florida, where sunshine, torrential rain, thunderstorms and tropical storms are all part of the ecosystem. Who better to show off the unpredictable climate than The Weather Channel?

The broadcaster posted the collaboration on X, writing "Nobody knows weather like we do. That's why Rockstar gave us an exclusive look at the forecast for Leonida and the dynamic weather in GTAVI."

Instead of just posting the six new screenshots, The Weather Channel provided six different weather reports for the various locations across Leonida. Each has its own conditions and some local facts, making the entire post sound like a genuine forecast.

The reports include heavy rain reducing visibility across the Keys, a thunderstorm rolling over the swamps of Pelican Valley--and obscuring some feisty "nippers" at the same time--and sea fog threatening to obscure the expensive beachfront views at South Ocean Beach. There's also a tropical storm making the waters around the Rusty Anchor particularly choppy, and Gambit Bay has a low-lying morning mist ahead of hunting season.

One forecast warns commuters traveling from Key Lento to expect more rain and wind. It seems like an almost mundane detail for a game about a pair of criminals, but it's this exact impressive world-building that makes Leonida feel real.

The six new screenshots are especially impressive, showing off the towering storm clouds and lightning strikes through to dense fog that makes entire stretches of the coastline disappear. Rockstar isn't treating weather as just a visual effect--it will have a real impact on the way you play the game.

Owen Shepherd, Rockstar's VP of Art: Light and Rendering, explained that the studio had to completely reimagine its in-game weather systems to make them feel "more localized, persistent, and above all dynamic." He added that Leonida's weather can range from clear blue skies to towering cumulonimbus clouds, reflecting the unpredictable conditions of the real-world Florida climate.

The emphasis on localized weather is interesting. Instead of having the entire map experience the same conditions, Leonida's different environments can have their own atmospheric conditions. A coastal resort might be swallowed by fog, while a storm rolls over the wetlands in the distance. This approach will make exploring the enormous map feel different depending on when and where players visit. The screenshots don't confirm how individual gameplay mechanics will be affected, but they offer a deeper look at the environmental detail Rockstar is aiming for.

There's something pretty extraordinary about a real-world weather broadcaster getting involved in the marketing of Grand Theft Auto--and it really puts into perspective how the arrival of GTA 6 is a once-in-a-generation event.

GTA 6 launches on November 19, but players in New Zealand will be able to get their hands on the game ahead of the rest of the world, thanks to hitting midnight before anywhere else. For unrelated reasons, if you want to set your Xbox region to New Zealand, we've got you covered.

#3572. Xbox Game Pass Is Losing 8 More Games In November

Don't get too comfortable with your Xbox Game Pass library, because you never know which game will be removed from it next. This month, several more games are on their way out on November 30, so say goodbye to deadly xenomorphs, even deadlier house spiders, and a Cold War battleground infested with killer robots.

One of the biggest departures this month is Aliens: Dark Descent. It's a solid entry in the Aliens franchise if you don't mind some base-management chores, as it nails the atmosphere of the classic sequel while giving you plenty of acid-blooded bugs to mow down.

This month will also see the 17th Century Ghostbusters game, Banishers: Ghost of New Eden, leave Game Pass, along with a few kid-friendly titles. As a reminder, you can save 20% on these games if you decide to buy them before they leave Game Pass.

#3571. Sony Is Updating The PS5 Again, And It Might Have GTA 6 Pirates In Mind

A new PS5 firmware update has dropped, but even at a chunky 1.2GB download, version 26.07-14.23.00 doesn't include a comprehensive list of notes.

"We've made some security fixes to the system software," the very short update notes read. Notably, this is the fourth PS5 firmware update since October 1, and typically there's a buffer period of several months between downloads. While Sony hasn't confirmed it, the current thinking is that the company is shoring up its defenses for the release of GTA 6 to prevent the game from being pirated.

The new firmware will be mandatory for new game releases as well, including GTA 6, which means that PS5 hackers and homebrew hobbyists have their work cut out for them. The hacking scene recently made big advances on the console, jailbreaking systems that have update 14 and below installed, and thus allowing more pirated games to be played. Sony is under pressure to prevent GTA 6 from being pirated, and with the PS5 console holding the lion's share of GTA 6 preorders, there's plenty of financial incentive to keep the game secure on that platform.

Security researchers and hackers have been leveraging generative AI and automated decompilation analysis to discover lower-level system vulnerabilities and dump game binaries much faster, creating an arms race between Sony and hackers.  Every time a potential vulnerability or homebrew exploit surfaces--like the recent vulnerabilities that targeted PS5 consoles running 13.60 and 14.22 firmware--Sony rushes out a mandatory console patch to plug the hole.

Beyond security measures, we've also seen base PS5 consoles updated with Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR), which is also rolling out to more games. An AI-based upscaling technology derived from the PS5 Pro's PSSR, it initially supported only Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei.

#3570. Casting Walter White: How ‘Breaking Bad’ Found Bryan Cranston

While the Breaking Bad universe would eventually expand to include dozens of characters, the pilot was actually a tidy affair. At its center was Walter White, whose journey would require an actor of extraordinary depth and nuance. It’s not an exaggeration to say that the success or failure of Breaking Bad would rest primarily on his sagging shoulders.

SHARON BIALY, casting director: I don’t know if Bryan knows this, but when Sherry [Bialy] and I went in to meet with Vince to try to get the job as casting directors—­our “audition”—­we literally said, “You may think we’re crazy. We hope you don’t fire us before you hire us. But what about Bryan Cranston?” And he said, “By golly, that’s who I want. I worked with him on The X-­ Files.”

Sherry and I did a lot of theater at the time. We were doing Aaron Sorkin’s new play [The Farnsworth Invention], and Bryan came in and read. We were blown away. He was so talented on Malcolm in the Middle, obviously, but this was live theater with a lot of language. Anyway, Bryan didn’t get the role, but his audition was incredible. And I never forgot it.

VINCE GILLIGAN, creator: Bryan was the only guy I was thinking of when I wrote the script. I had written an episode of The X-­ Files called “Drive,” which came out in 1998, and I was lucky enough to hire him to play the bad guy.

We were really struggling to cast this role because we needed a guy who could be really scary, someone who could make us feel like our hero, Agent Mulder, could get his head blown off at any second. But also, he had to be kind of an asshole. [Throughout the episode] he’s ranting about the government. He’s ranting about stuff like, “Agent Mulder— is that a Jewish name?”

He’s a thoroughly unlikable guy. And yet you had to feel bad for him, for what happens to him at the end of the episode. You had to feel sympathy.

We only had a day or two left before production was going to start. We were going to have to settle on somebody. We had plenty of actors come in who were scary as all get out, but they weren’t necessarily likable. And then this guy walks in the door: Bryan Cranston. Never heard of him before. And he nails it in the audition. As he left, we all stood up and shook his hand, and then I looked to the other producers and to Rick Millikan, our casting director, and I said, “Off to wardrobe!” He was that good.

When I came up with the idea of Breaking Bad, I thought, This is a guy who, again, is going to be very unlikable. He’s going to do a lot of unlikable things, and the audience still has to sympathize with him. Who would be good for this role? I know! That guy, Bryan Cranston. And I wrote it for him. I never really had anyone else in mind.

MELISSA BERNSTEIN, co-executive producer: He was in an episode of X-­Files, playing this racist, and somehow, over the course of the episode, you go from loathing him to feeling badly that he doesn’t make it. He just was able to make someone so unsavory be human. Vince also said, “And he’s so great with comedy. I just feel it in my bones that he could bring those chops to drama—­his sense of timing, the way he embodies those choices physically. He’s perfect.”

BRYAN CRANSTON: I instruct young actors all the time that without a healthy dose of luck, you will not have a career. And this [episode of The X-­ Files] was a lucky break for me.

I had just gotten back from shooting this little movie that I wrote and directed, called Last Chance. I spent all of our money on it, and by the end I was like, Wow, what are we doing on this film? But we rolled the dice on it, and now I was back in town and got a call from my agent about an audition. I said, “Whatever it is, let me know, because I really could use the money.” It just so happened that my look at the time, from this movie that I did, was a perfect look for this guy [on The X-­Files]. So, I went in, and I got the job—­and I was grateful for it.

It’s only in retrospect that I realized Vince Gilligan wanted to see me [to discuss Breaking Bad] was because I had played this reprehensible character that, despite his actions, still needed the audience to root for his life. Despite the despicable person in the back seat, David Du­chovny’s humanity would not allow him to just pull over and say, “Fuck it, die. You’re a horrible human being. I just want you to die.” He couldn’t do it. That’s really, in a nutshell, what Vince Gilligan does.

I knew intuitively that coming off seven years of a comedy, I needed to look for a drama. If I didn’t, I could have been typecast. If you want to expand on the opportunities that may present themselves, you need to take control. I was offered a couple of comedy pilots that I turned down, and I was perfectly willing to wait. Then Breaking Bad came into my lap.

I read it . . . and I couldn’t believe it. I was stunned. I thought, This is perhaps the best hour­-long screenplay that I’ve ever read. I felt tremendous empathy for this character. This poor guy who is just struggling. And I was the same age as Walter White—­I was fifty.

But reading the pilot, I didn’t know where it was going. You have this fish­ out­ of­ water teacher, cooking crystal meth? How could that possibly be sustained year after year after year? How can someone who knows nothing about that world survive? And Vince explained that he wanted to turn Mr. Chips into Scarface.

In the same way that The Sopranos is unthinkable with someone other than James Gandolfini in the role of Tony Soprano, I can’t get my head around the idea of a version of Breaking Bad that doesn’t include Bryan Cranston. But this is Hollywood, and even on basic cable, you don’t just sign up a former sitcom star—­ not even one as gifted as Bryan—­and hand him the starring role in a complex drama without a bit of, shall we say . . . discussion.

MARK JOHNSON, executive producer: Obviously, some people came up for Walter White who were names, but we never got around to entertaining them seriously. It was Vince’s idea to cast him. And despite the fact that there wasn’t a unanimous wave of approval, there wasn’t the kind of pushback that you’d probably have today, in large part because I don’t think the expectation was that we were going to get any real name, any big name.

MELISSA BERNSTEIN: AMC had found Jon Hamm for Mad Men, and they sort of got to reintroduce him to the business. I think they thought we would do something similar with Bryan.

CHARLIE COLLIER, president, general manager, AMC: I was never in the room when they were debating the cast with Vince and Mark. That would have been the programming group. And then they would come back to us and say, “They want that father from Malcolm in the Middle.” And we’d be like, “Really? He’s going to be the linchpin for this whole ambitious project?”

CHRISTINA WAYNE, senior VP, scripted programming, AMC: When Vince suggested Bryan, we all kind of said, “That guy from Malcolm in the Middle?” And then he started showing us a bunch of tape of Bryan in other things, and I was, like, Oh my God—­he’s a total chameleon.

JAMIE ERLICHT, co­-president, Sony Pictures Television: It’s funny. This is one of those great Hollywood stories that has been told so many times. You sit on the sidelines and watch, and it takes on a life of its own. That life is a little different than the truth, sure, but it’s a better story.

The story is that Zack [Van Amburg] and I heard “Bryan Cranston,” and we were really unsure, and we tried to convince Vince that, No, that’s not the way to go. That’s part of a story about how despite all the forces against him, Bryan Cranston became Walter White.

It’s a great story. I love that story. I mean, I don’t love that story.

The truth is, the show was going forward. We weren’t worried about the writing because Vince was knocking it out of the park. The directing? We weren’t worried about the directing. The casting was going to be the next critical element. If you don’t have it—­ well, it’s funny to think about it now. With ninety­ nine point nine percent of other actors in that role, that show is just a well­ written good show that doesn’t become the legacy show that it’s become. And so Vince brought up Bryan Cranston.

I had worked with Bryan on King of Queens. He was the wacky neighbor, a guest star. I was a mid­ level executive, and I was in charge of that show. I always thought he brought a lot of comedic value, just like he did on Seinfeld, and obviously Malcolm in the Middle.

So, when the name Bryan Cranston came up, I was like, Hmmm, that’s interesting. I’ve never seen him do the more dramatic stuff. Do you think he can do it?

Vince was very passionate. He said he had worked with him on X-­Files, and that’s where he really saw what he was capable of on the drama side. We said, “Great, would you send us the X-­Files episode?” Which he did. I remember it was the next day. Zack and I were watching it. We looked at each other and said, “It’s a little bit of a leap of faith, but Vince is passionate, and Bryan is truly talented. Sure, we’re in.” The process took all of thirty­ six hours.

That version of the story, the true version of the story, is not as sexy as the one where Bryan jumped through thirty­ nine hoops and almost didn’t get cast. But that’s how it happened.

ZACK VAN AMBURG, co­-president, Sony Pictures Television: Remember, at this point, Michael Chiklis had gone from doing comedy to being a badass antihero (in The Shield). So, on one hand, you worry: Wait, are we just pulling a page out of the same playbook? Let’s take another sitcom guy and have him do a dark drama.

I think Vince was really clear on why he wanted Bryan. There was a likability factor that was undeniable. There was also a sort of sympathy that Bryan was able to elicit. And Vince also said, “No, wait a second—­ this guy’s also a dramatic actor.”

While some of this stuff gets lost in the haze of time—­ and the internet has a way of transforming rumors into something disguised as fact—­ it’s fair to say that Bryan was always the first choice for the role of Walter White. Regardless of what you may have heard, no one else was offered the job. Not Matthew Broderick, not John Cusack. No one. But you can’t fault anyone for doing their due diligence.

SHARON BIALY: The network likes names. They want to talk about other names. We did that. We did a couple of auditions and meetings. We just met recently with an actor on something else, and he reminded me that he was in the waiting room when Bryan walked out, and he turned to the other three actors and said, “We should all just go home. It’s over. That guy’s going to get it.”

VINCE GILLIGAN: We saw a lot of really good actors, several of them now famous names. They never dissuaded me that Bryan was the guy. And luckily, Bryan said yes, because he was up at the same time for a pilot for Fox that was going to pay him . . . well, my understanding is, substantially more money. Like a doctor show. Thank goodness he went with us instead.

Spoilers for the latest episode of Boston Blue, “Bloodlines” lie ahead.

Boston Blue Season 2 has been chugging right along amid the 2026 TV schedule, and viewers have been treated to some serious action and tense family drama. Mae Silver’s re-election (for Boston District Attorney) campaign, Sarah Silver’s impending marriage to Seth Yates and the reunion of Reagan brothers Danny and Jamie are among the highlights thus far. The season has also been eventful for Lena Silver and, based on the latest episode, I think she may end up in a messy storyline, which I’d prefer not to see.

Sonequa Martin-Green’s Lena Silver has a busy career, and she also has an eventful personal life, which has been tackled again this season. One of the biggest plot points revolves around her relationship with Detective Brian Rodgers (Ryan Broussard). At the tail end of Season 1’s finale, Rogers was in a car accident (which fans learned in Season 2 was part of an orchestrated hit). While Lena and Brian rehabbed together following the former’s own gun injury, Rogers became restless due to not being cleared to work again.

At the end of the episode, it was revealed that the flowers came not from Rogers but from Lena’s other ex-boyfriend, Dr. Troy Underwood, who was introduced in Season 1. It was established that prior to the events of the show, Troy and Lena dated, with the latter putting her life on hold to support him during medical school. That made it quite painful for Lena when Troy cheated on her during his training. Lena seemed to be done with the doctor but, amid this newest episode, she accepted a dinner invitation from him in order to hear him out.

So, with all of these plot threads in mind, my theory is that Lena and Troy will get closer and that Rogers will return to Boston after being assigned to a local DEA office. With that, Ms. Silver will find herself in the middle of a tense love triangle (and have to choose who she’ll want to bring to those Shabbat dinners). That’s the sense I’m getting, at least, but I’m hoping that’s not the case.

What It’ll Actually Take For Tom Selleck To Appear On The Blue Bloods Spinoff (Per Donnie Wahlberg)

First off, love triangles – whether they’re featured in procedurals or not – have become incredibly ubiquitous and feel somewhat clichéd at this point. Given that, I would hope that Boston Blue’s writers can think of something more interesting to do when it comes to handling Lena’s love life. There are also more specific reasons why this specific triangle would be relatively odd.

It would be weird for Lena to legitimately re-enter a relationship with Troy due to how he hurt her. Yes, Lena is a rational person who can extend grace but, given her characterization, it just feels weird for her to even think about getting back with someone who wronged her in such a deep way. Plus, if faced with a decision between Troy and Brian, I just can’t see her not choosing the latter, as her issue with Rogers amounts to a lovers quarrel. So, if Rogers comes back and is ready to accept help, why choose Troy?

Whatever the case, I’m getting the feeling that Lena’s romance journey will greatly differ from that of Danny and his partner, Maria Baez. Here’s hoping Silver gets a nuanced relationship story as Boston Blue’s second season continues. The show returns with a new episode on Friday, December 11 at 10 p.m. ET, and fans can stream it the next day with a Paramount+ subscription.

#3568. GTA 6 Nearing 16 Million Copies Sold And Passes $1.5 Billion In Revenue

The video game research company Sensor Tower has updated its GTA 6 sales tracker to reveal the latest, albeit unofficial, sales data for the open-world crime game. According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has now sold 15.88 million total units via pre-purchases, which works out to about $1.54 billion in gross revenue.

The report said PS5 sales are dominating the mix, with GTA 6 selling 11.83 million units on PS5 so far, compared to 4.04 million on Xbox Series X|S. That means of the 15.88 million GTA 6 sales so far, 75% are on PS5 and 25% on Xbox Series X|S.

In total, GTA 6 sales for PS5 have so far reached $1.15 billion in revenue, compared to $390 million for Xbox Series X|S. Sony and Microsoft keep about 30% of revenue due to their platform fees, so GTA 6 being a huge success directly benefits both of those companies.

The huge gap in sales between platforms is not surprising because the PS5 is dominating Xbox Series X|S in terms of console sales. In fact, GTA 6 is breaking records on Xbox, Microsoft has said, and the sales numbers for GTA 6 on Xbox line up with Xbox's share of the console market.

Sensor Tower is projecting as many as 25 million total pre-purchases for GTA 6 by launch, and if the 75/25 split holds, that would be about 18.5 million units on PS5 and 6.5 million on Xbox Series X|S.

GTA 6 is the most preordered game of all time for PlayStation and Xbox. If the 10 million pre-purchase number is real, that would break a record for most preorders set by Cyberpunk 2077 (8 million).

Sony holds the marketing rights for GTA 6 on PS5, but that doesn't mean that Microsoft is doing nothing to try to promote the game. Just recently, Microsoft announced a GTA 6-inspired custom Xbox console that sits inside an alligator.

Circana has released new data that shows that GTA 6 holds 29% purchase intent among US console and PC gamers. That means nearly 1 in 3 console and PC gamers in the US plan to buy GTA 6–this is the highest purchase intent that Circana has ever measured for any game.

GTA 6 may indeed be a gigantic hit commercially, and one that helps lift the entire industry with increased sales of hardware and accessories. But anyone looking to buy a new console to play GTA 6 is set for major sticker shock, as consoles today are more expensive than ever. Not only that, but GTA 6 is not going to save the industry’s many serious and deep-rooted issues, experts believe.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game's file size is about 212GB, and thankfully, preloading is already underway. The game unlocks on November 19 at midnight local time, and that means US players will be among the last in the world to get in.

People in New Zealand, meanwhile, will be the first in the world to play GTA 6. If you're thinking about booking a flight to the land of Hobbits, here are some tips for packing your PS5 safely.

#3567. Ocarina Of Time Is 2026’s Best-Selling Physical Game In The US, But GTA 6 Is Coming

Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 is the best-selling physical game of 2026, according to Circana, but GTA 6 is coming out soon and could topple that record.

Circana's Mat Piscatella said the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 was the first game to surpass 1 million physical units sold in the US for its launch week since 2023's The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.

Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 released on November 5, and Circana's reporting period ended on November 7, so the achievement was actually accomplished in just two days, not even a full week.

Ocarina of Time's physical edition, which includes a cartridge, sells for $70, compared to $60 for its digital counterpart.

GTA 6 launches on November 19, and while the game is fully digital, Rockstar is releasing a "physical" version of the game at brick-and-mortar retailers. Buyers don't get a disc--only a code for the game.

In any event, for Circana, code-in-a-box games are considered new physical game sales, so GTA 6 is no doubt going to topple Ocarina of Time's record.

Ocarina of Time's remake for Switch 2 sold more than 5 million copies over its first four days globally. The latest sales data for GTA 6 pre-purchases show that the game has passed 16 million units sold worldwide.

#3565. New Ubisoft Boss Wants Studio To Become “A24 Of Video Games”

Ubisoft recently hired games industry veteran Christoph Hartmann to become the general manager of Creative House 2. In a new interview, Hartmann talked about his hopes for the unit, saying his dream would be for it to become "like the A24 of video games."

He told Variety that what he means by this is that Creative House 2 can be like A24 in that it can make games that are both critically and commercially successful. A24's biggest hit ever was this year's Backrooms, which made more than $400 million worldwide against a reported budget of $10 million and was received positively by fans and critics.

Some of A24's other recent big critical and commercial hits have included Marty Supreme ($192 million), Everything Everywhere All at Once ($148 million), The Drama ($135 million), and Civil War ($127 million).

Saying Ubisoft's Creative House 2 could aim for what A24 is doing is certainly an ambitious goal, and it's not the first time that Hartmann has made such a bold claim about what he's working on. When he was at Amazon, Hartmann said his objective was to help Amazon become “the Disney of the future,” with gaming standing alongside TV, film, music, and retail.

Creative House 2 covers franchises like The Division, Ghost Recon, Splinter Cell, and March of Giants (which Ubisoft bought from Hartmann's previous company, Amazon). "Hartmann’s role is to oversee strategic direction and development of the studios and brands under Creative House 2," Ubisoft said.

Hartmann told Variety that he wants Creative House 2 to "definitely not" be a place that only makes shooter games.

"I want us to be a label which really looks after the core gamer. And what I mean by that, it’s almost easier to describe what we’re not going to do. So I’m not going to do a racing game. I’m not going to do sports. I’m not going to do a casual kids title. But could we do an RPG one day? Could we do MMO? Could I maybe do even a strategy game? Sure, it’s all coming down to the right talent," he said.

Hartmann also discussed why he left Amazon, saying the company is focused on the AI buildout right now and "games just can't be their prime focus right now." Prior to Amazon, Hartmann worked at 2K for decades.

#3564. Camille Grammer Alleges Ex Kelsey Grammer Fired Daughter Via Text Message

Camille Grammer is once again putting her ex-husband, Kelsey Grammer, on blast.

During a Monday, November 16, appearance on the inaugural episode of the “Everybody Sees the Villain. Nobody Sees Who Needed Her to Be One” podcast, Camille, 58, alleged that the Frasier star once fired their daughter, Mason, 25, from a job via text message.

The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills alum said that Mason, a film major from Emerson College, recently filmed a television project (believed to be a pilot for a Los Angeles-based spinoff of Bravo’s Next Gen NYC), but that her last name didn’t make breaking into Hollywood any easier.

“She needs something to open the door,” Camille said, alleging that Kelsey, 71, “doesn’t do anything for either one of us.”

“He fired her through text… it was ridiculous,” she claimed. “She went from working for a year to over text, ‘Oh, I’m shutting down the office. Your employment’s up.’ That’s it.”

Camille said that Kelsey’s alleged text message firing was “like how he dumped me” and that he “said our marriage was over through text … what a coward.”

As for Mason, the Bravolebrity said that prior to filming her own project, “She worked with her dad. She did work in production for a while, she did script coverage and other things, but she’s like, ‘Where is the work?’”

Camille added, “She has to fight against the nepo baby [stigma]. Listen — nepo babies, big, yes,” but conceded that while “you can get in the door as a nepo,” it isn’t as easy as it seems.

Us has reached out to Kelsey’s representative for comment.

Last month, Camille hit out at her ex, claiming that he never reached out to Mason on her 25th birthday.

“A daughter should never have to wonder whether her father remembers her birthday. Three days later, and still not a call or a text. 💔,” she wrote via Instagram at the time. “You can be a beloved actor to the world, but being a father is a role that requires showing up when the cameras are off. Fame, accolades, and public admiration mean very little if you neglect the people who should matter most. Some wounds come not from what is said, but from the silence.”

“A mother never stops hurting when her child is hurt. 25 is a milestone birthday. Sometimes the silence is deafening, and the disappointment speaks volumes,” Camille wrote.

She further claimed, “Mason told me she kept checking her phone all weekend, hoping her father had called, even from an unfamiliar number or that his message had somehow ended up in her spam folder. She even checked there, searching for any sign that he had reached out.”

Kelsey did not publicly respond to Camille’s allegations at the time.

Camille and Kelsey were married from 1997 to 2011 and share daughter Mason and son Jude, 22. Kelsey has six other children, including the actresses Spencer, 43, whom he shares with first wife Doreen Alderman, and Greer, 34, whom he shares with ex-girlfriend Barrie Buckner. He and his current wife, Kayte Walsh, have four more children together.
